constats.titre: Relecture Registry-verified désynchronisée par un nœud address(0)
constats.resume: `_verifyRows` fait `continue` quand le client vaut 0 sans sauter les nE arêtes de la ligne. Un nœud adresse `0x02‖address(0)`, accepté par `_appendNodes` et ajoutable par n'importe qui sur un set ouvert, donne un client nul avec une ligne non vide : toutes les lignes suivantes sont relues au mauvais décalage, alors que `_rowLoop` (arithmétique, feuilles Merkle) lit les vraies.
constats.scenario: Set ouvert Registry-verified : un certificat qui contient une ligne pour address(0) puis une ligne d'agent portant une arête absente du registre est accepté ; sans la ligne address(0), la même soumission échoue en `EdgeMismatch(1,0)`. `isTrusted` renvoie alors vrai pour un agent qui n'a reçu aucun avis (trustLow 0,148 WAD, MESURÉ, PoC forge `PocD`/`Exploit`).
constats.correctif: Avancer `off` de nE·(W+6) (ou exiger nE = 0) avant le `continue`, refuser address(0) dans `_appendNodes`, exiger `off == rows.length` en fin de `_verifyRows` ; idéalement un seul décodage des lignes partagé avec `_rowLoop`.

details_en.summary: _verifyRows does `continue` on client == address(0) without advancing `off` past the row's nE edges, and an address node 0x02||address(0) (accepted by _appendNodes, permissionless on open sets) yields client 0 with a non-empty row, so _verifyRows parses every later row at a wrong offset and the Registry-verified re-read and shape rule never run on the rows actually committed.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set: a certificate containing a row for the node address(0) with nE >= 1, followed by an agent row carrying an edge that does not exist in the registry, is accepted by submitCertificate (the same certificate without the address(0) row reverts EdgeMismatch(1,0)); isTrusted then returns true for an agent that has never received feedback (status OK, trustLow 0.148 WAD, distrustUp 15 wei).
details_en.evidence: l.1120 `if (client == address(0)) continue;` skips the row without `off += nE*(W+6)`; l.469-471 _appendNodes accepts address(0); l.1179-1180 _clientRare returns client 0 for it with no nE check; _verifyRows has no `off == rows.length`, ordering or u < n check, while _rowLoop/leaves use the true parse. Scratch tests PocD.t.sol::test_zeroAddressNodeBypassesRegistryVerification and Exploit.t.sol::test_exploit_zeroAddressDesync PASS on the current source (copied unchanged into phase2/v1a_work); controls test_controlFabricationRefused / test_control_fabricationRefused PASS (EdgeMismatch(1,0)).
details_en.fix: Advance off by nE*(W+6) (or require nE == 0) before the continue, reject address(0) in _appendNodes, and require off == rows.length at the end of _verifyRows (ideally parse rows once, shared with _rowLoop).

constats.titre: Après la désynchronisation K6, une ligne sans source portant des arêtes est inattaquable
constats.resume: Même cause que K6, conséquence pire : la ligne d'un agent sans SRC mais avec des arêtes (interdite par la règle de forme, contrôlée seulement dans `_clientRare`, jamais atteint) est engagée, et aucune preuve ne l'atteint : `proveEdge` revert `BadProof(7)` (l.1817) et `proveWallet` revert `NothingToProve` tant que l'agentWallet reste à 0. Comme elle gonfle la masse, elle gagne aussi la voie rapide du remplacement.
constats.scenario: Agent B sans wallet ; certificat avec la ligne address(0) puis la ligne de B sans SRC et l'arête fabriquée B→X : accepté, `isTrusted(X)` vrai, les deux preuves échouent. Le certificat honnête est refusé `NotBetter` (masse 0,5556 contre 0,7037 WAD, MESURÉ) et l'attaquant reprend la place après chaque fenêtre de rafraîchissement : X reste payable indéfiniment.
constats.correctif: Corriger K6 ; en défense en profondeur, faire respecter « ligne d'agent sans SRC ⇒ nE = 0 » dans `_rowLoop` et dans `_verifyRows` lui-même.

details_en.summary: Same root cause as K6, different consequence: after the desync, a source-less agent row WITH edges (forbidden by the shape rule, checked only in _clientRare l.1168, which is never reached) is committed, and no proof can challenge it: proveEdge reverts BadProof(7) and proveWallet reverts NothingToProve.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set, agent B with agentWallet = 0: a certificate with the address(0) row followed by B's row without SRC but with an edge to agent X (no such feedback in the registry) is accepted; isTrusted(X) is true; proveEdge(B's row, X) reverts BadProof(7) (l.1817) and proveWallet reverts NothingToProve (_sourceHolds l.1833 returns true for a source-less row while agentWallet is 0), so the edge stands until the certificate is replaced or expires, removing the after-the-fact correction that limits K6.
details_en.evidence: Scratch Exploit.t.sol::test_exploit_unprovable PASS on the current source: both proof calls revert as stated and isTrusted(101) is still true afterwards. l.1168 is the only place requiring a source-less agent row to be empty (H_NE == 0); l.1817 `if (v.wallet == address(0)) revert BadProof(7)`; l.1831-1833 return true for wallet == 0 rows when agentWallet == 0.
details_en.fix: Same as K6 (the desync is the enabler); as defence in depth, also enforce the source-less-row emptiness in _rowLoop (H_SRC clear on an agent row => nE == 0) so it cannot be skipped by a parse error.

constats.titre: La garde « REFUSED first » se contourne en réencodant le certificat
constats.resume: La garde compare les racines brutes (`vectorRoot`, `graphRoot`), or l'encodage n'est pas canonique : W = 4 accepté pour nCert ≤ 65 535, ligne vide d'un nœud sans masse, SPLUS égal à S⁺, empreintes non vérifiées des ancres et des agents sans masse, SRC à zéro sur une ligne d'ancre (K10). Un certificat déjà prouvé faux se resoumet sous d'autres racines et ses preuves sont effacées.
constats.scenario: Titulaire prouvé dilué (eLow > 0, agent non trusted) : la resoumission identique octet pour octet est refusée, la même réencodée en W = 4 ou avec une ligne vide en plus est acceptée, eLow revient à 0 et l'agent redevient trusted, y compris par la voie rapide (MESURÉ, tests `FinderA`).
constats.correctif: Rendre l'encodage canonique (W = 2 ssi nCert ≤ 65 535, refuser SPLUS = S⁺, refuser les lignes des nœuds sans masse, empreinte 0 pour ancres/agents sans masse, bits SRC testés) ou fonder la garde sur la sémantique (tant que le titulaire est prouvé, exiger une amélioration stricte).

details_en.summary: The REFUSED-first guard compares raw vectorRoot/graphRoot, but the encoding is not canonical (W = 4 accepted for nCert <= 65535 at l.638, an extra empty row of a zero-mass node, SPLUS == S+, unchecked ownerFp lanes of anchors and zero-mass agents), so a certificate already proven wrong can be resubmitted with identical semantics under different roots and its proofs are erased.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set, incumbent proven to dilute a row (eLow > 0, agent X STALE/not trusted): the byte-identical resubmission is refused (NotBetter), but the same vectors with rows re-encoded at W = 4, or with an added empty row for a zero-mass agent, are accepted; eLow returns to 0, quality().proven becomes false and the diluted X is trusted again; it also passes through the fast path when the incumbent is not stale (eLowMax = 1 WAD).
details_en.evidence: l.576 `if (proven && vRoot == s.vectorRoot && P.root == s.graphRoot) revert NotBetter(...)`; l.638 only rejects W == 2 with n > 0xffff (ENCODING §3.2: W = 2 iff nCert <= 65535); l.1187 _verifyOwners starts at i = k and skips zero-mass agents. Scratch FinderA.t.sol::test_W4ReencodingErasesProofs, test_extraEmptyRowErasesProofs and test_W4ReencodingFastPath PASS on the current source.
details_en.fix: Make the encoding canonical (require W == 2 iff nCert <= 65535, reject SPLUS == S+, reject rows of zero-mass nodes, require ownerFp == 0 for anchors and zero-mass agents), or base the guard on semantics (while proven, require a strict improvement) instead of raw roots.

constats.titre: Un seul avis à tag long rend un couple illisible : soumission et preuves bloquées
constats.resume: `_readFb` ne donne que `VIEW_CALL_GAS` (120 k) à `readFeedback`, qui recopie `tag1` et `tag2` sans limite de longueur (registre v2.0.0). Le client d'une arête engagée rend son propre couple illisible avec un avis à long `tag2` : toute soumission Registry-verified qui engage ce couple revert `RegistryUnreadable` (l.1134) et `proveEdge` aussi (l.1657).
constats.scenario: Le wallet d'un agent massif a une arête engagée X→Y (par ex. un slash, jamais omissible) et poste un avis sur Y avec un `tag2` d'environ 13 ko (seuil MESURÉ entre 12 500 et 13 000 octets dans `submitCertificate`, 7,4 M gas pour l'écrire) : le certificat honnête est refusé à chaque tour, le set passe STALE après maxAge et tous les payeurs refusent. Le solveur n'implémente ni l'omission sous sPlus (arête positive) ni le retrait de ligne (arête négative).
constats.correctif: Dans les chemins payants (`_verifyRows`, `proveEdge`), transmettre le gas restant (ou un plafond large) aux lectures du registre et garder `VIEW_CALL_GAS` pour les vues ; borner le coût total par une fenêtre de relecture engagée (voir EFF1).

details_en.summary: _readFb forwards only VIEW_CALL_GAS (120k) to readFeedback, which copies tag1 AND tag2 (unbounded strings) out of storage, so the client of a committed edge can make its own pair permanently unreadable with one long-tag feedback: every Registry-verified submission committing that pair reverts RegistryUnreadable and every proveEdge on it reverts too.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set; agent X has mass, its wallet OX has a committed edge X->Y (e.g. a slash, which may never be omitted). OX posts ONE feedback on Y, tag1 'note' (out of the filter), tag2 of ~13 kB (7.4M gas, ~0.75 MON at GAS.md's 102 gwei; 20 kB = 11.3M gas for margin against page alignment). _pairEdge reads that feedback first (scan from the last index), the 120k staticcall runs out of gas, _readFb returns ok=false, _verifyRows reverts RegistryUnreadable (l.1134): the honest certificate is refused every round, the set goes STALE after maxAge and every TrustGatedPayer on it refuses. For a negative edge the only sound escape is to drop X's whole row (ENCODING §3.2: negatives are never omitted; the truncation margin ~(1-alpha) t_X / alpha lands on every column, prohibitive for a directly endorsed X); for a positive edge the contract also allows omission under a declared sPlus. The reference solver implements neither, so with the shipped tooling any client of a provided row can do this. proveEdge on that pair also reverts (l.1657), so a stale committed edge of X can no longer be challenged.
details_en.evidence: l.45 VIEW_CALL_GAS = 120_000; l.1600 `staticcall(VIEW_CALL_GAS, rep, ...)` for readFeedback; l.1523 `if (!rok) return (false, 0, 0, 0);`; l.1134 / l.1657 `if (!ok) revert RegistryUnreadable();`. Upstream v2.0.0 (scratchpad/ReputationRegistryUpgradeable.sol): giveFeedback stores `tag2: tag2` with no length check, readFeedback `return (f.value, f.valueDecimals, f.tag1, f.tag2, f.isRevoked);` (CR-conseil.md:574 'VERIFIE on-chain + source', IERC8004.sol same ABI). Re-ran finder PoC e/c/test/LongTag.t.sol: 5/5 pass (40 kB tag2: write 22.4M gas, read 363,574 gas). Own bracket in the real submitCertificate flow, isolated tx, network=monad (phase2/v5a_work/c/test/V5aLongTag.t.sol): negative edge X->Y + one 'note' feedback: tag2 12,500 B accepted, 13,000 B -> RegistryUnreadable (write 7,391,179 gas), 20,000 B (positive edge too) -> RegistryUnreadable. The finder's 11,406 B threshold is a staticcall from the test context (cold registry account); the exact threshold moves by a few hundred bytes with MIP-8 page alignment, the conclusion does not.
details_en.fix: In the paying paths (_verifyRows at submission, proveEdge) forward the remaining gas (or a large explicit cap) to getLastIndex/readFeedback and keep VIEW_CALL_GAS for the view paths (assess/isTrusted/_lastFeedback); bound the total re-read cost with a committed scan bound (see EFF1).

constats.titre: Table des nœuds reconstruite depuis le calldata externe : un `addNodes` relayé arrête certificateur et watcher
constats.resume: `chain_table` décode l'input de la transaction derrière chaque `NodesAdded` et lève si ce n'est pas un appel direct ; `addNodes` est ouvert à tous sur un set ouvert. Le watcher saute aussi (« undecodable ») tout certificat soumis via un contrat.
constats.scenario: Un `addNodes` via Multicall3, un Safe, un compte 4337 ou un EOA 7702 : `RuntimeError cannot decode the transaction behind NodesAdded` à chaque tour (MESURÉ), plus aucun certificat ni preuve, set STALE. Coût : une transaction. L'adaptateur `demo/certify.py` lit déjà `nodeKeyAt`, pas les `main`.
constats.correctif: Synchroniser la table par `nodeCount`/`nodeKeyAt` ; récupérer un `submitCertificate` relayé par trace d'appels.

details_en.summary: chain_table rebuilds the node table by decoding the OUTER calldata of the transaction behind each NodesAdded log and raises when it is not a direct addNodes/submitCertificate call; addNodes is permissionless on open sets, so one addNodes made through any contract permanently stops both the certifier and the watcher, which both sync through chain_table; separately, the watcher skips (never audits) a certificate submitted through a contract.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open (Registry-verified, no submitters) set. Anyone calls AnchoredReputation.addNodes(setId, 0x01||agentId) through Multicall3.aggregate3, a Safe, an ERC-4337 account or an EIP-7702-delegated EOA (_gate lets everyone in when numSubmitters == 0). NodesAdded is emitted but `cast tx <hash> input` returns the wrapper's selector, so chain_table raises RuntimeError('cannot decode the transaction behind NodesAdded'). Certifier.table never advances _table_block and certifier.main keeps the window, so every later run_once raises on the same log; watcher.main does the same (journal 'error', retry the same window). No certificate is ever submitted again (the set goes STALE after maxAge, every payment refused) and no proof is ever sent. Cost: one transaction appending a single node, no mass, no stake. Variant: an attacker who replaces the certificate through the refresh window via a wrapper contract is logged 'undecodable' by watch_once and never audited or proven.
details_en.evidence: certifier.py:308-314 `inp = chain.tx_input(...)`; `if inp[:10] == _selector(ADD_NODES_SIG) ... elif ... SUBMIT_SIG ... else: raise RuntimeError(...)`, docstring l.298 admits a multisig/router 'raises'; certifier.py:534-539 Certifier.table sets _table_block only after chain_table returns; certifier.py:686-687 main keeps frm on error; watcher.py:295-305 the same chain_table in a retry-forever try; watcher.py:189-193 decode_submission decodes the outer input only and watcher.py:211-215 turns the failure into 'undecodable' + continue. AnchoredReputation.sol:398-401 `_gate`: only `numSubmitters != 0` restricts addNodes (l.406-410); l.436-441 `nodeKeyAt(setId, i)` exposes every key. Re-ran scratchpad/a5/table_dos.py (NodesAdded behind a Multicall3 input): RuntimeError on rounds 0, 1, 2; checked locally that `cast decode-calldata submitCertificate(...)` on a wrapper input exits 1 ('ABI decoding failed'). The demo adapter (demo/certify.py, journal/06.md) already avoids this by reading nodeCount/nodeKeyAt; solver/certifier.py main and watcher.main do not.
details_en.fix: Sync the table from the views (nodeCount, then nodeKeyAt(setId, i) for i in [len(table), nodeCount)) instead of decoding transactions, and in the watcher recover a wrapped submitCertificate from a call trace (debug_traceTransaction callTracer) rather than skipping it.

constats.titre: Titulaire prouvé puis registre remis à l'identique : le set reste mort
constats.resume: Si le titulaire a été prouvé (eLowEff > 0) et que le registre revient exactement à son contenu, la recertification honnête est identique : `run_once` la saute même quand le set est STALE, `replacement_wait` lève au rafraîchissement, et la garde REFUSED-first du contrat (avant les clauses d'âge) la refuserait de toute façon, même après maxAge.
constats.scenario: Trois transactions bon marché : l'owner d'un agent fait `setApprovalForAll(A)` (ou change son agentWallet), quelqu'un prouve (`proveEdge`/`proveWallet`), l'owner annule. Set ouvert STALE indéfiniment (MESURÉ, `B1Freeze.t.sol`, `stuck_modes.py`) ; set attesté bloqué jusqu'au rafraîchissement.
constats.correctif: 04-bis : ne jamais sauter tant que le titulaire est prouvé ou STALE, et soumettre un certificat distinct valide si besoin. 02-bis : exempter un titulaire STALE de REFUSED-first quand les relectures passent.

details_en.summary: Once the incumbent has been proven (eLowEff > 0 or eEff widened) and the registry is put back to the incumbent's exact content, the honest recomputation is byte-identical: run_once skips it as identical even while the set is STALE through eLowEff > eLowMax, then at the refresh replacement_wait raises, and the contract's REFUSED-first guard (checked before the age and eLow conditions) refuses it even after maxAge, so the reference certifier can never recertify the set.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set; certificate C commits A -> X (+1). X's owner calls setApprovalForAll(A, true) (or approve(A, X)); anyone calls proveEdge on A's row for X (R6 now gives wNew = 0: eLow widened, proven = true; for an anchor row eLowEff easily exceeds eLowMax, i.e. STALE at once); the owner then revokes the approval. The registry equals C again, so certify() rebuilds C byte for byte: run_once journals skip_identical (the skip ignores proven and eLowEff), and once refresh is due replacement_wait raises 'resubmitting the same certificate is refused' on every round, also past maxAge; the contract would revert NotBetter anyway. The set stays STALE and every payment is refused until some unrelated registry change alters the certificate (or someone appends a node by hand). Same with agentWallet W1 -> W2, proveWallet, W2 -> W1 on a massive agent. Cost: 3 cheap transactions. On an attested set the identical certificate is accepted, but run_once still skips it while the set is STALE, for up to maxAge - refreshLead (about 22 h).
details_en.evidence: certifier.py:578 `if (gr, vr) == (oc.graph_root, oc.vector_root) and not refresh and not oc.registry_changed:` -> skip_identical, no test of oc.proven or oc.e_low_eff > cfg.e_low_max; certifier.py:511-512 `if same_content and oc.proven: raise ValueError(...)`; AnchoredReputation.sol:575-576 `bool proven = s.eLowEff != 0 || s.eEff > s.eSubmitted; if (proven && vRoot == s.vectorRoot && P.root == s.graphRoot) revert NotBetter(...)` placed before the `age > s.maxAge || s.eLowEff > s.eLowMax` acceptance at l.577. Forge on an unchanged copy of contracts/src (scratchpad phase1/B1/c/test/B1Freeze.t.sol, re-run, PASS): proven via setOperator + proveEdge, registry restored, identical resubmission refused before and 5,000 blocks after maxAge = 1,000, assess = STALE, isTrusted false. Python (scratchpad phase2/v7a_work/stuck_modes.py, real Certifier.run_once on a fake chain with eLowEff 1e17 > eLowMax): open set: young -> skip_identical, refresh due -> ValueError, past maxAge -> ValueError, 0 sends; attested set: young -> skip_identical, refresh due -> certified. Re-ran scratchpad/phase1/C1/stuck_identical.py: same.
details_en.fix: In run_once never skip while the incumbent is proven or STALE, and when the honest recomputation equals a proven incumbent submit a distinct valid certificate (e.g. append one node so nCert and vectorRoot change); on the contract side (02-bis) consider exempting a STALE incumbent (age > maxAge or eLowEff > eLowMax) from the REFUSED-first guard when the re-reads pass.

constats.titre: Le certificateur n'écoute pas le contrat : un certificat censuré par un tiers reste en place environ 22 h
constats.resume: La boucle ne se réveille que sur les events des deux registres ou sur l'âge du certificat courant, jamais sur `CertificateSubmitted`/`EdgeProven`/`RowVoided` : la réponse « re-remplacé aussitôt par l'honnête » sur laquelle compte ENCODING §5 n'a pas lieu.
constats.scenario: Après minRefresh (600 blocs), un tiers soumet le point fixe exact d'un graphe censuré (vouches d'un rival omis, slash pardonné) : accepté par la fenêtre ; trust du rival 0,074 → 0 WAD (MESURÉ) ; le certificateur dort environ 268 000 blocs (environ 22 h, CALCULÉ à 0,302 s) alors que le certificat honnête serait accepté dans le même bloc.
constats.correctif: Écouter les events du set (ou comparer `certificate(setId)` au dernier certificat soumis) et recalculer aussitôt.

details_en.summary: The certifier loop only wakes on IdentityRegistry/ReputationRegistry events or on the age of the CURRENT certificate, never on AnchoredReputation events, so when a third party replaces the honest certificate with a censored one through the refresh window, the immediate honest re-replacement that ENCODING §5 relies on never happens and the censorship stands for about maxAge - refreshLead.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set, honest incumbent C (q = 0) older than minRefresh (600 blocks by default, about 3 min). Anyone submits C', the exact fixed point of the same registry with some endorsements of a rival agent (or the slash edges of a non-anchor row on agent Y) omitted: every committed edge is real, q' = 0 <= q_cur + slackRefresh, so the refresh window accepts it. registry_events polls only the two registries and relevant() never sees CertificateSubmitted/EdgeProven/RowVoided; due_refresh now measures the age of C', so run_once is not called again until an unrelated relevant registry event or about 268,000 blocks (about 22 h at 0.302 s). Meanwhile the rival is untrusted (its trust 0.074 WAD -> 0 in the forge test) or Y's forgiven slash makes it payable; after the honest recertification the attacker repeats after minRefresh. Cost: one submitCertificate per cycle.
details_en.evidence: certifier.py:611-639 REGISTRY_EVENTS/registry_events read only the identity and reputation addresses; certifier.py:678-681 `evs = [... registry_events(chain, a.identity, a.reputation, frm, head) ...]`, `due = svc.due_refresh(OnChain.read(...), head)`, `if first or evs or due:`; certifier.py:555-556 due_refresh = `head - oc.cert_block > max_age - refresh_lead` (cert_block of whoever submitted last). AnchoredReputation.sol:579 `(age > s.minRefresh && qNew <= qCur + s.slackRefresh)` admits the censored certificate. ENCODING.md:202-204 'A certificate that slipped through it is re-replaced by the honest one at once (more mass, same q)'. Forge on an unchanged copy of contracts/src (scratchpad phase2/v7a_work/forge/test/V7aThird.t.sol): censored certificate from 0xBAD accepted after minRefresh, trust(Y) 74074074074074074 -> 0, then the honest certificate is accepted again in the same block (trust back), so only the trigger is missing. Re-ran scratchpad/a5/no_retrigger.py (third_party): after the replacement at block 1705, no run_once and no send over 80 rounds (head 2625).
details_en.fix: Poll the set's own CertificateSubmitted/EdgeProven/RowVoided/RegistryChanged events (or compare certificate(setId) with the last certificate this service submitted each round) and recompute at once when the incumbent is not ours or was widened.

constats.titre: 257 avis négatifs d'une simple adresse bloquent toute recertification
constats.resume: `certify()` applique `cap_row` à la ligne de CHAQUE nœud avant de connaître la masse, et `cap_row` lève au-delà de ROW_MAX arêtes négatives : une adresse sans agent (masse toujours nulle, ligne jamais fournie) suffit à faire lever chaque recalcul. Le saut des lignes sans masse existait avant le commit 04e7cf3.
constats.scenario: N'importe quelle adresse poste 257 `slash` −100 (ou `review` −1) sur 257 agents : `ValueError row with 257 negative edges > ROW_MAX` (MESURÉ, `a/dos_rowmax.py`), le certificateur réessaie à l'infini, le set passe STALE après maxAge et tous les payeurs refusent. Sets ouverts comme attestés ; touche la démo (filtre avec `slash`).
constats.correctif: Reporter le contrôle des négatifs après le calcul de masse (les négatifs ne changent pas t) et ne lever (ou tronquer) que pour une ligne massive.

details_en.summary: certify() applies cap_row to the row of EVERY graph node before it knows which rows carry mass, and cap_row raises on more than ROW_MAX negative edges, so one zero-mass plain address with 257 negative feedbacks makes every recomputation of the set raise, although that row would never be provided.
details_en.failure_scenario: Any address X that owns no agent posts 257 giveFeedback(tag1='slash', value=-100) (or 'review' -1, or a quality score below neutral) on 257 distinct existing agents (permissionless in ERC-8004 v2.0.0). build_graph makes X an address node whose row has 257 negative edges (address nodes never receive edges, so X's mass is always 0). On the next run_once (any relevant event, the due refresh, or a restart) certify() -> cap_row raises ValueError('row with 257 negative edges > ROW_MAX'); certifier.main journals 'error', keeps the window and retries the same failing round forever, so the set is never recertified, goes STALE after maxAge and isTrusted/TrustGatedPayer refuse every agent. X's own feedbacks are not 'relevant' events, so the crash fires at the next honest trigger or refresh. Works on open AND attested sets whose filter has a negative-capable tag (core/reference filters, the demo set with 'slash'); cost about 257 feedback txs, no mass, no stake.
details_en.evidence: ppr.py:331-332 `committed = {u: cap_row([...g.rows.get(u, [])], is_anchor=u in anchors) for u in range(g.n)}` runs before power_from_zero; ppr.py:302-304 `if len(neg) > ROW_MAX: raise ValueError(...)`; ppr.py:339 then drops every zero-mass row anyway (`rows = {u: r ... if any(t[a][u] ...)}`); graph.py:524 and 558-560: every client that is neither an agent's wallet nor an anchor becomes an address node carrying its full row; certifier.py:544 compute -> certify, not caught in run_once; certifier.py:686-687 main catches, logs 'error' and does not advance frm/first. Re-ran scratchpad/a/dos_rowmax.py and a5/dos_service.py: honest graph certifies (n=4), with 257 'slash' (or 'review' -1) from a zero-mass EOA: 'ValueError row with 257 negative edges > ROW_MAX=256: cannot be certified honestly'. FORMAT.md:88 documents the raise for a row that must be certified; ENCODING §3.2 and FORMAT.md:93 say a zero-mass row SHOULD NOT be provided, so no honest certificate needs it.
details_en.fix: Defer the ROW_MAX-negatives check until the mass is known: negative edges do not change t, so iterate on the (capped) positive parts, then drop every zero-mass row as ppr.py:339 already does, and raise (or truncate the whole row, paying the truncation margin) only for a massive row with more than ROW_MAX negatives.

constats.titre: Watcher : dilution jugée arête par arête, jamais cumulée
constats.resume: `audit()` teste chaque arête omise seule (`S⁺ + q > B⁺`) : plusieurs omissions positives qui tiennent chacune sous B⁺ mais le dépassent ensemble sont toutes « OMITTED_POSITIVE » non prouvables, alors que le contrat les facture par une chaîne de preuves. Le test par ligne a été remplacé au commit 9959ffb.
constats.scenario: Le wallet de l'agent #1 recommande 10 agents à +5 000 ; un certificat ne garde que #1→#2 : 9 OMITTED_POSITIVE, rien de prouvé, t(#2) × 5 (MESURÉ, `wA/t1`), alors que la 2ᵉ preuve facturerait dec = 0,333 WAD à eLow. Sur un set ouvert, ce certificat entre par la fenêtre de rafraîchissement.
constats.correctif: Décider la dilution par ligne (vrai B⁺ du client contre B⁺ engagé) et prouver toutes les omissions de la ligne en une chaîne d'amendements.

details_en.summary: audit() decides dilution one omitted edge at a time (`elif s_plus + pe.q > b_plus:`), so several omitted positive edges that each fit under B+ = max(GRID, sPlus or S0) but together exceed it are all classified OMITTED_POSITIVE (provable=False) and never proven, although the contract bills their dilution to eLow through a chain of proveEdge calls; the module's premise 'OMITTED_POSITIVE without dilution: t stays a lower bound' is false cumulatively.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set: wallet W of agent #1 (mass from anchor A) vouches #2..#11 at +5000 each (true S+ = 50000). A third party submits, through the refresh window (age > minRefresh, q unchanged), a certificate whose row of #1 keeps only W->#2 (S0 = 5000, no sPlus, B+ = GRID). Each omitted edge gives 5000 + 5000 > 10000 = false -> 9 x OMITTED_POSITIVE, nothing proven; t(#2) = 0.037 WAD instead of 0.0074 (x5.0, re-run of wA/t1) with eLow = 0, so trustLow(#2) is 5x its true value and isTrusted/TrustGatedPayer can approve #2. On chain the 1st omission proof is _side(5000,0,5000,GRID) = (dec 0, inc 0.5) and the 2nd _side(10000,0,5000,GRID) bills dec 0.333 WAD to eLow (cumulative cap S0/B0 = 0.5 >= true decrease 0.4).
details_en.evidence: watcher.py:133-137 per-edge test, OMITTED_POSITIVE hint 'no dilution: t stays a lower bound'; still_dilutes (l.170-176) only re-checks rows already classified DILUTION/DEFLATED. Re-ran scratchpad/wA/t1_cumulative_dilution.py at a8eefc5: 'ratio 5.0', 'provable: []'. Contract _side (AnchoredReputation.sol:1888-1898) computed by hand for the chain above. ENCODING.md §5: 'Dilution (under-declared sPlus) still passes: AM-02.2, only a watcher with proveEdge closes it'; PROOFS.md: 't <= t* n'est garanti qu'après que tout écart existant a été prouvé'. Regression: 9959ffb removed the row-level test `committed_bplus < max(GRID, true_plus)`.
details_en.fix: Decide dilution per row: if max(GRID, true registry S+ of the client) > committed B+ (or the committed shares exceed the true ones), mark every omitted positive edge of the row provable and prove them as one amendment chain (stopping once the amended row matches the registry).

constats.titre: Watcher : la liste d'amendements n'est jamais reconstruite depuis la chaîne
constats.resume: Chaque ligne repart de `amends = []` avec le poids de l'export, alors que le contrat authentifie une ligne amendée par `keccak(leaf ‖ amends)` avec le wNew réel : dès qu'une preuve a touché une ligne (tiers, soumetteur tricheur, redémarrage, wNew réel différent de l'export), toutes les preuves suivantes du watcher sur cette ligne revert `BadProof(5)`.
constats.scenario: Griefing : le soumetteur omet une arête diluante D et une petite arête s, puis prouve lui-même s (presque gratuit) ; la preuve de D par le watcher revert `BadProof(5)`, la ligne est abandonnée et le certificat n'est plus jamais audité (test du dépôt `Verified.t.sol:302-304` qui vérifie exactement ce revert).
constats.correctif: Reconstruire les amendements depuis les events `EdgeProven` du certNonce courant (contrôlés par `rowStateOf`) et chaîner avec le wNew de l'event.

details_en.summary: Each row's amendment chain always starts empty (`amends = []`) and is extended with the snapshot weight d.w_registry, never rebuilt from the chain (no rowStateOf/EdgeProven read anywhere in solver/), while the contract authenticates an amended row by RowState.h = keccak(leaf || amends with the LIVE wNew) per certNonce: once any proof has landed on a row (any third party, the cheating submitter, a retried window, a restart) or the live wNew differs from the export, every later watcher proof on that row reverts BadProof(5) and, with the break at l.236 and the single audit, the row's remaining discrepancies are never proven.
details_en.failure_scenario: Griefing on an open set: the submitter commits a row that omits a diluting edge D (DILUTION, provable) and a tiny edge s of the same client, then immediately calls proveEdge(s) itself (dec 0, eUp + q_s/B: negligible). The watcher's next round sends proveEdge(D) with amends = 0x and the Merkle path; _openRow sees st.h != 0 and keccak(leaf) != st.h -> BadProof(5) -> 'error', break, frm advances: D's dilution is never billed to eLow and t stays inflated. Without an attacker: round 1 proves 2 facts, then OnChain.read in liveness() raises -> frm kept -> round 2 re-audits the same certificate from amends = [] -> BadProof(5); a restart with --from-block <= certBlock does the same; and if the export says q = 3000 while the live registry gives 2000, the contract stores (j, w, 2000), the watcher chains (j, w, 3000) and the next proof of the row reverts BadProof(5).
details_en.evidence: watcher.py:224 `amends: list[...] = []` per row; l.238 `amends = amend(amends, d)` with amend() using d.w_registry (l.184-186); prove() sends the Merkle path when amends is empty (l.141-143). Contract _openRow (AnchoredReputation.sol:1797-1803): `if (st.h == 0) {...} else if (keccak256(abi.encodePacked(v.leaf, amends)) != st.h) revert BadProof(5);` and l.1678 stores `_amend(amends, agentJ, m.wCommitted, wNew)` with the live wNew. test/Verified.t.sol:302-304 asserts exactly this revert for a second proof sent with amends = "". `grep rowStateOf|EdgeProven solver/*.py`: no match.
details_en.fix: Before proving a row, rebuild its amendment list from the chain (EdgeProven logs of the current certNonce, checked against rowStateOf(u).h) and chain each success with the wNew read from its EdgeProven event, not the export's q.

constats.titre: Un `registerAnchorSet` avec alphaD ≥ 2^31 arrête l'indexeur sur les trois chaînes
constats.resume: `AnchorSetRegistered` écrit les uint32 alphaN/alphaD dans des colonnes `Int` (Int32 d'Envio, INTEGER Postgres, maximum 2^31 − 1), alors que `registerAnchorSet` est ouvert à tous et n'exige que 0 < alphaN < alphaD : l'écriture du lot échoue, Envio la traite comme fatale et la rejoue à chaque redémarrage.
constats.scenario: N'importe qui enregistre sur le contrat configuré (gratuit sur testnet) un set valide avec alphaN = 1, alphaD = 3 000 000 000 : indexeur arrêté pour de bon (endpoint GraphQL, export du solveur, écran de démo). Latent tant que l'adresse configurée est le placeholder, exploitable dès le branchement prévu par le MUSTDO ; le store en mémoire des tests ne peut pas le voir (lecture du code d'Envio 3.12.1, Postgres non exécuté).
constats.correctif: Déclarer alphaN/alphaD en `BigInt` (ou en chaîne) dans `schema.graphql`, et passer en revue les autres colonnes `Int` alimentées par des valeurs du contrat.

details_en.summary: AnchorSetRegistered writes the event's uint32 alphaN/alphaD into AnchorSet.alphaN/alphaD, declared `Int` in schema.graphql (Envio Int32 -> Postgres INTEGER, max 2^31-1), while registerAnchorSet is permissionless and only requires 0 < alphaN < alphaD: one registration with alphaD >= 2^31 makes the batch write fail, which Envio treats as fatal for the whole multichain indexer and replays on every restart.
details_en.failure_scenario: Anyone calls registerAnchorSet on the configured ANCRE contract (testnet: free) with valid params and alphaN = 1, alphaD = 3 000 000 000 (anchors increasing, lambdas summing to 1e18, 1 tag, valid policy: the contract checks only alphaN != 0 && alphaN < alphaD, AnchoredReputation.sol:277). ancre.ts:50 sets alphaD: Number(3000000000); at flush the AnchorSet row is converted with S.int / cast to INTEGER[] -> 'value out of range for type integer' (or an S.Raised conversion error), classifyWriteError does not treat it as an encoding error -> rethrown -> FatalError: the indexer (all 3 chains, the GraphQL endpoint read by solver/from_indexer.py and the demo screen) stops, and every restart replays the same batch. The scratch test indexer (in-memory, no Postgres) stores [1, 3000000000, true] without complaint, so the repo's tests cannot catch it.
details_en.evidence: ancre.ts:50 `alphaN: Number(event.params.alphaN), alphaD: Number(event.params.alphaD),`; schema.graphql:139-140 `alphaN: Int` / `alphaD: Int`; Envio 3.12.1 Config.res:388 `| "int" => (Table.Int32, S.int)`, db/Table.res:174 `Int32 => Postgres.Integer`, bindings/Postgres.res:118 `@as("INTEGER")`; PgStorage.res:866-878 conversion/insert errors wrapped as StorageError, :784-794 classifyWriteError escapes only the two NUL/Unicode messages (S.Raised rethrown), :1561-1574 rethrow -> fatal (same path as V9's LONGTAG). Contract: AnchoredReputation.sol:110-111 `uint32 alphaN; uint32 alphaD;`, :277 `if (p.alphaN == 0 || p.alphaN >= p.alphaD) revert BadParams(2);`, registerAnchorSet has no access control (:274). Scratch test sweep/ix/test/sweep.test.ts 'ALPHA' -> 'ALPHA stored [1,3000000000,true]' (in-memory test store, no INTEGER column). (Other Int columns fed by contract values are bounded in practice: nCert/numRows/index by the node table size, w by the grid; Discrepancy.bCommitted/bRegistry would need a client row of > 214 748 max-weight edges.)

constats.titre: Les NUL de `tag1` : collision d'identifiants (arrêt) et tags fantômes
constats.resume: Sur une erreur Postgres liée à un NUL, Envio réessaie en retirant U+0000 de toutes les chaînes de l'entité, identifiant compris : « x » et « x\0 » donnent la même clé dans un seul upsert (erreur fatale), et un avis « vouch\0 » est stocké « vouch », exporté vers le solveur, engagé par le certificateur puis refusé par la relecture du contrat (EdgeMismatch à chaque tour).
constats.scenario: (a) Deux avis « x » et « x\0 » dans une transaction : arrêt fatal à chaque redémarrage. (b) Un avis « vouch\0 » d'un client certifié : arête fantôme, certificats refusés, set STALE (fonction d'Envio rejouée, MESURÉ).
constats.correctif: Clés et comparaisons par keccak256(tag1) comme le contrat ; stocker sans perte (hex) les tags contenant un NUL et ne jamais en faire un tag de filtre.

details_en.summary: Tags are keyed by the decoded tag1 string, but Envio 3.12.1's escape-and-retry for Postgres NUL errors strips U+0000 from every string field of the failing table, the entity id included: 'x' and 'x\0' collapse into one TripleLatest id (two rows with one key in a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is a fatal Postgres error) and a 'vouch\0' feedback is persisted as tag1 'vouch', which the solver then commits and the contract refuses.
details_en.failure_scenario: (a) Halt, anyone, a few cents: a contract client calls giveFeedback(A, 1, 0, 'x', ...) and giveFeedback(A, 1, 0, 'x\0', ...) in one transaction (same block; during a historical resync any two such feedbacks in one batch suffice). The first write fails on 0x00, the retry strips both TripleLatest ids to 'C-A-x' inside one unnest upsert -> Postgres 21000 'ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time' -> not an encoding error -> FatalError, on every restart. (b) Corruption: a client W whose row is certified sends giveFeedback(X, 100, 0, 'vouch\0', ...): in memory isRefTag is false, but the DB stores Feedback.tag1 = 'vouch', triple and TripleLatest 'W-X-vouch' (overwriting the genuine triple); from_indexer.py exports t1 = 'vouch', the certifier commits W->X with that feedback's index, and the Registry-verified re-read (_pairEdge matches keccak(tag1)) finds no such vouch -> EdgeMismatch on every round, the set's certificates age to STALE. The same overwrite with value 0 erases a genuine negative edge from the indexer/solver view (an omission provable against the honest certifier).
details_en.evidence: Current code: reputation.ts:16 triple from raw p.tag1, :17-23 Feedback{tag1, triple}, :28 TripleLatest{id: triple}. Envio PgStorage.res:741-762 removeInvalidUtf8DeepInPlace replaces "\x00" in every string of the entity object (id included); applied on retry to entitiesToSet (1366-1369) after classifyWriteError maps the 0x00 message to PgEncodingError (788-790) and writeBatch is re-run with escapeTables (1576-1590); entity upserts are ONE statement per table (859-863 'Use UNNEST approach for single query', ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE at 584-596), so collapsed ids collide inside one statement; any other error is fatal (Writing.res:190, Main.res:693-696). Re-ran phase1/d3/nul.mjs (Envio's own function): ids ['0xc1..-182-vouch', '0xc1..-182-vouch'] and both Feedback rows stored with tag1 'vouch'. Contract: AnchoredReputation.sol:1528-1529 `if (ts.hash != th) continue;` (tag matched by keccak); solver/from_indexer.py:130 exports `"t1": r["tag1"]` from the stored row; mismatch revert AnchoredReputation.sol:1135. Real Monad data: 0 tags containing U+0000 in the 9 290-feedback fixture (attacker-driven).
details_en.fix: Key and compare tags by keccak256(tag1) (indexedTag1) like the contract; store tags containing U+0000 losslessly (hex) and never as a filter tag, so no NUL ever reaches a key or an exported tag.

constats.titre: Un `tag1` de plus de 2 704 octets arrête l'indexeur sur les trois chaînes
constats.resume: Le `tag1` brut entre dans `TripleLatest.id` (clé primaire) et dans `Feedback.triple` (index btree) ; au-delà de la limite btree de Postgres (2 704 octets, contenu incompressible), l'insertion échoue avec une erreur qu'Envio traite comme fatale pour tout le processus, et chaque redémarrage rejoue le même lot.
constats.scenario: Un seul `giveFeedback` avec un tag1 d'environ 4 ko aléatoire sur Monad, le testnet gratuit ou Optimism : indexeur arrêté pour de bon (endpoint GraphQL, export du certificateur, écran de démo). Jugé sur la limite documentée de Postgres et le code d'Envio 3.12.1 (Postgres non disponible ici).
constats.correctif: Ne jamais mettre le tag brut dans une clé ou un index : clé = keccak256(tag1) (le topic `indexedTag1` de l'event l'est déjà).

details_en.summary: The raw, unbounded tag1 of every feedback (any tag, not only filter tags) is embedded in TripleLatest.id, a Postgres PRIMARY KEY, and in Feedback.triple, a btree @index; a tag1 longer than the btree tuple limit (2704 bytes, incompressible content) makes the batch INSERT fail with a non-NUL error, which Envio treats as fatal for the whole process (all 3 chains), and every restart replays the same batch.
details_en.failure_scenario: Anyone calls giveFeedback(anyAgent, 1, 0, tag1 = ~4 KB of random base64, ...) on Monad 143, the free Monad testnet 10143 or Optimism (the registry bounds valueDecimals and value only). reputation.ts:16 builds triple = client-agentId-tag1 and :28 upserts TripleLatest{id: triple} unconditionally; Feedback.triple is indexed. Postgres raises 54000 'index row size ... exceeds btree version 4 maximum 2704' (random base64 does not compress by the 25% pglz needs), classifyWriteError only escapes the two NUL messages, so the error is rethrown, Writing.runWriteLoop -> recordWriteFailure -> Main.onError -> FatalError: the indexer (live GraphQL endpoint, from_indexer.py export used by the certifier, demo screen) stops for good; the certifier's export cannot pass the indexer head, so certificates age to STALE.
details_en.evidence: Current code: reputation.ts:16 `const triple = `${client}-${agentId}-${p.tag1}`;`, :28 `context.TripleLatest.set({ id: triple, client, agent_id: agentId, tag1: p.tag1, feedback_id: id });` (no tag filter before it); schema.graphql:28 `triple: String! @index`, :115 TripleLatest id = client-agentId-tag1. Upstream ReputationRegistryUpgradeable.sol:95-133 giveFeedback: only `valueDecimals <= 18` and |value| <= 1e38 checks, tag1 stored and emitted as is. Envio 3.12.1: PgStorage.res:162 `PRIMARY KEY(...)` (btree), db/IndexDefinition.res:127 @index = btree; PgStorage.res:784-792 classifyWriteError retries only `invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00` / `unsupported Unicode escape sequence`, anything else is parked and rethrown (1561-1574); Writing.res:184-192 runWriteLoop -> IndexerState.res:899-902 recordWriteFailure -> Main.res:693-696 FatalError. Postgres: btree v4 max item size 2704 bytes (documented limit, 'Values larger than 1/3 of a buffer page cannot be indexed'). Postgres not available locally: judged from the documented limit and Envio's code. Real data: max tag1 length 33 bytes over the 9 290 Monad feedbacks of solver/tests/fixtures/indexer/Feedback.json, so only a deliberate feedback triggers it.
details_en.fix: Never put raw tag1 in a key or an index: key TripleLatest (and Feedback.triple) by keccak256(tag1) (the event's indexedTag1 topic already is that hash) and keep the raw tag only in a non-indexed column.

constats.titre: Nœuds parasites via `addNodes` ouvert : le set ouvert gèle (et un tiers fait monter nCert)
constats.resume: Sur un set ouvert, `addNodes` sans permission ajoute à une table append-only des entrées que chaque certificat doit couvrir dès que nCert les dépasse. Chaque nœud parasite sans masse coûte environ 3 975 gas par certificat (MESURÉ, k = 3, Registry-verified ; 1 608 en attesté), 10 à 40 fois le chiffre AM-R5.7 de GAS.md. Un tiers peut aussi renvoyer le titulaire complété de zéros pour faire monter nCert (voie rapide acceptée), ce qui efface aussi les preuves (famille K7).
constats.scenario: Le certificateur de référence certifie toute la table (`align`) : au-delà d'environ 2 100 à 7 500 nœuds parasites (10 à 35 MON, CALCULÉ à 102 gwei), aucun certificat ne tient sous la limite par transaction, le set est STALE pour de bon. Risque connu et accepté pour la démo (soumetteurs listés, tour 7), mais chiffré faux dans GAS.md, et il tue aussi les rafraîchissements, pas seulement la croissance.
constats.correctif: Implémenter D23 (zone de transit : un nœud n'entre dans la table que par un certificat accepté qui lui donne de la masse) ou une caution par nœud ajouté ; corriger GAS.md AM-R5.7 et le texte Security de l'ERC ; côté 04-bis, ne pas étendre nCert au-delà du support du certificateur.

details_en.summary: On an open set, permissionless addNodes appends junk entries (any uint32 agentId, no existence check, no deposit) to an append-only table that every certificate must cover once nCert passes them; each zero-mass junk node costs ~3,975 gas per certificate (k = 3, Registry-verified; 1,608 attested), 10-40x the AM-R5.7 figure in GAS.md, so a few thousand junk nodes push every certificate past the per-tx limit and the set is frozen for good. Any third party can also ratchet nCert over the junk at once by resubmitting the incumbent zero-padded (fast path: same mass, q, D).
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set, k = 3. The attacker calls addNodes with N junk agent entries (45,927 gas per node, measured; ~650 per 30M tx). The reference certifier always certifies the whole on-chain table (solver/certifier.py align(): 'nCert = full table'), so its next certificate carries the junk. That costs a one-off ~25.9k gas per junk node for the new vector slots (reserveCapacity at 17,261 gas per slot, 1.5 slots per node), then ~3,975 gas per junk node in EVERY later certificate, refreshes included. Measured updates: 285,376 gas with 0 junk nodes, 8,235,105 with 2,000, 32,108,299 with 8,000. No certificate fits under the 30M per-tx limit past (30M - base) / 3,975 junk nodes: ~7,500 on the 285k mock graph, ~3,800 for a 15.0M demo-size Registry-verified certificate (GAS.md). Under the certifier's own 25M tx_cap (7.5% margin) the thresholds are ~5,800 and ~2,100. Past that point the certifier raises 'gas limit > cap' every round, the set goes STALE after maxAge, and every payer bound to that setId refuses for good (the set is immutable and the table append-only). Attacker cost (computed from measured unit costs): ~2,100 to 7,500 nodes x 45.9k = 96M to 344M gas, ~10 to 35 MON at the 102 gwei measured on 28/09. Ratchet (test_nCertRatchet): after addNodes of 200 junk nodes, the incumbent resubmitted with nCert 3 -> 203 and 200 x 16 zero bytes appended to the vectors is accepted at age 0; the honest nCert = 3 certificate then reverts BadNCert. The padded copy has a new vectorRoot, so it also slips past the REFUSED-first guard of a proven incumbent (K7 family; 02-bis fix C, provenFalse per canonical row hash, closes that part).
details_en.evidence: l.405 comment 'Open sets: permissionless (AM-R5.7 stays open there, D23 staging zone not implemented)'; l.400 _gate restricts only listed submitters; l.455-485 _appendNodes: no existence check, no bound but uint32; l.506 'if (n < s.nCert || n > s.nodeCount || n < k) revert BadNCert();' (nCert never decreases); l.1187 _verifyOwners walks every node in [k, n); _verifyPass and _storeVectors are O(n). Re-ran the finder PoC (phase2/v5c_work/c/test/FinderA2.t.sol, copy of finderA/c, src identical to HEAD): 5/5 pass, 3,974 gas per junk node (0 -> 2,000), 3,978 (2,000 -> 8,000), 1,608 attested. Own measurements (phase2/v5c_work/c/test/V5cA1b.t.sol): addNodes 45,927 gas per node (the finder's 28.7k is the v0 figure), reserveCapacity 17,261 per slot. Docs: GAS.md AM-R5.7 '≈ (k+1)·8 octets + ~100-400 gas par nœud et par certificat, à vie' (wrong by 10-40x); docs/erc/anchored-reputation.md:967 already says 'Past a few thousand junk nodes (estimated), no certificate fits in one transaction, and the set is frozen for good'; docs/erc/relecture-conseil.md D1 puts the cost at '≈ 15 à 44 MON (ESTIMÉ)'; docs/conseil/tour7.md D-7.1 'On assume : AM-08.17 (addNodes ouvert) ... documentés. La démo ... liste ses soumetteurs'. So this is a known risk, accepted for the demo (listed submitters close addNodes through _gate), and the outcome matches the ERC text. What is new: measured costs (GAS.md is stale); the reference certifier carries the junk in every certificate, so the freeze kills refreshes too (STALE), not only growth; large honest certificates lower the threshold to ~2,100 junk nodes (~10 MON); a third party can ratchet nCert itself.
details_en.fix: Implement D23 (a node enters the table only through an accepted certificate that gives it mass; addNodes and reserveCapacity write to a per-submitter staging zone), or require a refundable deposit per appended node on open sets. Meanwhile, correct GAS.md AM-R5.7 and the ERC Security text with the measured figures, and (04-bis) take nCert = max(previous nCert, last index of the certifier's own support) rather than the full table, so that refreshes stay possible.

constats.titre: Règle de forme testée sur la valeur décodée de SRC, pas sur le bit H_SRC
constats.resume: `_clientRare` ne refuse qu'un wallet NON NUL : une ligne d'ancre ou d'adresse avec H_SRC et 20 octets à zéro passe, une ligne d'adresse peut servir d'alias à une autre (comparaison brute 0 = 0), une ligne d'agent avec H_SRC et source nulle est lue comme « sans source ». L'arithmétique ne change pas, mais les miroirs hors chaîne divergent et graphRoot devient malléable.
constats.scenario: L'indexeur jette `EncodingError` sur l'ancre avec SRC nul et classe le certificat UNDECODABLE (pas d'audit) ; l'audit et le watcher émettent des écarts SOURCE/SHAPE dont la preuve revert `NothingToProve`. Et après un `proveEdge`, la même soumission avec la seule ligne d'ancre réécrite ainsi est acceptée et remet eLowEff à 0 (MESURÉ, `V4Verify.t.sol`) : c'est un des réencodages de K7.
constats.correctif: Tester les bits : lignes d'ancre/adresse ⇒ revert si H_SRC ou H_VIA_OWNER ; ligne d'agent avec H_SRC ⇒ SRC non nul ; ALIAS seulement entre nœuds agents à SRC non nul.

details_en.summary: The shape rule is tested on the decoded SRC value instead of the H_SRC bit: _verifyRows only fills `wallet` when H_SRC is set, and _clientRare (l.1167-1170, 1179) rejects only a NON-ZERO wallet, so an anchor/address row carrying H_SRC + 20 zero bytes, an address-node ALIAS row (the l.1014 alias check compares raw SRC fields, 0 == 0) and an agent row with H_SRC + zero source (accepted as source-less) all pass at both levels, although ENCODING §3.2 forbids SRC on anchor/address rows and requires SRC for ALIAS; the trust arithmetic is unchanged, but the off-chain mirrors (indexer decoder/audit, watcher) disagree with the contract on these encodings and graphRoot becomes malleable.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set (anyone submits). (1) Anchor row encoded `u=0 | hdr 0x8001 | 20 zero bytes | edge` is accepted (scratch FinderAShape + V4Verify tests). indexer/src/lib/certificate.ts:64,71 turns the 20 zero bytes into src='0x00..00' (truthy) and throws EncodingError 'anchor row with SRC/VIA_OWNER' (reproduced by running decodeRows on that calldata), so handlers/ancre.ts:131-133 records the accepted certificate as UNDECODABLE and the set as UNAUDITED: the indexer audit is off for that certificate. (2) Address node Q (never gave feedback) with `hdr 0xA000 | zero SRC | ref = P` copies P's row (or the anchor row) and is accepted on a Registry-verified set (test_K10_addressAliasOfAddressRowAccepted / ...OfAnchorRowAccepted); t_Q = 0 so nothing spreads, but each copy adds its positive edges to E+, and by code reading indexer audit.ts:99-101 reports SHAPE (and FABRICATED for the copied edges, audited against Q) on a certificate the contract deems valid. (3) Agent #102 with agentWallet 0 and row `hdr 0x8000 | zero SRC`: accepted as source-less, proveWallet reverts NothingToProve (test_K10_agentRowZeroSrcAcceptedAsSourceless), while watcher.audit (have=('0x00..0','wallet') != want=(None,'')) and indexer audit.ts:94 both report a SOURCE discrepancy whose only proof reverts. (4) Each variant gives another graphRoot for identical (mass, q, D): after proveEdge widened the incumbent (eLowEff 0.333 WAD), the byte-identical resubmission reverts NotBetter, but the same certificate with its anchor row re-encoded as in (1) is accepted and resets eLowEff to 0 (test_K10_reencodedAnchorRowErasesProof). So K10 is one of the re-encodings that defeat K7's REFUSED-first guard, and the replacing certificate is at the same time undecodable by the indexer.
details_en.evidence: AnchoredReputation.sol:1109-1112 `if (hdr & H_SRC != 0) { wallet = address(bytes20(rows[off:off + 20])); ...}`; :1152 the fast path needs `wallet != address(0)`; :1167-1170 agent row `if (wallet == address(0)) { ... return address(0); }` (the H_SRC bit is never tested); :1179 `if (wallet != address(0) || via) revert EdgeMismatch(ri, ROW_MAX);`; :1011-1016 alias needs only `u >= k`, both hasW bits and `eq(shr(96, inf), wal)` (raw SRC, both 0), not the node kind or the resolved client. ENCODING.md §3.2: 'ALIAS ... both rows carry SRC and it is the same address' and 'an anchor or address row carries neither SRC nor VIA_OWNER; an agent row is either (a) SRC without VIA_OWNER ... or (c) without SRC: empty'. Scratch: phase2/v4_work/contracts/test/V4Verify.t.sol (9/9 pass), FinderAShape.t.sol (pass), phase2/v4_work/ix/k10.mjs (indexer decodeRows throws on (1), decodes (2) and (3)).
details_en.fix: Test the bits, not the value: anchor/address rows revert if hdr & (H_SRC|H_VIA_OWNER) != 0; an agent row with H_SRC must carry a non-zero SRC; ALIAS only for agent nodes with a non-zero SRC. The indexer and watcher decoders then agree with the contract.

constats.titre: `_pairEdge` relit tout l'historique d'un couple : le client d'une ligne fixe le coût de chaque soumission
constats.resume: La seule sortie anticipée du balayage exige un avis vivant sous CHAQUE tag d'endorsement du filtre, ce qu'aucun couple réel n'a ; chaque avis du couple coûte environ 12,9 k gas à chaque soumission Registry-verified et à chaque preuve. La borne MAX_SCAN a été retirée au commit b0aa1ad. Pour une arête négative, le certificateur honnête n'a aucune échappatoire.
constats.scenario: Le wallet d'un agent massif slashe Y une fois puis poste H avis « uptime » sur Y : 454 k gas sans avis supplémentaire, 5,6 M avec 400 (MESURÉ) ; environ 1 900 avis font dépasser le plafond de 25 M du certificateur sur un petit certificat, 640 pour le certificat de démo (CALCULÉ). `run_once` lève alors « gas limit > cap » à chaque tour : set STALE, payeurs bloqués. Un client massif honnête qui note après chaque interaction y arrive aussi.
constats.correctif: Engager dans la politique une fenêtre de relecture (D14 sur les scanMax derniers avis du couple, même règle dans graph.py, rules.ts et audit.ts) ; en attendant, laisser le solveur omettre les couples positifs coûteux sous sPlus et signaler les négatifs au lieu de lever.

details_en.summary: _pairEdge re-reads the whole feedback history of every committed pair (its only early exit, seen == endoMask, needs a live feedback under EVERY endorsement tag of the filter), so the client of a provided row controls the cost of every Registry-verified submission and proof touching its pair (~12.9k gas per feedback, unbounded since MAX_SCAN was removed in b0aa1ad), and for a negative edge the honest certifier has no omission escape.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set with the reference filter (review/slash/vouch endorsement + uptime measurement). Agent X has mass; its wallet slashes Y once (a negative edge: never omittable, ENCODING §3.2) and then posts H feedbacks on Y under 'uptime' (or any tag that leaves some endorsement tag unseen). Each later submission re-reads all H (12,851 gas each, isolated, network=monad): H ~ 1,900 (~338M gas, ~34 MON at GAS.md's 102 gwei) pushes even a small certificate over certifier.py's tx_cap of 25M, H ~ 640 (~11.6 MON) for the 15M demo certificate. run_once then raises 'gas limit > cap' every round (certify() has no omission/truncation fallback), the set goes STALE after maxAge and every payer on it refuses. Also reached without malice by a massive client posting per-interaction or monitoring feedback (288/day at one per 5 min). Below the cap the extra cost recurs on every recertification; a proof on such a pair costs the same, so beyond ~2,300 feedbacks a committed weight on that pair becomes unprovable.
details_en.evidence: l.1521-1541 scan from `last` down to 1 with `if (seen == allMask) break;` (l.1538) as the only early exit, allMask = s.endoMask (l.1512); comment l.1500-1501 'it is unbounded otherwise, at the caller's expense'. b0aa1ad removed `MAX_SCAN = 32` / `lo = last > MAX_SCAN ? ...`. Re-ran effbench/test/Scan.t.sol: H=0 467,395; H=200 uptime after a slash 3,037,695 (12,851/fb); 201 vouches 2,979,057 (12,558/fb). Re-ran phase1/B1/c B1Scan: 454,725 / 1,731,875 / 5,595,325 gas for 0/100/400 extra feedbacks. GAS.md P1 (real registries, fork): ~13k per extra feedback, and limit 2 only offers 'omit these edges and declare B+' (positive edges) or switching to Submitter-attested (a new setId); ENCODING §3.2: 'Negative edges are never omitted'. solver: certify() is called without truncate_below (certifier.py:544), cap_row omits only beyond ROW_MAX (ppr.py:294-306), certifier.py:589 raises when the limit exceeds tx_cap = 25M. Documented cost, but the outcome (honest certification impossible, set STALE) is wrong.
details_en.fix: Commit a scan bound in the policy (D14 over the last scanMax feedbacks of the pair, same rule in graph.py, rules.ts/edges.ts and audit.ts; a client can already revoke its own feedback, so a window gives it no new power), or a per-tag latest index once the registry offers one; meanwhile let the solver omit expensive positive pairs with sPlus and report negative ones instead of raising.

constats.titre: Lignes à sPlus déclaré : `proveEdge` sous-facture eUp quand une arête positive engagée tombe
constats.resume: Avec un sPlus déclaré, `proveEdge` garde le plancher G = max(GRID, sPlus) : quand une arête positive engagée disparaît (révocation, avis plus récent), la renormalisation du reste de la vraie ligne n'est jamais facturée à eUp. C'est la formule d'ENCODING §7.1 elle-même ; la borne supérieure de PROOFS L6 tombe pour le vrai graphe.
constats.scenario: k = 1, α = 1/3 : ligne déclarée sPlus = 20 000, engagée {P : 10 000, B : 5 000}, C : 5 000 omise ; le client révoque P. Une fois tous les faits prouvés, eUp reste à 0,111 WAD alors que l'écart réel vers le haut vaut 0,333 WAD (MESURÉ, `V1aBound.t.sol`) : distrustUp n'est plus une borne et le test ρ peut passer à tort.
constats.correctif: Calculer le côté positif sur la vraie somme déclarée corrigée des amendements (S = sDecl + Σ(wn⁺ − wc⁺), G = GRID) et ne garder le prépayé que pour la masse omise à son poids d'origine ; mettre à jour ENCODING §7.1 et PROOFS L6.

details_en.summary: For a row with a declared sPlus, proveEdge keeps the positive budget floor at G = max(GRID, sPlus), so when a committed positive edge drops, the renormalisation increase of the rest of the true row (committed and omitted edges) is never billed to eUp, and after every provable fact is proven eUp no longer bounds ||(t*_true - t)^+||_1 (PROOFS L6 fails; the ENCODING §7.1 formula itself is at fault).
details_en.failure_scenario: Honest certificate, k = 1, alpha = 1/3: row u (t_u = 0.2222 WAD) declares sPlus = 20000 and commits {P: 10000, B: 5000}, omitting C: 5000 (B and C rate each other). The row's client then revokes its feedback on P; proveEdge(P) bills eLow only, proveEdge(C) bills 0 (prepaid), and no other proof is possible. eUp stays 0.1111 WAD while the true upward gap is 0.3333 WAD, a shortfall of 0.2222 WAD = 0.5(1-alpha)t_u/alpha, matching the partial report's figure. So distrustUp = d + eEff is no longer an upper bound for targets of B/C's negative edges, and q_cur is understated; the lower (trust) side stays sound.
details_en.evidence: l.1662 `gP = e.sDecl > GRID ? e.sDecl : GRID`, l.1663 `_side(m.sP, ..., gP)`, l.1857-1858 b0 from sDecl, l.1673 prepaid. Scratch test phase2/v1a_work/contracts/test/V1aBound.t.sol::test_declaredRowBoundAfterRevocation PASS: eUp at submission = eUp after all proofs = 111111111111111129, sum (t*_true - t)^+ = 333333333333333332, eLow = 222222222222222222 >= sum (t - t*_true)^+ = 74074074074074074. The solver emits SPLUS whenever it omits positive edges (solver/export.py:201).
details_en.fix: For declared rows, compute the positive side on the declared true sum adjusted by the amendments (S = sDecl + sum(wn+ - wc+), G = GRID) so that a dropped committed edge bills the renormalisation increase of the whole remaining true row to eUp (keep prepaid only for the omitted mass at its original weight), and update ENCODING §7.1 / PROOFS L6 accordingly.

constats.titre: Lignes à sPlus déclaré : une arête positive nouvelle ne facture rien à eLow (côté confiance)
constats.resume: Pendant de K8 côté confiance : sur une ligne à sPlus > S0, une arête positive qui apparaît ou augmente après le certificat donne dec⁺ = 0 (B reste à max(GRID, sPlus)), alors que la vraie somme sPlus + δ dilue toutes les entrées engagées. trustLow reste au-dessus de t* et D36 (eLowEff > eLowMax ⇒ STALE) ne se déclenche jamais.
constats.scenario: Politique de démo (θ 1e15, ρ 1/2, eLowMax 1e16) : la ligne d'ancre engage A→X avec sPlus = 10 200 ; A recommande ensuite Z. `proveEdge(Z)` passe mais eLow reste 0 alors que L6 exige 0,0126 WAD > eLowMax : le set devrait être STALE, `assess(X)` reste OK et trusted (trustLow 0,2179 > t* 0,2137, MESURÉ, `A2.t.sol`). Le watcher classe ces arêtes « OMITTED_POSITIVE » sans effet et ne prouve rien.
constats.correctif: Tarifer le côté positif sur la vraie somme max(GRID, sPlus + (S − S0)) avant et après (corrige aussi K8), et engager la liste (ou le hash) des arêtes omises déclarées pour que la preuve d'une omission déclarée consomme le prépayé sans surfacturer.

details_en.summary: Trust-side mirror of K8: on a row with a declared sPlus > S0, proveEdge prices the positive side with B = max(GRID, sPlus, S_amended), where S_amended excludes the still-omitted declared mass, so a positive edge that appears or grows after the certificate bills dec+ = 0 to eLow although the true row sum sPlus + delta dilutes every committed entry; trustLow stays above t* and D36 (eLowEff > eLowMax => STALE) never fires.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set, default demo policy (theta 1e15, rho 1/2, eLowMax 1e16): the anchor row commits A->X (+1) with sPlus = 10,200 (A->Y +0.02 omitted, declared). After the certificate A endorses Z (+0.02): true row sum 10,400. proveEdge(A row, Z) succeeds but _side(10000, 0, 200, G = 10200) gives B = B' = 10,200, so dec+ = 0 and eLow stays 0, while L6 requires ~0.0126 WAD (> eLowMax: the set should be STALE). assess(X) = OK, trustLow 0.2179 > true t* 0.2137. Variant sPlus = 2*S0, theta 0.1, rho 4/1: X's true t* = 0.074 < theta, isTrusted stays true. eLow is billed only if the declared (honest) omission Y is proven too, which the reference watcher never does: audit() classifies both Y and Z as OMITTED_POSITIVE, provable=False (s_plus + q <= b_plus). The overstatement persists until a replacement certificate is accepted, and the replacement rule gets no eLow credit to accept a less massive honest newcomer early.
details_en.evidence: l.1662 `uint256 gP = e.sDecl > uint256(GRID) ? e.sDecl : uint256(GRID);` then l.1663 `_side(m.sP, _pos(m.wOld), _pos(wNew), gP)` with m.sP = committed + amended sum (l.1853-1865, the declared omitted mass sPlus - S0 is not in it); l.1888-1898 _side: B = max(G, S), B2 = max(G, S2), dec = 0 whenever S2 <= G. ENCODING §3.2 defines sPlus as 'the TRUE positive sum of the full row', so the true sum after the new edge is sPlus + (S2 - S0), not max(sPlus, S2). Re-ran c/test/A2.t.sol::A2Test: 2/2 pass (eLow after the proof 0, eUp 0.01307, trustLow 0.21786 > t* 0.21368, L6 requires 0.012569 > eLowMax; variant trustLow 0.1111 > t* 0.0741 < theta, then proving Y as well bills eLow 0.2222). watcher.py:118-138 (s_plus = committed S+, b_plus = max(GRID, sPlus): both omissions 'OMITTED_POSITIVE', provable=False). PROOFS.md only promises t <= t* 'after every existing discrepancy has been proven', but the proof of the new edge itself is what ENCODING §7.1 says covers dilution. Distinct from K8 (eUp side, dropped committed edge): different trigger (new or grown edge) and consequence (trust lower bound, D36).
details_en.fix: Price the positive side on the true row sum max(GRID, sPlus + (S - S0)) before and after (also fixes K8), and commit the declared omitted edges (list or hash in the row) so a proof of a DECLARED omission consumes the prepaid part without dilution; otherwise honest-omission proofs over-bill eLow and become a griefing lever (see ALT8).

constats.titre: Arrondis prépayé (bas) contre preuves (haut) : des preuves d'omissions honnêtes marquent le titulaire « prouvé »
constats.resume: Le reste prépayé d'une omission déclarée est arrondi vers le bas, chaque preuve vers le haut : prouver les omissions honnêtes d'une ligne à sPlus déclaré facture quelques wei à eUp, `eEff > eSubmitted` rend le titulaire « prouvé », et la garde REFUSED-first refuse ensuite la recertification identique honnête, même après maxAge.
constats.scenario: Ligne X : Y1 engagée, Y2 et Y3 omises sous sPlus = 11 600. Deux `proveEdge` honnêtes facturent 2 wei, `quality().proven` passe à vrai ; la recertification identique revert `NotBetter` à 60 blocs et à 1 001 blocs alors que le set est déjà STALE (MESURÉ, `V5aPrepaid.t.sol`). Un griefer peut répéter sur chaque nouveau certificat.
constats.correctif: Facturer l'omission déclarée une fois par ligne en entiers exacts (cumul du poids réintroduit, ceil au-delà de sPlus − S0), ou ne marquer « prouvé » que si une preuve facture au-delà de la marge déclarée.

details_en.summary: proveEdge bills each proof's ceil'd positive increase (_side) against a floor'd prepaid margin (l.1673), so proving the HONEST omissions that a declared sPlus already covers still bills a few wei to eUp; eEff then exceeds eSubmitted, the incumbent reads as 'proven', and the REFUSED-first guard (l.576) refuses the identical honest recertification, even after maxAge.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set; row X declares sPlus > S0 (the solver does this for every ROW_MAX-capped row; any certifier may also omit positive edges this way): X's true row Y1 +5000, Y2 +3300, Y3 +3300, only Y1 committed, sPlus = 11,600. Anyone proves Y2 then Y3 (honest omissions: wNew = registry weight, nothing is wrong): inc = 2 x ceil(WAD*3300/11600) = 568,965,517,241,379,312 vs prepaid floor = ...310, so 2 wei are billed, eEff goes 252,873,563,218,390,815 -> ...816 and quality().proven = true. With an unchanged graph, the honest certifier's identical recertification at the age refresh reverts NotBetter (at age 60 and at age 1001 when assess already returns STALE), and certifier.replacement_wait raises 'the incumbent was proven wrong' every round: the set stays STALE until the graph changes, and the griefer can repeat on every new certificate (one proof per omitted edge; 44 proofs bill 42 wei on the toy_alias_owner_rowmax row).
details_en.evidence: l.1673 `uint256 prepaid = e.sDecl != 0 ? ((e.sDecl - m.s0) * WAD) / m.b0 : 0;` (floor) vs l.1896-1897 `inc = (up * WAD + den - 1) / den;` (ceil per proof), l.1674 billP = _sat(st.incP + addP, prepaid) - _sat(st.incP, prepaid); l.575-576 `proven = s.eLowEff != 0 || s.eEff > s.eSubmitted; if (proven && vRoot == s.vectorRoot && P.root == s.graphRoot) revert NotBetter(...)` is evaluated before the `age > s.maxAge` acceptance (l.577). Intent violated: comment l.1671-1672 'only the positive increase beyond that prepaid part is billed again'; watcher.py:12/136 classifies these omissions as INFO, provable=False ('proving them would only widen'). Re-ran alt/prepaid_round.py: prepaid 22,772,277,227,722,772, billed 42 wei beyond it, eEff ...260 -> ...263, proven = True. Own end-to-end forge test (phase2/v5a_work/c/test/V5aPrepaid.t.sol, network=monad): baseline identical resubmission without proofs accepted; after the 2 proofs incP = 568,965,517,241,379,312, proven = true, identical resubmission refused at age 60 and at age 1001 (status STALE) with NotBetter. certifier.py:511-512 raises on same_content and oc.proven (read from quality()). The only escape today is K7's non-canonical re-encoding (e.g. W = 4), which the reference certifier does not use and which the K7 fix removes.
details_en.fix: Bill the declared omission once per row from exact integers (accumulate the re-added positive weight, bill ceil(WAD*max(0, sum - (sPlus - S0))/B0) beyond it), or set 'proven' only when a proof bills beyond the declared margin, so honest omissions never mark the incumbent wrong.

constats.titre: `newNodes` ajoutés au nodeCount du moment : un `addNodes` intercalé fait échouer le certificat
constats.resume: `submitCertificate` ajoute `newNodes` à la position courante de la table, alors que les lignes et vecteurs utilisent des indices calculés hors chaîne. Un `addNodes` de tiers (ou un certificat concurrent portant les mêmes nœuds) inclus entre l'estimation et l'exécution décale les indices : `EdgeMismatch` ou `NodeExists`, et Monad facture quand même toute la gas limit.
constats.scenario: Set ouvert, mise à jour de croissance avec un nouvel agent en ligne (cas « small » du certificateur, jusqu'à 100 nœuds) : un griefer paie environ 93 k gas (MESURÉ) pour un `addNodes` intercalé, le certificateur perd sa limite (environ 1,6 MON pour une mise à jour de la taille de la démo, CALCULÉ) et recommence au tour suivant. Deux certificateurs honnêtes du même set produisent le même gaspillage.
constats.correctif: 04-bis : sur un set ouvert, ne jamais porter de nœuds en ligne (addNodes dans sa propre transaction, relire la table, soumettre avec `newNodes` vide). 02-bis : supprimer `newNodes` en ligne sur les sets ouverts ou exiger un indice de départ attendu.

details_en.summary: submitCertificate appends newNodes at whatever nodeCount is at execution (l.503), but its rows and vectors use indices computed off-chain. Any addNodes, or any competing certificate carrying newNodes, included between the certifier's eth_estimateGas and its execution shifts or duplicates the new nodes, and the certificate reverts (EdgeMismatch or NodeExists). On Monad the certifier is still charged its full gas limit. The reference certifier takes this inline path for every growth update of up to 100 new nodes.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set with table [A, X]. The certifier builds a growth update for a new agent Y with newNodes = [Y] at index 2 (certifier.plan 'small case', up to inline_nodes_max = 100 new nodes), runs cast estimate, then cast send. A third party's addNodes(agent 999) (92,788 gas billed, ~0.0095 MON) is included first and moves Y to index 3. The certificate reverts EdgeMismatch(1, 0), because X -> 'node 2' is now agent 999. Appending Y itself first gives NodeExists instead. The certifier pays its gas limit (CLAUDE.md §7: Monad bills the limit): ~1.64 MON for a Registry-verified update of the demo's size (15.0M x 1.075 at 102 gwei, GAS.md). It raises ChainError and retries next round, and the griefer repeats; each griefing node also stays in the table as junk (A1b). The window from estimate to execution is a few blocks. A griefer that posts one addNodes per block after each relevant NewFeedback (the certifier polls every 5 s) lands in it for ~0.03 MON/s, so growth updates of an open set can be blocked repeatedly. No attacker is needed for the waste: two honest certifiers of the same open set (the ERC's Liveness section invites consumers to recertify) carrying the same inline node race, and the second reverts NodeExists and pays its limit.
details_en.evidence: l.503 'if (newNodes.length != 0) _appendNodes(s, setId, newNodes);'; _appendNodes (l.456, l.478) writes at s.nodeCount with no expected start index; l.476 NodeExists. Finder PoC re-run: FinderA5 test_newNodesIndexShift passes, revert data EdgeMismatch(1, 0), griefer 92,788 gas (own measurement 92,812). Own tests in phase2/v5c_work/c/test/V5cA1d.t.sol (3/3): a same-node front-run gives NodeExists; with concurrent honest certifiers the second gets NodeExists; with the certifier's own addNodes first and newNodes = '' at submission, a later third-party append is harmless (existing indices never move). solver/certifier.py: plan() carries newNodes inline when len(appended) <= 100 and unreserved slots <= 800; run_once runs cast estimate then cast send with limit = estimate x 1.075 + 5,000. The large plan is safe: its submit carries no newNodes, and a shift between addNodes chunks makes the estimate fail before the send. Open sets only: _gate (l.400) closes addNodes to third parties when submitters are listed, so the demo is not exposed. Root cause is the permissionless addNodes (AM-R5.7, D23 not implemented), but this race after the certifier's read is undocumented: integration.md:110 only tests 'addNodes d'un tiers : absorbé', i.e. before the read.
details_en.fix: 04-bis: on open sets never carry nodes inline. Append them in their own transaction, re-read the table, then submit with newNodes = '' (a later append cannot move existing indices; one extra tx). 02-bis: drop inline newNodes on open sets, or take an expected start index so the failure is explicit (Monad still bills the limit), and design D23 so that staged nodes keep reserved indices.

constats.titre: Lots `addNodes` de 600 nœuds : au-dessus du plafond de 25 M du certificateur
constats.resume: `add_nodes_per_tx = 600` repose sur le chiffre v0 (29,1 k/nœud) ; en v1, `addNodes` coûte environ 45,9 k/nœud (GAS.md, MESURÉ 01/10) : tout lot de 507 nœuds ou plus dépasse le plafond et `run_once` lève avant le premier envoi, à chaque tour.
constats.scenario: 506 nœuds : limite 24 984 760, passe ; 507 : 25 033 936, refusé ; 600 : 29 620 829 (MESURÉ, forge 06/10). Un premier certificat qui ajoute au moins 507 nœuds (gros set attesté) ne passe jamais avec la politique par défaut ; `simulate.py` masque le défaut en forçant 500.
constats.correctif: Dimensionner les lots sur le coût v1 et le plafond (≤ 450, ou couper en deux un lot trop gros) et dater les commentaires.

details_en.summary: GasPolicy.add_nodes_per_tx = 600 was sized on the v0 figure (29.1 k/node, GAS.md 'Historique R5 (contrat v0, 27/09)'); on the v1 contract addNodes costs ~45.9 k/node, so any addNodes chunk of 507 nodes or more gets a gas limit above the certifier's own tx_cap (25 M) and run_once raises before the first transaction: a certificate appending >= 507 new nodes (typically a first certificate) can never be submitted under the default GasPolicy.
details_en.failure_scenario: Default SetConfig (no 'gas' override; no set config in the repo has one), first certificate appending N >= 507 nodes (e.g. a Submitter-attested set like simulate.py scenario D, 1 237 nodes). plan() takes the large path (N > inline_nodes_max = 100) and emits addNodes chunks of min(600, N) nodes (checked: N = 507 -> first chunk 507, N = 700/1237 -> 600). run_once estimates the first chunk: addNodes(507 agents) = 23 282 731 gas -> GasPolicy.limit = 25 033 936 > 25 000 000; addNodes(600) = 27 549 608 -> 29 620 829; addNodes(506) = 23 236 986 -> 24 984 760 passes (forge, network = monad, scratch V7bGas.t.sol on a byte-identical copy of contracts/src). RuntimeError before any send; certifier.main journals 'error' without advancing frm/first, so the same doomed plan is rebuilt every round and the set never gets a certificate (payers: NO_CERT). simulate.py scenario D hides it by passing GasPolicy(add_nodes_per_tx=500, reserve_slots_per_tx=600) (l.375). Exposure in practice: large Submitter-attested sets; a Registry-verified set of that size already exceeds the cap at submitCertificate (~45.5 k/edge).
details_en.evidence: certifier.py l.62-64: 'tx_cap: int = 25_000_000', 'inline_nodes_max: int = 100      # new nodes carried by submitCertificate itself (29.1 k/node, GAS.md)', 'add_nodes_per_tx: int = 600      # ~17.5 M per full addNodes chunk'; l.425-429 chunking by add_nodes_per_tx; l.587-591 estimate -> limit -> 'if lim > self.cfg.gas.tx_cap: raise RuntimeError' before send. GAS.md (v1, 01/10): '`addNodes` : 22,96 M pour 500 nœuds (≈ 45,9 k par nœud) ... constats.titre: `eth_getLogs` non découpé depuis le bloc 0 : certificateur (`--send`) et watcher inutilisables sur les RPC publics
constats.resume: `Chain.logs` envoie une seule requête (`cast logs` sans `--query-size`) et la table des nœuds se synchronise depuis le bloc 0 : sur `rpc.monad.xyz` et `testnet-rpc.monad.xyz` (100 blocs maximum, CLAUDE.md §7), les deux services échouent dès le premier tour et réessaient la même plage à l'infini, avec un message d'erreur vide (`cast --json` écrit l'erreur sur stdout).
constats.scenario: Réponse `-32614 eth_getLogs is limited to a 100 range` sur les deux RPC publics au-delà de 100 blocs (MESURÉ 06/10) ; en mode sec la table n'est jamais synchronisée, d'où des essais à sec qui semblent sains.
constats.correctif: Découper chaque getLogs en fenêtres de 100 blocs, démarrer la synchronisation au bloc d'enregistrement du set (ou lire `nodeKeyAt`), inclure stdout dans `ChainError`.

details_en.summary: Chain.logs sends one unchunked eth_getLogs (cast logs without --query-size) and both services sync the node table from block 0 (Certifier._table_block = -1, watcher table_block = -1, --from-block not used for it): on both public Monad RPCs (rpc.monad.xyz and testnet-rpc.monad.xyz, capped at 100 blocks) the certifier with --send and the watcher fail on their first round, retry the same range forever, and journal an empty error message.
details_en.failure_scenario: certifier.py --rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz (or https://testnet-rpc.monad.xyz) --send ...: round 1 -> run_once(dry=False) -> table(head) -> chain_table(from_block 0) -> `cast logs --from-block 0 --to-block <head> --json NodesAdded(...) <setId>` -> HTTP 413 {-32614 'eth_getLogs is limited to a 100 range'} (measured 06/10 13:55 UTC on both RPCs; a 100-block range returns []). cast --json exits 1 with the error on STDOUT, Chain._run keeps only stderr, so ChainError('') (reproduced with the real chain_table: message '') and main journals {action: error, error: ''}; frm/first are not advanced, so every round repeats it and no certificate is ever submitted. watcher.py does the same chain_table from 0 (l.295) before any audit, so it never audits or proves; even with the table fixed, its default 30 s interval is ~99 blocks at the measured 0.302 s/block plus processing, and frm is kept on error, so the window only grows.
