The certifier's registry_events loop has the same no-recovery property once one round exceeds ~30 s. Without --send the certifier never syncs the table (dry), which is why dry runs look healthy.
details_en.evidence: certifier.py l.256-260: `self._run("logs", "--address", address, "--from-block", str(from_block), "--to-block", str(to_block), "--json", event_sig, *topics)`; l.532 `self._table_block = -1`; l.536-537 `chain_table(..., self._table_block + 1, head, self._table)`; l.225-226 `raise ChainError(p.stderr.strip()[-2000:])`; l.685-687 frm/first advanced only on success. watcher.py l.285 `table, table_block = None, -1`, l.295, l.302-305. `cast logs --help` (1.8.3): '--query-size <BLOCKS> ... When omitted, the range is queried in a single request.' Probe (phase2/v7b_work/rpc_probe.txt, logs_probe.py): rpc.monad.xyz 0..latest and 201 blocks -> -32614; 100 blocks -> []; testnet-rpc.monad.xyz 0..latest -> -32614. CLAUDE.md §7: '`eth_getLogs` ≤ 100 blocs par appel sur `rpc.monad.xyz`'. docs/chantiers/rapports/04.md AM-04.7 marks it 'noté' and claims the incremental sync limits it 'après le premier passage', but the first pass itself starts at block 0; demo/certify.py bypasses chain_table precisely because 'the public testnet RPC limits eth_getLogs ranges'.
details_en.fix: Chunk every getLogs into <= 100-block windows (cast logs --query-size 100 or a Python loop), start the table sync at the set's registration block or rebuild it from nodeCount/nodeKeyAt, and include stdout in ChainError when cast runs with --json.

constats.titre: Personne n'appelle `checkRegistry` : une mise à jour du registre ne lève jamais REGISTRY_CHANGED
constats.resume: `Upgraded` est un déclencheur « pour REGISTRY_CHANGED », mais aucun composant hors chaîne n'appelle `checkRegistry` et le recalcul identique est sauté : après une mise à jour, le set reste OK sur un certificat vérifié sous l'ancienne implémentation (contre le SHOULD de l'ERC et le MUST du CR). Si un tiers l'appelle, le set est mort jusqu'au rafraîchissement car le drapeau n'est pas un déclencheur.
constats.scenario: L'EOA unique met à jour un proxy vers la v2.1.0 prête en amont : `skip_identical`, `assess` continue de répondre OK ; un opérateur appelle ensuite `checkRegistry` : REGISTRY_CHANGED pour tous les agents, le certificateur ne réagit pas avant environ 22 h (MESURÉ, `no_retrigger.py`).
constats.correctif: Sur `Upgraded`, appeler `checkRegistry` et recertifier ; traiter `oc.registry_changed`, déjà lu à chaque tour, comme un déclencheur.

details_en.summary: Upgraded is a trigger 'for REGISTRY_CHANGED (D17/D28)', but no off-chain component ever calls checkRegistry and run_once skips the identical recomputation, so after a registry upgrade the set is never flagged (fail-open, against the ERC's SHOULD and the CR's MUST); and if anyone else calls checkRegistry after that skip, every assess returns REGISTRY_CHANGED while the certifier, which never reads that flag as a trigger, stays idle until the age refresh.
details_en.failure_scenario: The registry owner EOA upgrades a proxy to an implementation with a new getVersion() (v2.1.0 is ready upstream). registry_events yields 'Upgraded', relevant() returns True, run_once recomputes the unchanged export: roots equal and oc.registry_changed false -> skip_identical. (a) Nobody calls checkRegistry: the stored versionHash stays the old one and assess/isTrusted keep answering OK from a certificate verified under the previous implementation. (b) Some operator follows the ERC and calls checkRegistry(setId) a few blocks later: registryChanged = true, every assess returns REGISTRY_CHANGED and TrustGatedPayer refuses everyone, but RegistryChanged is an AnchoredReputation event the certifier never polls and due_refresh is false, so the set stays dead until an unrelated relevant registry event or about 268,000 blocks after the last certificate (about 22 h); a recomputation would be accepted at once (replacement_wait returns 0 when registry_changed).
details_en.evidence: certifier.py:7 and :390-391 `if k == "Upgraded": return True`; certifier.py:578 `if (gr, vr) == (oc.graph_root, oc.vector_root) and not refresh and not oc.registry_changed: return ...skip_identical`; certifier.py:680 reads OnChain every round but only for due_refresh, never for registry_changed; grep: no checkRegistry call in solver/, indexer/, plugin/, demo/ or contracts/script (only contract tests and docs). AnchoredReputation.sol:1456-1468 checkRegistry is the only writer of registryChanged = true (submitCertificate l.536 clears it, l.530 stores the version at submission); l.1382-1384 assess returns REGISTRY_CHANGED. docs/erc/anchored-reputation.md:499 'Operators SHOULD monitor ... Upgraded events off-chain and call checkRegistry'; docs/conseil/CR-conseil.md:672 'Il faut que le certificateur l'appelle à chaque certification (MUST)'; contracts/test/Upgrade.t.sol:118 'before anyone calls checkRegistry: still OK (documented limit, D17)'. Re-ran scratchpad/a5/no_retrigger.py (upgrade): skip_identical at the Upgraded round (block 1105), checkRegistry at 1305, no run_once and no send through head 2645.
details_en.fix: On an Upgraded event call checkRegistry(setId) and recertify (or force the resubmission, which stores the new versionHash), and treat oc.registry_changed, already read each round at l.680, as a trigger for an immediate recomputation.

constats.titre: Aucun repli quand le certificat honnête dépasse le plafond de gas
constats.resume: `run_once` lève simplement : `compute()` ne tronque ni n'omet rien (le `truncate_below` de `certify` est inutilisé) alors que GAS.md impose au certificateur d'omettre les arêtes coûteuses avec B⁺ déclaré.
constats.scenario: Un agent attaquant avec de la masse gonfle l'historique d'un couple engagé (environ 1 800 avis, environ 49 MON à 102 gwei, CALCULÉ) : la soumission dépasse 25 M à chaque tour, le set ne se recertifie plus.
constats.correctif: Estimer le coût de relecture par couple et, au-delà du plafond, omettre les couples positifs coûteux sous sPlus ou retirer la ligne (marge de troncature) puis recalculer.

details_en.summary: When the honest certificate's submission estimate exceeds the gas cap, run_once just raises: compute() never truncates or omits anything (certify's truncate_below is unused, no 'omit expensive pairs with sPlus' logic), so the client of any provided row can inflate the history of one of its committed pairs until _pairEdge's unbounded re-read pushes every Registry-verified submission over the cap, and the set is never recertified.
details_en.failure_scenario: Registry-verified set, filter vouch/review/slash. Agent X has mass > 0 (one endorsement from any massive row) and its wallet, controlled by the attacker, vouches agent J once (a committed edge X->J), then posts about 1,800 feedbacks on J under a tag outside the filter's endorsement tags (e.g. 'uptime'), never completing the filter. _pairEdge reads the whole pair history at every submission (about 12.9k gas per extra feedback), so the estimate exceeds 23.3M, gas.limit() exceeds tx_cap = 25M, run_once raises 'gas limit > cap' (or cast estimate fails above the 30M tx limit), main retries forever: no recertification, STALE after maxAge, all payments refused. Cost about 1,800 feedbacks x 271k gas, about 49 MON at 102 gwei (AM-02.3 rate: 63 MON for 30M), plus an endorsed agent; an honest automated rater with mass that probes an agent it also endorsed reaches the same state over time. Dropping X's row, or omitting the positive pair X->J under a declared sPlus, removes the re-read (the same test graph without the spam costs 454,725 gas).
details_en.evidence: certifier.py:587-591 `est = self.chain.estimate(...)`; `lim = self.cfg.gas.limit(est)`; `if lim > self.cfg.gas.tx_cap: raise RuntimeError(...)` with no fallback; certifier.py:544 `cert = certify(g, self.cfg.alpha, lambdas=self.cfg.lambdas)` (truncate_below defaults to 0, ppr.py:309/335) and cap_row only omits for ROW_MAX (ppr.py:298); AnchoredReputation.sol:1521-1541 `for (uint256 j = last; j >= 1; --j) {... if (seen == allMask) break; }` (no window since b0aa1ad), called for every committed edge in _verifyRows l.1133. Measured with forge on an unchanged copy of contracts/src (scratchpad phase1/B1/c, B1Scan.t.sol, network = monad): submitCertificate 454,725 gas with 0 extra feedbacks, 1,731,875 with 100, 5,595,325 with 400 (12.85k each). contracts/GAS.md:76 (~13k per extra feedback) and :89 'le certificateur doit omettre ces arêtes et déclarer B⁺ ... ou passer au niveau Submitter-attested': the documented mitigation is not implemented; ENCODING.md:119 allows omitting expensive positive pairs with sPlus.
details_en.fix: Before planning, estimate each committed pair's re-read cost from the pair's feedback count (the watcher already counts history per pair), and when the estimate exceeds the cap, omit expensive positive pairs under a declared sPlus or drop the row (truncation margin) and recompute, instead of raising.

constats.titre: Les boucles « never die » meurent sur une seule erreur passagère
constats.resume: `certifier.main` appelle `chain.block_number()` hors du try ; `watcher.main` aussi, et relit l'export hors du try alors que `from_indexer.export` réécrit les fichiers sur place. `watcher --once` ne rend jamais la main après un tour en échec.
constats.scenario: Un 429 sur `cast block-number` arrête le processus ; une lecture d'export à moitié écrit lève `JSONDecodeError` (1 216 lectures déchirées sur 1 457 pendant une réécriture continue, MESURÉ). Pas de superviseur dans le dépôt ; la démo n'est pas touchée, le surveillant prévu pendant le jugement si.
constats.correctif: Tout mettre dans le try, écrire l'export en fichier temporaire + `os.replace`, et faire rendre un code non nul à `--once`.

details_en.summary: The two long-running service loops are documented as surviving errors ('journal, keep the window, retry next round' / 'never die'), but each does work outside its try that can raise. certifier.main calls chain.block_number() outside the try (certifier.py:676). watcher.main does the same (watcher.py:293) and also re-reads the export files outside the try (watcher.py:287-292). So one transient RPC failure, or one torn export file (from_indexer.export rewrites in place with Path.write_text), ends the process. Separately, watcher.main --once never returns when a round fails: the except branch `continue`s past the `if a.once: return 0`.
details_en.failure_scenario: During the unattended judging window (ROADMAP.md:162, MUSTDO item 16), `cast block-number` returns a 429 or a timeout once. ChainError escapes certifier.main or watcher.main and the process exits: no more recertification or proofs, and after maxAge the set is STALE, so every payer refuses. If from_indexer.py refreshes the export directory while the watcher reloads it, json.load sees a truncated onchain_feedbacks.json, JSONDecodeError escapes and the watcher exits. A refresh that lands between the feedbacks write and the identity write also mixes new feedbacks with the old identity for one round. `watcher.py --once` on an RPC that rejects the getLogs range never terminates, whereas certifier.py --once returns 0 after journaling.
details_en.evidence: certifier.py:675-687 `while True: head = chain.block_number()` comes before `try:`, and the except comment reads '# journal, keep the window, retry next round'. watcher.py:286-305: the loads at 288-292 and `head = chain.block_number()` at 293 come before `try:`; the except at 302 reads '# never die: journal and retry the same window next round' and is followed by `time.sleep(a.interval); continue`, while `if a.once: return 0` sits at 307 after the try. from_indexer.py:179-181 writes the three files with `.write_text(json.dumps(...))` (truncate, then write, no tmp + os.replace), unlike State.save (certifier.py:486-489, 'atomic'). PoC v7c_work/dies/poc.py (real main() loops, chain patched): '(a) certifier.main died on round 2: ChainError ... 429', '(b) watcher.main died: JSONDecodeError', '(c) watcher.main --once still looping after 5 rounds', '(d) 1.23 MB file, 1455 rewrites in 3 s: 241 good reads, 1216 torn reads (JSONDecodeError)'. No supervisor or restart wrapper exists in the repo (grep for systemd/restart/nohup). demo/certify.py calls run_once once per scene, so the demo is not affected.
details_en.fix: Move the block_number call and the data reloads inside the try (on failure, journal and sleep), have from_indexer.export write each file to a tmp file and os.replace it (ideally one versioned directory per block, swapped atomically), and make watcher --once return a non-zero code after a failed round.

constats.titre: Export `--data` en retard sur les events : l'event est consommé par un recalcul obsolète
constats.resume: Le bloc de l'export (`identity.json`, feedbacks) n'est jamais comparé à celui des events : sur un export en retard, le recalcul reproduit le titulaire (`skip_identical`), `frm` avance, et le rattrapage de l'export ne déclenche plus rien.
constats.scenario: Révocation vue par le RPC au bloc E, export indexeur à E − 50 : `skip_identical`, puis plus rien jusqu'au rafraîchissement (environ 22 h) ; le watcher ne prouve pas non plus (audit unique).
constats.correctif: Ne consommer les events que jusqu'au bloc de l'export (garder la fenêtre tant qu'il est en retard), ou exporter à la tête avant de recalculer.

details_en.summary: main() re-reads the --data export when a relevant event arrives but never checks that the export's block covers that event; on a lagging export the recomputation reproduces the incumbent, run_once logs skip_identical, frm advances past the event, and the export catching up later triggers nothing.
details_en.failure_scenario: The certifier sees, through the RPC, a relevant NewFeedback (an anchor's new vouch or slash, or a revocation) at block E, while the from_indexer.py export in --data was taken at a block < E (Envio lag, or the periodic export has not run yet: nothing in the repo refreshes it in step with the certifier). load() returns the old graph, the roots equal the incumbent's, run_once returns skip_identical and main sets frm = head + 1. When the export later includes E, no new event and no due refresh fire, so the change stays uncertified until the next relevant event or about 268,000 blocks (about 22 h). If the old export differs from the incumbent for another reason, the certificate is submitted without E's effect, with the same outcome for E.
details_en.evidence: certifier.py:672-673 `load = lambda: (load_feedbacks_onchain(Path(a.data) / ...), load_identity_json(Path(a.data) / ...))`; certifier.py:681-685 run_once on `first or evs or due`, then `frm, first = head + 1, False`; Identity.block (graph.py:109, filled from identity.json 'block' by load_identity_json l.276) and the feedbacks file's 'block' are never compared with the events' blocks anywhere in certifier.py; from_indexer.py:168-175 exports at an explicit --block and refuses only a block above the indexer head. Re-ran scratchpad/a5/stale_data.py: event at block 1030 seen with the export not yet refreshed -> 'skip_identical' with reason '1 relevant event(s)' at block 1065, then no further run_once up to head 2245.
details_en.fix: Compare the export's block with the highest triggering event block and, while it is behind, keep the window (do not advance frm) and retry, or have the certifier export from the indexer itself at the RPC head before recomputing.

constats.titre: Soumission différée par la règle de remplacement : jamais retentée
constats.resume: Quand `replacement_wait > 0`, `run_once` journalise et rend la main, `main` consomme la fenêtre d'events et rien ne reprogramme la tentative.
constats.scenario: Une ancre révoque une recommandation moins de 600 blocs après le dernier certificat : attente de 516 blocs journalisée (MESURÉ), puis plus aucun recalcul avant un autre event pertinent ou le rafraîchissement (environ 22 h) : la recommandation révoquée reste certifiée.
constats.correctif: Garder un recalcul en attente et le relancer à `block + waitBlocks`.

details_en.summary: A submission deferred by the replacement rule (replacement_wait > 0) is journaled and dropped: run_once returns normally, main sets frm = head + 1 past the triggering events, and nothing schedules a retry when the wait expires, so the change waits for an unrelated relevant event or the age refresh (about 22 h) instead of minRefresh.
details_en.failure_scenario: Defaults maxAge 288000, refreshLead 20000, minRefresh 600. Certificate C1 at block B. Within 600 blocks an anchor revokes its vouch of agent X, or endorses an agent whose mass is absorbed (mass 0.7407 -> 0.7202 WAD in the PoC graph): the honest C2 has less mass, so replacement_wait returns minRefresh + 1 - age (516 blocks in the PoC) and run_once journals 'deferred_replacement_rule'. main then consumes the window; the next run_once comes only with another relevant registry event or when head - B > 268000. In a quiet registry the revoked endorsement stays certified (isTrusted(X) true) for about 22 h, although the refresh window would have accepted C2 after 600 blocks. Bursts of feedback (the demo's scenes, a farm) hit this routinely.
details_en.evidence: certifier.py:580-583 `wait = replacement_wait(...)`; `if wait: return self.journal.log(action="deferred_replacement_rule", waitBlocks=wait, ...)` (waitBlocks is never read back); certifier.py:681-685 `if first or evs or due: ... svc.run_once(...)` then `frm, first = head + 1, False` unconditionally; certifier.py:515-521: a mass decrease fails the fast path, so the wait is min(max_age + 1 - age, min_refresh + 1 - age) when q_new <= q_cur + slack_refresh. Re-ran scratchpad/a5/defer_drop.py (main driven by a fake chain, export already containing the new feedback): 'deferred_replacement_rule' at block 1065 with waitBlocks 516 and massCur 740740740740740739 vs mass 720164609053497941, then no run_once and no send up to head 2245 (age 1245 > minRefresh). The module docstring (step 6) says the rule is checked before any transaction to avoid paying for a doomed plan, not to drop the update.
details_en.fix: Keep a pending recompute when run_once returns deferred_replacement_rule (or any non-certified outcome) and re-run it when head >= block + waitBlocks, instead of treating the events as consumed.

constats.titre: Watcher : une arête négative surévaluée (w < q < 0) n'est jamais signalée
constats.resume: La classification n'a que INFLATED, SIGN_FLIP et DEFLATED : un slash engagé trop négatif gonfle B⁻ et divise la méfiance des arêtes négatives voisines, alors que `proveEdge` l'accepte et facture à eUp ; l'audit de l'indexeur, lui, le signale.
constats.scenario: Registre : #2 à −10 000, #3 à −100 ; engagé : #3 à −10 000 : d(#2) passe de 0,110 à 0,056 WAD (MESURÉ, `wA/t3`), `audit()` rend [] et #2 peut passer le test ρ.
constats.correctif: Ajouter le cas `w < q < 0` (OVERSTATED_NEG) prouvé par `proveEdge`.

details_en.summary: audit() has no case for an overstated negative edge (committed w < registry q < 0): the chain INFLATED (w > q) / SIGN_FLIP (q > 0 > w) / DEFLATED (0 < w < q) never matches it (q == 0 is never an edge), so a too-negative committed slash, which inflates the row's B- and deflates the distrust of every sibling negative edge, is silently accepted although proveEdge accepts it (wNew != wOld) and bills incN to eUp.
details_en.failure_scenario: Anchor A slashes #2 at -10000 and #3 at -100 in the registry; the committed anchor row carries #3 at -10000 (a listed submitter of an attested set, or A softened its slash after the certificate). B- goes 10100 -> 20000 and d(#2) drops 0.110 -> 0.0556 WAD (agent-row variant: 0.0733 -> 0.0370); watcher.audit returns [] so nothing is proven, distrustUp(#2) = d + eEff is no longer an upper bound and #2 can pass rho*distrustUp <= trustLow. proveEdge(agentJ = #3) would bill _side(20000, 10000, 100, GRID) inc = 0.49 WAD to eUp. The indexer mirror (audit.ts:124-125) reports the same row as INFLATED(#2) + OVERSTATED_NEG(#3): the two audits diverge.
details_en.evidence: watcher.py:117-127 (`if pe is None` / `elif w > pe.q` / `elif pe.q > 0 > w` / `elif 0 < w < pe.q`); graph.py:13 'q == 0 => no edge'. Re-ran scratchpad/wA/t3_neg_deflation.py ('d(#2) = 110011001100110012' -> '55555555555555556', 'discrepancies: []') and t5_neg_deflation_agent.py ('73340667400073341' -> '37037037037037037', 'watcher discrepancies: []'). Contract: proveEdge l.1659 only refuses wNew == wOld; l.1664 bills the negative side through _side. On Registry-verified sets the re-read forbids it at submission, so it needs a post-submission softening (also hit by ONCE) or an attested submitter.
details_en.fix: Add a case `elif w < pe.q < 0` (OVERSTATED_NEG, provable when the row's committed S- exceeds GRID or always) proven with proveEdge(agentJ) and ordered with the distrust proofs.

constats.titre: Watcher : `still_dilutes` compare au B⁺ engagé, pas au budget courant du contrat
constats.resume: Après une preuve INFLATED avec 0 < q < w, la somme amendée passe sous B0 et une omission que le contrat facturerait encore est sautée : eLow reste sous la surestimation réelle et trustLow peut dépasser la vraie confiance.
constats.scenario: Ligne engagée #2 +10 000 (gonflé), #3 +5 000, #4 omis : après la seule preuve INFLATED, trustLow(#2) = 0,0519 > vraie confiance 0,0476 (MESURÉ au point fixe exact, `a6/w6_cycle.py`) ; prouver aussi l'omission couvrirait l'écart. L'objection de C1 est réfutée par ce calcul.
constats.correctif: Reproduire `_side` : prouver dès que dec > 0 avec B = max(max(GRID, sPlus), S_amendée).

details_en.summary: still_dilutes compares the amended positive sum with proof['rowBPlus'] = max(GRID, sPlus or committed S0) (the committed B0, since decode_rows returns splus[u] = S0 when no sPlus is declared), whereas the contract renormalises with B = max(max(GRID, sDecl), S_amended) (_side): after an INFLATED proof with 0 < q < w lowers S+ below B0, an omission the contract would still bill is skipped and eLow stays below the true overstatement, so trustLow can exceed the true trust after the watcher is done.
details_en.failure_scenario: Registry: A -> #1; W1 (source of #1) vouches #2 +5000, #3 +5000, #4 +4000; #2 <-> #5 vouch each other. Committed row of #1 (no sPlus): #2 +10000 (inflated), #3 +5000, #4 omitted (S0 = B0 = 15000), e.g. by a listed submitter of an attested set. audit -> [INFLATED #2, DILUTION #4]; the watcher proves INFLATED (contract dec = 0.1667, eLow_A = 0.0741 WAD), then still_dilutes: 10000 + 4000 > 15000 false -> 'skipped', although the contract would bill _side(10000,0,4000,GRID) dec = 0.2857. Exact fixed point of the true graph (column A): t(#2) - t*(#2) = 0.0826 > eLow_A alone (sum of excesses 0.1376), so trustLow(#2) = 0.0519 > true trust 0.0476 (lambda 1/2 each, 2 anchors). Proving the omission too gives eLow_A = 0.201 (sound). C1's objection ('only skips where the contract would over-bill') is wrong: the INFLATED step bills w/B0 - q/B2 with B2 = 10000 < B_true = 14000, so the true decrease 0.310 is only covered with the omission's 0.286.
details_en.evidence: watcher.py:105 b_plus = max(GRID, splus[u]); export.py:402 `splus[u] = sp if sp is not None else committed`; watcher.py:176 `... > d.proof["rowBPlus"]`; contract _side l.1888-1890 B = max(G, S) with G = max(GRID, sDecl) (l.1662), S = current amended sum from _sums. Re-ran scratchpad/a6/w6_cycle.py: 'watcher SKIPS DILUTION 4; contract would bill: (0.2857...)', 'sum (t - t*_true)+ = 0.1376 WAD; eLow_A = 0.0741 -> UNSOUND', 'eLow_A if the omission were also proven: 0.2011'; per-node figures recomputed by hand. PROOFS.md L6 only bounds the AMENDED graph, so a skipped provable fact leaves the true graph uncovered. Trigger needs an INFLATED (w > q > 0) at audit time: a listed submitter (attested set) or a feedback lowered before the audit round.
details_en.fix: Mirror _side in still_dilutes: prove iff the omission's B' = max(G, S_amended + q) exceeds B = max(G, S_amended) with G = max(GRID, declared sPlus) (i.e. S_amended + q > G), or simply compute _side's dec and prove when dec > 0.

constats.titre: Watcher : une erreur RPC passagère est classée « undecodable » pour toujours
constats.resume: Le `except Exception` autour de `decode_submission` (et de `prove`) ne distingue pas une erreur de transport d'un input vraiment indécodable : le tour se termine normalement et `frm` avance.
constats.scenario: Délai dépassé ou 5xx sur `cast tx` au tour qui voit un certificat diluant : « undecodable », fenêtre avancée, certificat jamais audité (MESURÉ, fausse chaîne).
constats.correctif: Laisser remonter les `ChainError` de transport pour garder la fenêtre ; réserver « undecodable » à un échec de décodage d'un input récupéré.

details_en.summary: The broad `except Exception` around decode_submission (and the one around prove at l.232) cannot tell a transient RPC failure from a truly undecodable transaction: a failed `cast tx <hash> input` (timeout, 5xx, connection reset, rate limit after cast's own retries) is journaled as a final 'undecodable' (or the row's first proof as 'error' followed by break), watch_once returns normally and main advances frm = head + 1, so that certificate is never audited (or that row never proven) again.
details_en.failure_scenario: A diluting or omitted-negative certificate lands; in the round that first sees its CertificateSubmitted log, Chain.tx_input -> cast exits non-zero (ChainError, e.g. '429 Too Many Requests' or a timeout on the 25-rps public RPC). watch_once journals {'action': 'undecodable'} and continues; main sets frm = head + 1 (l.306) and, as the audit is never repeated (ONCE), no proveEdge is ever sent while that certificate stays current. Re-run of phase1/D2work/w_swallow.py (fake chain): events = [('undecodable', '... error code 429 ...')], watch_once returns normally.
details_en.evidence: watcher.py:211-215 `try: sub = decode_submission(...) except Exception as e: ... 'undecodable' ... continue`; l.230-237 same pattern for prove then break; certifier.py:223-226 Chain._run raises ChainError on any non-zero cast exit, with no retry; watcher.py:302-306 only an exception escaping watch_once keeps the window. cast 1.8.3 has a rate-limit backoff, so a 429 is often absorbed, but timeouts and other transport errors still surface.
details_en.fix: Let ChainError (transport/RPC failures) propagate out of watch_once (or return a 'retry' marker) so main keeps the window, and reserve 'undecodable' for a decode failure of an input actually fetched; retry a transiently failed estimate instead of breaking the row.

constats.titre: Watcher : la boucle de preuves d'une ligne s'arrête au premier échec
constats.resume: Un `NothingToProve` sur un faux positif (export en retard) arrête la ligne, alors qu'une preuve en échec ne change ni l'état on-chain ni les amendements : les vraies dilutions qui suivent sont abandonnées pour de bon.
constats.scenario: FABRICATED périmé (arête créée après l'export) trié avant une vraie DILUTION : `proofs = [FABRICATED error NothingToProve]`, la dilution n'est jamais envoyée (MESURÉ, mock).
constats.correctif: Sur un revert qui laisse la ligne inchangée, journaliser et continuer ; ne s'arrêter que sur BadProof(5)/(23) ou une transaction envoyée en échec.

details_en.summary: The per-row proof loop breaks on ANY failed proof (`if r.get("status") is not True ...: break`), including an estimate that reverts NothingToProve because the live registry does not confirm a discrepancy seen in a lagging export; a reverted proof leaves the row's on-chain state and the local amendment list unchanged, so the row's later, real discrepancies (sorted after it) were still provable but are dropped and, the certificate being audited once, never retried.
details_en.failure_scenario: Watcher run without --data (the frozen versioned snapshot of run_mainnet.load_mainnet) or with an export older than the certificate: a committed edge (client -> #7) created after the snapshot looks FABRICATED; the same row also has a real DILUTION (#8). Sorted by PRIORITY, the FABRICATED estimate reverts NothingToProve() -> 'error' -> break; the DILUTION is never estimated nor sent (mock re-run: proofs = [('FABRICATED', 'error', 'NothingToProve()')], sent = []), frm advances and the dilution stays unbilled. A stale OMITTED_NEGATIVE (priority 0, e.g. a slash revoked after the export) blocks every fabrication proof of its row the same way.
details_en.evidence: watcher.py:230-237 (`except Exception` -> status 'error'; `if r.get("status") is not True or d.kind == "SOURCE": break`), l.238 amend() only after a success, so the amends are still valid after a failure. Contract proveEdge l.1659 `if (wNew == m.wOld) revert NothingToProve();` reverts without touching RowState. watcher.py:290-292 default data = R.load_mainnet() (frozen snapshot). Re-ran scratchpad/a6/break_on_false_positive.py (mock chain): 'sent agentJ: [] -> the real DILUTION (agentJ 8) was never attempted'.
details_en.fix: On a revert that leaves the row unchanged (NothingToProve, or any estimate failure before sending) journal it and `continue` with the same amends; break only on BadProof(5)/(23), a sent-but-failed transaction, or SOURCE.

constats.titre: Watcher : chaque certificat n'est audité qu'une fois
constats.resume: La boucle n'audite que les certificats dont l'event tombe dans la fenêtre du tour : révocations, avis adoucis, changements de contrôleur ou de wallet après la soumission ne sont jamais prouvés, et aucun code hors chaîne ne construit `proveTransfer`.
constats.scenario: Certificat honnête audité propre, puis le client d'une ligne révoque une recommandation : aucune preuve, eLow jamais crédité, le certificat honnête plus léger attend la fenêtre (600 blocs par défaut, jusqu'à maxAge si minRefresh = maxAge) pendant que les payeurs honorent l'arête révoquée.
constats.correctif: Réauditer à chaque tour le certificat COURANT contre des données fraîches (amendements reconstruits) et ajouter `proveTransfer` pour les sets non stricts.

details_en.summary: The production loop audits a certificate only in the round whose (frm, head] window contains its CertificateSubmitted log (watch_once audits only those logs, then main sets frm = head + 1), so every fact that appears later on the still-current certificate (revocation, softened or new feedback, a client becoming a controller, an agentWallet cleared by a transfer) is never detected nor proven; no off-chain code builds proveTransfer at all.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set (default SetConfig), honest certificate C at block b, audited clean at b+1. At b+500 the client of #1's row revokes its +10000 vouch of #2 (or #1 is sold, clearing its agentWallet). Every later watch_once finds no CertificateSubmitted log in (frm, head] and returns []: no proveEdge (ii)/(iii) or proveWallet (iv) is ever sent, eLow is never credited, so the honest certifier's lower-mass newcomer gets NotBetter and waits for the refresh window (600 blocks by default, up to maxAge = 288 000 blocks if minRefresh = maxAge, the censorship-resistant setting), while isTrusted/TrustGatedPayer keep honouring the revoked edge. replacement_wait's documented remedy ('prove the incumbent's overstatement first (watcher)') never happens. For a strictTransfer = false set, no component ever calls proveTransfer.
details_en.evidence: watcher.py:203 `logs = chain.logs(contract, C.CERT_SUBMITTED, from_block, ...)`, l.206-216 audits only those logs; l.306 `frm = head + 1`; main docstring 'audit each new certificate'. certifier.py:508 'A wait of maxAge means: prove the incumbent's overstatement first (watcher), or wait.' PROOFS.md table: 'Changement après la soumission: prouvable (proveEdge, proveWallet, proveTransfer)' and 't <= t* n'est garanti qu'après que tout écart existant a été prouvé'. simulate.py:192/284 only works because it re-passes the submission block as from_block. `grep -rn proveTransfer solver plugin/src indexer/src indexer/scripts` (tests excluded): no match. Default strict_transfer = True limits the proveTransfer part to non-strict sets.
details_en.fix: Make the loop state-driven: each round re-audit the CURRENT certificate (graphRoot from OnChain.read) against fresh registry data, rebuilding amendments from rowStateOf/EdgeProven, and add proveTransfer for certified agents whose ownerOf no longer matches ownerFp on non-strict sets.

constats.titre: Nouveaux handlers : un `addNodes` relayé laisse un trou définitif dans la table de l'indexeur
constats.resume: `ancre.ts`/`calls.ts` ne font confiance qu'à l'input externe (tx.to = contrat) : un `addNodes` (ouvert à tous sur un set ouvert) ou un `submitCertificate` avec `newNodes` envoyé via un contrat laisse `nodesComplete = false` à jamais, donc tout certificat suivant qui couvre le trou est NODES_MISSING et n'est jamais audité ; un set enregistré via un Safe reste UNKNOWN_SET.
constats.scenario: Un `Multicall3.aggregate([addNodes(setId, …)])` (quelques centimes) aveugle pour de bon l'audit en direct du set (test sur le code actuel : [[4, NODES_MISSING], [5, NODES_MISSING]]) ; le même appel arrête aussi le certificateur (TBL).
constats.correctif: Combler les trous par `nodeKeyAt(setId, i)` via un Effect Envio (clés immuables) et accepter les paramètres de set de toute source quand `computeSetId(params) == setId`.

details_en.summary: The new handlers only trust the OUTER transaction input (tx.to must be the contract); an addNodes (permissionless on open sets) or a submitCertificate with newNodes sent through any contract leaves a permanent hole in the indexer's node table (no SetNode rows, nodesComplete false, never repaired), so every later certificate of that set whose nCert covers the hole is NODES_MISSING and never audited; a set registered through a Safe/forwarder has no schema and all its certificates are UNKNOWN_SET forever.
details_en.failure_scenario: Anyone sends one Multicall3.aggregate([addNodes(setId, 0x01||anyAgentId)]) to an open set (~one node, cents). NodesAdded's tx.to is Multicall3, isDirect is false, ancre.ts:76-78 sets nodesComplete = false and returns without SetNode rows; nothing ever writes those indices again (nodes are immutable, NodeExists), and nCert is non-decreasing over an append-only table, so from the first later certificate that certifies any node appended after the junk one (the next one for a growing set) every CertificateSubmitted gets status NODES_MISSING and SetHealth stays UNAUDITED: the live audit (D42, README 'every CertificateSubmitted gets ... its Discrepancy findings') is blinded for that set for good, including for later faulty third-party certificates. Scratch test on the current handlers: forwarded addNodes, then two direct certificates (nCert 4 and 5) -> [[4,NODES_MISSING],[5,NODES_MISSING]], nodesComplete false, SetNode indices [0,1,4]. A single certificate relayed by a smart account with newNodes has the same permanent effect; registerAnchorSet via a Safe -> decodable false, every certificate UNKNOWN_SET (tags are only stored as hashes on chain, AnchoredReputation.sol:307). The same forwarded addNodes also stops the certifier (certifier.py chain_table raises on it, candidate TBL).
details_en.evidence: calls.ts:1-3 'Only DIRECT calls are decodable ... the caller gets undefined (UNDECODABLE)'; ancre.ts:37 isDirect = tx.to == contract; :71-79 `if (isDirect(...)) nodes = decodeAppendedNodes(...)` ... `if (!nodes || nodes.length !== count) { context.AnchorSet.set({ ...set, nodeCount, nodesComplete: false }); return; }`; :85 later appends keep nodesComplete false; :114-117 `if (![...Array(nCert).keys()].every((i) => nodes[i] !== undefined)) status = "NODES_MISSING"`; :45-53 relayed registration -> tagsJson undefined -> :112 UNKNOWN_SET. Contract: AnchoredReputation.sol:404-410 addNodes 'Open sets: permissionless' (`_gate` only checks listed submitters); :476 NodeExists (a node is never re-added); :506 `if (n < s.nCert || n > s.nodeCount ...) revert BadNCert()` (nCert non-decreasing); nodeKeyAt (l.436-441) exposes the immutable keys. schema.graphql:147 documents 'later certificates NODES_MISSING' but not that any third party can trigger it permanently. Scratch tests phase2/v9_work/ix/test/v9.test.ts ('OUTERCALL', 'OUTERCALL-reg') pass on a copy of the current indexer.
details_en.fix: Fill node-table holes from the contract (nodeKeyAt(setId, i) through an Envio Effect: keys never change once appended, so any block works) instead of giving up, and accept set params from any source when computeSetId(params) == setId.

constats.titre: `register()` émet le wallet après le callback ERC-721 : l'indexeur garde un wallet que le registre n'a plus
constats.resume: Le registre v2.0.0 écrit agentWallet avant `_safeMint` mais émet `MetadataSet(agentWallet)` après `onERC721Received` : un changement de wallet fait dans le callback (unset, set, transfert) est écrasé dans l'indexeur (et dans le rejeu de graph.py) par l'event d'enregistrement.
constats.scenario: Confirmé sur un fork du registre réel du testnet : `getAgentWallet` = 0, indexeur = C. Dès que l'agent a de la masse, chaque `submitCertificate` Registry-verified revert `EdgeMismatch(row, 256)` (AnchoredReputation.sol:1153) : set STALE au gré de l'attaquant.
constats.correctif: Ignorer le `MetadataSet` qui suit `Registered` dans la même transaction si un event de wallet ou de transfert du même agent est intervenu après le mint ; même règle dans `graph.py`.

details_en.summary: agentWallet is rebuilt from MetadataSet events in log order, but the deployed ERC-8004 v2.0.0 register() writes agentWallet = msg.sender before _safeMint and emits MetadataSet(msg.sender) only after the onERC721Received callback, so a wallet change made inside the callback (unsetAgentWallet, setAgentWallet, transferFrom) is overwritten in the indexer (and in graph.py's identity replay) by the stale registration event.
details_en.failure_scenario: Contract C calls register() and, in onERC721Received, calls unsetAgentWallet(j) (or transferFrom(C, D, j), or setAgentWallet(j, W2, ...)). Logs: Transfer(0,C), MetadataSet(''), [Transfer(C,D)], Registered, MetadataSet(C). On chain getAgentWallet(j) = 0 (or W2); identity.ts sets Agent.wallet = C. Once j has mass in a Registry-verified set (one endorsement by a trusted node), the solver commits j's row with SRC = C and every submitCertificate reverts EdgeMismatch(row, 256) at AnchoredReputation.sol:1153 until the attacker (or any later wallet event) changes the wallet: the set's certificates age to STALE. Variants: with W2 set in the callback, W2's endorsement of its own agent j is kept by rules.ts/graph.py but refused by the contract (AnchoredReputation.sol:1130, EdgeMismatch); with the transfer variant, C's feedback on j is wrongly rejected as CONTROLLER_WALLET (an omitted negative provable against the honest certifier). The indexer audit uses the same wrong wallet, so it reports nothing for the solver's rows and SOURCE_MISSING for a correct third-party row.
details_en.evidence: Upstream v2.0.0 IdentityRegistryUpgradeable.sol:60-66: `$._metadata[agentId]["agentWallet"] = abi.encodePacked(msg.sender); _safeMint(msg.sender, agentId); emit Registered(...); emit MetadataSet(agentId, "agentWallet", ..., abi.encodePacked(msg.sender));` (same in both other register overloads, l.69-86). Re-ran the C2 PoC on a fork of the LIVE testnet registry at the latest block (phase2/v9_work/reg, forge test -vv, getVersion 2.0.0): unset-in-callback -> logs MetadataSet(0x) then MetadataSet(C), `event replay wallet: C`, `getAgentWallet: 0x0`; transfer-in-callback -> owner 0xbEEF, getAgentWallet 0x0, replay wallet C. Current identity.ts:45-51 applies every MetadataSet(agentWallet) in order (`const wallet = v.length === 42 ? lc(v) : ZERO; ... context.Agent.set({ ...agent, wallet })`), no special case for the registration event. Contract re-read: AnchoredReputation.sol:1152-1153 `if (reads && identity.getAgentWallet(key & ID_MASK) != wallet) revert EdgeMismatch(ri, ROW_MAX);`.
details_en.fix: Treat the MetadataSet that follows Registered in the registration transaction as a no-op when a wallet-changing event (MetadataSet or Transfer) of the same agent occurred earlier in that transaction after the mint (keep the in-callback state); same rule in solver/graph.py replay_identity_events.

constats.titre: Audit en direct : une dilution est signalée sur la mauvaise arête, et la vraie preuve ne ferme rien
constats.resume: `audit.ts:124` classe INFLATED, avec la preuve `proveEdge`, les arêtes SŒURS dont la part monte quand une arête positive est omise, alors que `proveEdge` sur elles revert `NothingToProve` (poids engagé = poids du registre) ; l'arête omise, seule prouvable (que `watcher.py` signale), n'apparaît jamais. `remedy()` (`ancre.ts:164-165`) ne ferme un écart que sur le couple prouvé : le vrai `EdgeProven(u, X)` ne ferme rien et SetHealth reste DISCREPANCY jusqu'au certificat suivant.
constats.scenario: Set ouvert : W1 recommande #2 et #3 ; le certificat n'engage que l'arête vers #2. L'audit donne [INFLATED, u 2, agent 2, proveEdge] ; `proveEdge(2, #2)` revert, la preuve utile `proveEdge(2, #3)` passe mais l'écart reste ouvert (test sur le code actuel). Le vecteur normatif `violations/dilution.json` est attendu ainsi par `ancre.real.test.ts:75`. Même racine : sur une ligne SOURCE/UNKNOWN_AGENT, les écarts d'arête sont étiquetés `proveEdge` qui revert `BadProof(25)`.
constats.correctif: Signaler la dilution sur l'arête omise ou dégonflée (DILUTION/DEFLATED, comme le watcher) avec la bonne preuve, et faire fermer par `remedy()` les écarts d'une ligne quand un `EdgeProven` de cette ligne corrige la dilution.

details_en.summary: Dilution (an omitted or deflated positive edge X that raises the share of the row's other edges) is filed as INFLATED on the SIBLING edges Y with proof 'proveEdge', although proveEdge(u, Y) reverts NothingToProve (committed w == registry w); the edge X that is actually provable (and that solver/watcher.py reports as DILUTION/DEFLATED) is never reported, and remedy() (handlers/ancre.ts:164-165) closes findings only by (node, agentId) of the proven edge, so the real proof EdgeProven(u, X) closes nothing and SetHealth stays DISCREPANCY until the next certificate.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open (Registry-verified) set, registry: W1 (wallet of #1) vouches #2 = 100 and #3 = 100. A certificate commits row u=2 (#1, src W1) with only the edge to #2 (re-read OK at submission, B+ = 10 000 instead of 20 000). The audit files [INFLATED, u 2, agentId '2', wCommitted 10000, wRegistry 10000, proof proveEdge]; a watcher following it calls proveEdge(u=2, agentJ=2) -> NothingToProve. The watcher's real proof proveEdge(u=2, agentJ=3) lands (EdgeProven node 2, agentId 3, eLow widened) but remedy() matches no finding: SetHealth stays [DISCREPANCY, openDiscrepancies 1] (scratch test). In a Registry-verified set every INFLATED finding with wCommitted == wRegistry is of this kind, i.e. the main case the live audit exists for (audit.ts:21-22, AM-5.11). Related mislabel (same root: proofOf labels each finding by its kind only, ancre.ts:19-25): on a row that also carries a SOURCE or UNKNOWN_AGENT finding, every edge finding is labelled proveEdge although proveEdge reverts BadProof(25) '-> proveWallet' there (_rowClient, AnchoredReputation.sol:1818); RowVoided does close those, so only the label is wrong in that case.
details_en.evidence: audit.ts:117-124 compares shares and pushes INFLATED for the committed edge e (agentId = its dst) whenever |w|*B_true > |wr|*B_committed, with no finding for an omitted positive edge (only OMITTED_NEG, :135-139); ancre.ts:21-25 proofOf(INFLATED) -> 'proveEdge'; ancre.ts:164-165 `if (d.certificate_id !== h.lastCertificate_id || d.provenAtBlock !== undefined || d.u !== node) continue; if (agentId !== undefined && d.agentId !== undefined && d.agentId !== agentId) continue;`. Contract AnchoredReputation.sol:1659 `if (wNew == m.wOld) revert NothingToProve();` (proveEdge on Y), :1683 EdgeProven(setId, v.u, agentJ, ...) names the proven edge X. Twin path: solver/watcher.py:8-10 DEFLATED / DILUTION are reported on the omitted/deflated edge with proveEdge(agentJ = that edge). Scratch test sweep/ix/test/sweep.test.ts 'DILUTION': before {ds:[[INFLATED,2,'2',10000,10000,proveEdge,null]], health:[DISCREPANCY,1,0,0]}, after EdgeProven(node 2, agentId 3): {ds:[[INFLATED,2,'2',10000,10000,proveEdge,null]], health:[DISCREPANCY,1,1,0]}. The repo's own normative vector agrees: solver/vectors/violations/dilution.json ('edge #18 -> #3 omitted ... #2 receives twice its share', violation.wRegistry = wCommitted = 10000 on dst #2) is expected as [['INFLATED','2']] by indexer/test/ancre.real.test.ts:75, i.e. the finding names #2, whose proveEdge reverts NothingToProve, while the provable edge is #18 -> #3.

constats.titre: Flux x402 « upfront » : une réponse non-2xx avec `PAYMENT-RESPONSE success:true` est annoncée refusée
constats.resume: `flows.ts:249` exige `res.ok` en plus de `success === true`. En flux upfront (accepté pour exact/eip3009 en @x402 2.27), le serveur règle avant le handler et renvoie un non-2xx avec un PAYMENT-RESPONSE réussi si le handler échoue : le plugin dit REFUSED/« Not paid ». Même défaut dans override.ts:151.
constats.scenario: Reproduit de bout en bout avec @x402/express 2.27.0 en upfront : règlement fait, HTTP 500 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE success, plugin REFUSED/SETTLEMENT_FAILED avec note d'override : l'humain peut payer une seconde fois.
constats.correctif: Traiter `success:true` avec un hash comme PAID quel que soit le statut HTTP (et lire `authorizationState`, voir A4a).

details_en.summary: A settled payment is reported as REFUSED / paid:false when the response is non-2xx but carries a successful PAYMENT-RESPONSE (x402 v2 'upfront' flow, which selectOffer does not filter); the same check exists in override.ts:151.
details_en.failure_scenario: Provider offers exact USDC with extra.paymentFlow='upfront' (supported for eip3009 in @x402/evm 2.27, exact/server paymentFlows). The server settles before the handler; the handler fails and the server answers 500 with PAYMENT-RESPONSE {success:true, transaction:0x..} (core createFailurePathSettlementHeaders). flows.ts:249 requires res.ok, so it goes to the REFUSED branch. explain (TrustGatedPayer.sol:240, which does not look at nonce use) returns OK, and afterFailure (verdict.ts:85) turns that into SETTLEMENT_FAILED 'Not paid'. The result also carries liveAuthorization 'can still be settled' and a humanOverride note (flows.ts:269-270), and the journal records settlement_refused. Yet the USDC already left the payer, so the human may approve a second payment. override.ts:151-160 has the same defect: OVERRIDE_FAILED after the human's funds have moved.
details_en.evidence: V3 verifier (partial save): CONFIRMED. partial save; e2e with @x402/express 2.27.0 upfront: settle=1, HTTP 500 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE success, plugin REFUSED/SETTLEMENT_FAILED Independently reproduced end to end with @x402/express 2.27.0 upfront flow (settle=1, HTTP 500 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE success -> plugin REFUSED/SETTLEMENT_FAILED).
details_en.fix: Treat PAYMENT-RESPONSE success:true with a transaction as PAID whatever the HTTP status (and read authorizationState, see A4a); same in override.ts:151.

constats.titre: Après un paiement signé, toute réponse non-2xx sans preuve est annoncée « non payé »
constats.resume: `payFlow` décide sur le seul statut HTTP : une réponse non-2xx sans `PAYMENT-RESPONSE success:true` (y compris le `settlement_pending` de x402 2.27 qui porte un hash diffusé) donne REFUSED, SETTLEMENT_FAILED « Not paid », note d'override et journal `settlement_refused`, alors que le transfert a pu être miné. Le plugin ne lit jamais `USDC.authorizationState(payer, nonce)`, que le contrat utilise pourtant.
constats.scenario: Reproduit avec un vrai serveur `@x402/express`/`@x402/core` 2.27.0 : facilitateur qui renvoie `settlement_pending` avec un hash, facilitateur en délai dépassé après diffusion, proxy qui renvoie 504 après règlement. L'humain lit « non payé » et peut repayer après validBefore. Distinct de K15.
constats.correctif: Après une réponse non-2xx, lire `authorizationState(payer, nonce)` (et le reçu si un hash est fourni) : PAID si le nonce est consommé, sinon UNKNOWN avec `liveAuthorization` ; même chose dans override.ts:159.

details_en.summary: After a signed payment, payFlow decides only from the HTTP status: any non-2xx response that lacks PAYMENT-RESPONSE success:true, including x402 2.27's own non-terminal 'settlement_pending' failure that carries a broadcast transaction hash, is reported as outcome REFUSED, explainAfterFailure SETTLEMENT_FAILED 'Not paid', journal settlement_refused, with the humanOverride note. The plugin never reads USDC.authorizationState(payer, nonce), which the payer contract itself uses (_settleable) to tell whether the authorisation was consumed.
details_en.failure_scenario: End to end with the real @x402/express + @x402/core 2.27.0 server and the plugin's payFlow built from the current source (phase2/v3/e2e/v6_a4a.mjs). (1) The facilitator broadcasts tx 0x77.. but returns {success:false, errorReason:'settlement_pending', transaction:0x77..} twice. settleWithPendingRetry retries once, then buildSettlementFailureResponse answers 402 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE with that hash. The plugin returns REFUSED paid=false, 'Not paid, and not because of ANCRE', humanOverride PRESENT, journal settlement_refused(HTTP 402), although it holds the hash of a broadcast transfer. (2) The facilitator times out after broadcasting: 402 success:false, transaction '' -> same output. (3) The origin settles and answers 200 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE, but a reverse proxy or CDN times out first (504) -> same output with settlement undefined. In each case the USDC can be gone from the payer while the human is told it was not paid. Once validBefore passes, the human can approve a second payment (pay's own hint says only 'do not sign again before validBefore'), and a payee that settles and then answers 402 can induce exactly that. Distinct from K15, where the header says success:true.
details_en.evidence: flows.ts:249 `if (res.ok && settlement?.success === true && settlement.transaction)` -> PAID; :254 `if (res.ok)` -> UNKNOWN; every other response falls through to :259-270 (explain, then `j("settlement_refused")`, `outcome: "REFUSED"`, humanOverride when !pay). explain (TrustGatedPayer.sol:240) never looks at nonce use; afterFailure (verdict.ts:85) turns its OK into SETTLEMENT_FAILED, whose action begins 'Not paid' (verdict.ts:81). The plugin's own definition at flows.ts:171 ('UNKNOWN: no settlement evidence') says a 504 without PAYMENT-RESPONSE should be UNKNOWN. TrustGatedPayer.sol:474-480 `_settleable` already reads `authorizationState(address(this), p.nonce)`. @x402/core 2.27 chunk-FV2JN4FK.mjs:673 SETTLEMENT_PENDING_REASON = 'settlement_pending', :1699 settleWithPendingRetry, :2918-2934 failure response = 402 + settlement headers. SKILL.md:71-73 tells the agent to report paid:false/signed:true as 'the settlement was refused ... the gate working'.
details_en.fix: After any non-2xx paid response, read USDC.authorizationState(cfg.payer, auth.nonce) (plus the receipt of settlement.transaction when one is present). Report PAID when the nonce is used (the plugin never cancels). Report UNKNOWN with liveAuthorization when the response does not prove a verify-time rejection. Never print 'Not paid' from the HTTP status alone. The same applies to override.ts:159.

constats.titre: `payer status` ne bannit que le wallet sélectionné, l'override bannit tous les wallets de l'hôte
constats.resume: `statusFlow.isHuman` (flows.ts:319) exclut le payeur, les opérateurs et le seul wallet sélectionné ; `override` exclut toutes les adresses du wallet hôte. Les deux règles divergent déjà.
constats.scenario: L'hôte gère A (sélectionné, opérateur) et B ; owner = treasury = B : `payer status` coche « owner and treasury are the human » alors que l'agent peut basculer sur B et appeler setPolicy/setOperator/sweep (reproduit sur `dist` avec des stubs). Même défaut pour la vérification « pas d'USDC sur l'Agent Wallet ».
constats.correctif: Passer `allWalletAddresses(snapshot)` à `statusFlow` et partager un seul helper `humanSigners()` avec `overrideFlow`.

details_en.summary: statusFlow re-implements the 'owner/treasury must be the human' rule with its own isHuman (payer, operators, SELECTED wallet only) instead of reusing the banned-set logic of overrideFlow (override.ts:83-84, fed by host.ts:allWalletAddresses); the two copies already disagree.
details_en.failure_scenario: Host Agent Wallet manages A (selected, payer operator) and B (another remoteWallets/byokWallets entry); payer owner = treasury = B. `mm ancre payer status` (status.ts:28 passes only selectedWallet) reports guarantee 'owner and treasury are the human' ok:true (reproduced on dist/lib/flows.js with stubs), while `mm ancre override` bans B and refuses with ANCRE_OVERRIDE_MISCONFIGURED. Status therefore certifies a setup where the agent can switch to B and call setPolicy/setOperator/sweep, i.e. the hard guard does not hold; the 'no USDC on the Agent Wallet' check has the same flaw (only the selected address's balance is read). Fix: pass allWalletAddresses(snapshot) and share one humanSigners(owner, treasury, payer, operators, agentWallets) helper between statusFlow and overrideFlow.
details_en.evidence: V3 verifier (partial save): CONFIRMED.  Reproduced by the Reuse finder on dist/lib/flows.js with stubs (status ok:true vs override ANCRE_OVERRIDE_MISCONFIGURED).
details_en.fix: Pass allWalletAddresses(snapshot) to statusFlow and share one humanSigners() helper with overrideFlow (also check every host address's USDC balance).

constats.titre: L'override « humain » se décide sur un payeur et un RPC choisis par l'appelant
constats.resume: Le seul contrôle qui rend l'override humain (signataire = owner ou treasury du payeur, pas un opérateur) lit ces adresses sur le payeur de `--payer`/`ANCRE_PAYER`, via le RPC de `--rpc-url`/`ANCRE_RPC_URL` : un agent qui lance l'override dans un pty avec un faux RPC (ou un payeur qu'il a déployé) fait accepter sa propre clé financée comme « l'humain ».
constats.scenario: Faux RPC qui répond owner = treasury = K : la page de signature est pilotée sans navigateur, résultat `OVERRIDE_PAID human=K`, journalisé comme override humain (MESURÉ, PoC sur build frais). Aucun fonds du payeur ni de l'humain ne bouge, mais la promesse du README (« any freshly funded key is refused ») et D47 tombent.
constats.correctif: Lire owner/treasury/opérateurs uniquement via `ctx.publicClient(cfg.chainId)` (pas de `--rpc-url` pour cette commande) et prendre le payeur d'une valeur épinglée par l'humain ; reformuler le README.

details_en.summary: The only check that makes the override human-only (signer == payer.owner() or payer.treasury(), not an operator) reads those addresses from the payer named by --payer/ANCRE_PAYER, through the RPC named by --rpc-url/ANCRE_RPC_URL, both chosen by whoever runs the command, so an agent that runs the override in a pty gets a key it funded accepted as 'the human'.
details_en.failure_scenario: The agent runs `mm ancre override https://farm/quote --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:9545` in a pseudo-terminal. Its own JSON-RPC answers owner() = treasury() = K (a key it funded itself), operators() = [Agent Wallet], decide() = UNTRUSTED and balanceOf(K) = 1000 USDC. It types `override 666`, reads the page URL and token from stderr, GETs /template, signs with K and POSTs /done, with no browser and no MetaMask. Re-run of a4/poc_override_rpc.mjs on a fresh build of the current source (v6_work/poc): outcome OVERRIDE_PAID, human = K, journal override_requested -> override_signed payer=K -> override_paid payer=K. Same result through the real gateway with `--payer <a TrustGatedPayer the agent deployed with owner = treasury = K>`. No funds of the payer or of the human can move, and K could pay the farm outside the plugin anyway (README condition 2). What breaks is the documented property: README 'any other key is refused ... and any freshly funded key' and D47 'Un agent ne peut jamais l'exécuter'. The result and the journal then report an agent payment as a human override.
details_en.evidence: override.ts:78-84 `read<Address>(d, cfg.payer, payerAbi, "owner")` / `"treasury"` / `"operators"`, then `humans = [owner, treasury]...filter(!banned)`. d.readContract comes from commands/ancre/override.ts:41 `hostDeps(this.ctx, io, cfg, null, inp.rpcUrl ?? process.env.ANCRE_RPC_URL)`, and host.ts:14 builds a plain http client on that URL. cfg.payer comes from `resolveConfig({ payer: inp.payer })` (override.ts:38, config.ts:29). The signature check at override.ts:121-131 is local and only compares against those RPC-supplied addresses. interactive.ts:2-4 itself says a program can allocate a pty. test/override.test.mjs:136 ('a funded third-party key ... is refused') stubs readContract so that owner = the human, and so does not cover this case. README.md:82-85.
details_en.fix: Read the override's owner/treasury/operators only through ctx.publicClient(cfg.chainId) (drop --rpc-url/ANCRE_RPC_URL for this command), take the payer from a value the human pinned at setup rather than from --payer or the environment, and reword the README: the check binds only for the payer the human configured, and an agent holding funded keys can always pay outside the plugin.

constats.titre: `ancreGuard` (garde SDK x402) ignore réseau, schéma, actif et montant
constats.resume: La garde côté client ne vérifie que `agentWallet(agentId) == payTo` et `isTrusted` : elle approuve une offre sur n'importe quelle chaîne (le README l'enregistre pour `eip155:*`), en n'importe quel jeton, avec n'importe quel plafond upto, et n'a pas de contrôle de wallet nul. Les règles de `selectOffer` n'existent que sur le chemin CLI.
constats.scenario: Offres sur eip155:8453, eip155:1 ou solana, schéma upto, actif quelconque, montant 1e9 : toutes ALLOWED sur la base du verdict lu sur Monad (reproduit par cinq agents, `e/guard_net.mjs`). Sur Base, l'adresse `payTo` d'un portefeuille contrat peut appartenir à quelqu'un d'autre.
constats.correctif: Un seul prédicat d'offre partagé avec `selectOffer` (exact, réseau = chaîne d'ANCRE, USDC de cette chaîne, domaine FiatToken, plafonds) et refus d'un agentWallet nul.

details_en.summary: ancreGuard (the client-side hook for the official x402 SDK) checks only agentWallet(agentId) == payTo and isTrusted: it never checks the offer's network, scheme, asset or amount (the README registers it for 'eip155:*'), and has no zero-wallet check (a cleared agentWallet 0x0 equals a payTo 0x0), so a Monad ERC-8004/ANCRE verdict approves payments on any chain, in any token, with any 'upto' cap; the CLI path's selectOffer rules exist on one path only.
details_en.failure_scenario: Guard registered as documented (x402Client().register('eip155:*', ...)), isTrusted(12) = true, getAgentWallet(12) = W on Monad: offers {network eip155:8453 / eip155:1 / solana:..., scheme 'upto', asset any token, amount 1e9, payTo W, extra.erc8004AgentId '12'} are all ALLOWED (scratch e/guard_net.mjs against plugin/dist, reproduced by five agents). The EOA signs a Base payment to W, an address whose control on Base is unrelated to Monad agent #12 (contract/counterfactual wallet), with no amount bound.
details_en.evidence: V3 verifier (partial save): CONFIRMED; reproduced by A4, ALT, E, D3 (e/guard_net.mjs, a4/guard_net.mjs). x402-guard.ts:25 Requirements has no scheme/asset; l.42-52 decide() reads only agentId, payTo, getAgentWallet, isTrusted; l.48 `getAddress(wallet) !== getAddress(req.payTo)` (0x0 == 0x0 passes).
details_en.fix: Share one offer predicate with selectOffer (scheme exact, network = the chain ANCRE is read on, asset = that chain's USDC, FiatToken domain, amount caps) and refuse a zero agentWallet, as TrustGatedPayer does (NO_WALLET).

constats.titre: Calldata passé à `cast` en argument de ligne de commande : E2BIG sous Linux
constats.resume: `Chain._run` et `Chain.decode` passent les blobs entiers en argv ; sous Linux un argument de plus de 131 072 octets fait lever `OSError E2BIG` avant tout appel RPC.
constats.scenario: Certificat attesté de la taille du scénario D (1 237 nœuds) : input de 179 146 caractères (MESURÉ avec l'encodeur actuel) ; le watcher le classe « undecodable », la synchronisation de table peut se bloquer, et au-delà d'environ 4 100 arêtes le certificateur ne peut même plus estimer. Non atteignable sur macOS ni en Registry-verified ; non testé sous Linux (PLAUSIBLE).
constats.correctif: Ne jamais mettre un blob en argv : `cast decode-calldata --file`, `eth_estimateGas`/`eth_sendRawTransaction` par stdin ou JSON-RPC direct.

details_en.summary: Chain._run and Chain.decode (l.266) hand whole calldata blobs (vectors, rows, the full tx input) to `cast` as single argv strings; on a Linux host any string above MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131 072 bytes incl. NUL) makes subprocess raise OSError E2BIG before any RPC call, so large Submitter-attested certificates cannot be audited by the watcher, can wedge the node-table sync of both services, and above ~4 100 edges cannot even be estimated by the certifier.
details_en.failure_scenario: Linux host, Submitter-attested set like simulate.py scenario D (1 237 nodes, 3 741 edges, k = 2; rebuilt offline with the current encoder): the submitCertificate input is 179 146 hex chars (vectors 59 378, rows 119 164). watcher.decode_submission -> Chain.decode(SUBMIT_SIG, input) -> OSError [Errno 7] -> journaled 'undecodable', the certificate is never audited or proven (same path reproduced on macOS with the finder's PoC at 1.2 MB). Threshold for the whole input ~65.5 KB of calldata, i.e. ~800-900 nodes at k = 2-3 (CALCULÉ from the measured sizes). chain_table decodes the same full input whenever an update carries inline newNodes (<= 100 new nodes, plan's small case), so after the first such update of a large set every table sync of the certifier and the watcher raises forever. The certifier's own estimate/send fails when rows > 65 534 bytes (~4 100 edges at the measured ~15.9 B/edge; ~15.7 M gas CALCULÉ by scaling scenario D's 14.25 M, under the cap) or vectors > 65 534 bytes (n > 2 047 at k = 3, > 910 at k = 8). Not reachable on macOS (ARG_MAX = 1 048 576 for argv+env, more calldata than any certificate under the 25 M cap) nor for Registry-verified sets (~480 edges max under the cap, ~23 KB of input). To confirm: run watcher.py on Linux against a scenario-D-sized certificate, or `subprocess.run([cast, 'decode-calldata', SUBMIT_SIG, <179 146-char input>])` on Linux.
details_en.evidence: certifier.py l.223 `subprocess.run([self.cast, sub, "--rpc-url", self.rpc, *sig, *args], ...)` with args from plan l.437-438 (`"0x" + enc["vectors"].hex()`, `"0x" + enc["rows"].hex()`); l.266 `subprocess.run([self.cast, "decode-calldata", sig, data], ...)`; l.312 chain_table decodes SUBMIT_SIG inputs; watcher.py l.191 and l.211-215 (`except Exception` -> 'undecodable'). export.encode: vectors = n x (8k + 8) bytes. Sizes measured with the current encoder: phase2/v7b_work/argv_sizes.py (scenario D 179 146 chars; 755 nodes k = 3: 122 058; 957 nodes k = 3: 154 378; 1 972 nodes / 5 964 edges k = 3: rows 189 972). Finder PoC re-run: 'undecodable', "[Errno 7] Argument list too long" at 1 200 650 chars on macOS. `getconf ARG_MAX` = 1048576 on this Mac; Linux execve(2): MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 131072. No hosting for the services is documented (Docker daemon not running here, Linux not tested).
details_en.fix: Never put a blob on argv: decode with `cast decode-calldata --file <tmp>` (cast 1.8.3 supports -f/--file) or in Python, estimate with `cast rpc eth_estimateGas --raw` reading its JSON params from stdin, and send the signed transaction the same way (eth_sendRawTransaction over stdin or a direct HTTP JSON-RPC request).

constats.titre: Recul de la tête ou bloc spéculatif abandonné : « node table gap » à vie
constats.resume: `Certifier.table` et `watcher.main` enregistrent `head` comme point de synchronisation sans condition et ne vident jamais le cache après un échec : toute désynchronisation transforme chaque tour suivant en `RuntimeError node table gap` jusqu'au redémarrage.
constats.scenario: eth_blockNumber plus bas qu'au tour précédent (backend en retard) ou `NodesAdded` lu sur un bloc `latest` (proposé, révocable sur Monad) puis abandonné : blocage reproduit avec le vrai code ; déclencheur non observé (120 lectures monotones, MESURÉ 06/10).
constats.correctif: Synchroniser jusqu'à `finalized`, ne jamais faire reculer le point de synchronisation, vider le cache sur un trou (ou lire `nodeKeyAt`).

details_en.summary: Certifier.table (certifier.py:536-538) and watcher.main (watcher.py:295-296) record the sync point as `head` unconditionally and never reset the cached node table after a failed sync. Any desync between the cache and the chain then turns every later round into RuntimeError('node table gap') until the process restarts. Two triggers: an eth_blockNumber lower than an earlier answer, or a NodesAdded read from Monad's speculative `latest` block that is later abandoned.
details_en.failure_scenario: Round 1 syncs to head 100 and applies NodesAdded(start=k) mined at block 98. Round 2 gets eth_blockNumber = 95 from a lagging backend: chain_table(101, 95) returns early and _table_block becomes 95. Round 3 re-reads [96, head] and meets the same NodesAdded with start=k while the table already has k+2 entries, so it raises 'node table gap'. Neither _table nor _table_block changes on the exception, so every later round raises the same error (reproduced with the real Certifier.table/chain_table, PoC phase1/D2work/head_regress.py). certifier.main stops submitting (after maxAge the set is STALE and every payer refuses) and watcher.main stops auditing; both only journal 'error'. The same lock-up follows if a NodesAdded is read from a Proposed block (Monad `latest`) that is abandoned and re-included later, or dropped. To confirm on the deployment RPC: a non-monotonic eth_blockNumber, or an abandoned proposal that carries a NodesAdded.
details_en.evidence: certifier.py:536-538 `self._table = chain_table(..., self._table_block + 1, head, self._table)` / `self._table_block = head`; chain_table:300-301 `if isinstance(to_block, int) and from_block > to_block: return table` and :306-307 `if start != len(table): raise RuntimeError(f"node table gap ...")`; watcher.py:295-296 same pattern (`table, table_block = nodes, head`). PoC output: 'sync to head 95 ... _table_block = 95' then 'sync to head 120: RuntimeError: node table gap: NodesAdded from 1, table has 3' (and again at 130). Trigger not observed: 40 eth_blockNumber calls on each of rpc.monad.xyz, rpc1.monad.xyz and testnet-rpc.monad.xyz (06/10, read-only) were monotonic. Vault note 'Différences EVM — Monad vs Ethereum' §2.5: `latest` = Proposed, speculatively executed; an abandoned proposal is 'abandonnée implicitement (aucun event d'abandon)', a 'très rare' case. Scope: demo/certify.py overrides table() (DemoCertifier) and calls run_once once, so the act-2 demo is not affected. Only the long-running certifier.main / watcher.main are, which are planned for the judging period (ROADMAP.md:162, MUSTDO item 16).
details_en.fix: Sync the table only up to a final block (Monad `finalized` = latest-2), never move _table_block backwards (max(old, head)), and on a gap reset the cache (_table=None, _table_block=-1) to resync from block 0, or read nodeCount/nodeKeyAt as demo/certify.py does.

constats.titre: `registryChanged` saute aussi la garde REFUSED-first
constats.resume: La garde se trouve dans le bloc `if (... && !s.registryChanged && ...)` : une fois le drapeau levé, la resoumission identique d'un certificat prouvé faux est acceptée, alors qu'ENCODING §5 applique REFUSED-first avant toutes les clauses d'acceptation.
constats.scenario: Titulaire prouvé dilué, puis `checkRegistry` lève le drapeau après une mise à jour du registre : la resoumission identique est acceptée et efface les preuves (MESURÉ, test `FinderA`). Effet propre marginal, K7 suffit déjà à contourner la garde.
constats.correctif: Sortir REFUSED-first du bloc `!registryChanged` (comme le dit §5) ; c'est la correction de K7 qui ferme vraiment le trou.

details_en.summary: The REFUSED-first check sits inside `if (s.certBlock != 0 && !s.registryChanged && s.numSubmitters == 0)`, so once registryChanged is set a byte-identical resubmission of a proven-wrong certificate is accepted, whereas ENCODING §5 applies REFUSED first before the registryChanged acceptance clause.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set, incumbent proven wrong by a dilution proof; a registry version change is recorded by checkRegistry; the byte-identical certificate is resubmitted and accepted (registry re-reads still match), resetting eLow to 0 and quality().proven to false. Incremental impact is small: under registryChanged the spec accepts any other valid certificate anyway, and K7 already defeats the byte-identity check, so this is mainly a spec deviation.
details_en.evidence: l.572 wraps l.576; ENCODING §5: 'REFUSED first: ... then accepted iff: no certificate | registryChanged | ...'. Scratch FinderA.t.sol::test_registryChangedSkipsProvenRefusal PASS on the current source (rep.setVersion("2.1.0"), checkRegistry true, identical resubmission accepted, proof erased).
details_en.fix: Hoist the REFUSED-first check out of the !registryChanged block (apply it whenever certBlock != 0 and numSubmitters == 0), as ENCODING §5 specifies; the K7 fix is what actually closes the hole.

constats.titre: Règle de remplacement : croissance honnête refusée avec un sPlus déclaré (jusqu'à maxAge)
constats.resume: (a) Une croissance qui renormalise une ligne fait baisser la masse ou D de la mise à jour honnête, refusée jusqu'à minRefresh : c'est la voie « baisse » prévue (une preuve débloque), seule la phrase « graphe qui grandit : certifié sans attente » des rapports est trop large. (b) Défaut réel mais latent : avec un sPlus déclaré, q contient une marge proportionnelle à la masse de la ligne, donc une croissance honnête fait monter q et les deux voies la refusent jusqu'à maxAge ; le commentaire l.557 « q = 0 quelle que soit la taille du graphe » est faux.
constats.scenario: (b) k = 1, ligne X déclarée sPlus = 20 000 : un nouvel avis honnête Y→X fait passer la masse de 0,6296 à 0,7143 WAD mais q de 0,2222 à 0,2857 : `NotBetter` même après minRefresh, accepté seulement après maxAge (environ 24 h, MESURÉ par test). Le solveur ne déclare un sPlus que pour une ligne de plus de 256 arêtes positives : aucune aujourd'hui sur le mainnet.
constats.correctif: (b) Comparer les marges par unité de masse (par ex. qNew·mCur ≤ qCur·mNew) ou exempter une marge dont la part omise est inchangée, et corriger le commentaire l.557 ; (a) documentation seulement.

details_en.summary: Both refusals reproduce, but only (b) is a defect. (a) Growth that renormalises a row (S+ + w_new > GRID) lowers the honest update's mass or D and is refused until minRefresh: this is the documented decrease route, since the incumbent now overstates and a proveEdge unlocks it; a lower D waits for the window by design. Only the claim 'growing graph certified at once' is too broad. (b) With a declared sPlus (honest under ENCODING §3.2, and what the solver's cap_row emits for rows over ROW_MAX), q includes a margin proportional to the row's mass. An honest update that raises that mass raises q, so both paths refuse it (slackRefresh 0) until maxAge. The only other way out is a proof against an HONEST incumbent, which the reference watcher deliberately never sends. This contradicts the l.557 comment 'q = 0 whatever the graph size'.
details_en.failure_scenario: (b) k = 1 open Registry-verified set. A -> X; X -> Y committed, X -> Q omitted with declared sPlus = 20,000; certificate 1 has q_cur = 0.2222 WAD and mass 0.6296. A new honest feedback Y -> X raises mass to 0.7143 and q to 0.2857: the honest update reverts NotBetter(0.2857, 0.2222, 0.7143, 0.6296) even after minRefresh. It is accepted only at age > maxAge (default 288,000 blocks, ~24 h at 0.302 s). Until then X's new trust, and any agent the update would add, stays uncertified. The same growth without the declared omission is accepted at once (test_b_noDeclaredIsFine). Proving the new edge Y -> X (OMITTED_POSITIVE) on the incumbent lifts q_cur to 0.3704 and unlocks the update (test_b_proofUnlocks). But watcher.py 'reports them and never proves them', and certifier.replacement_wait just waits maxAge. In the reference solver the trigger is a certified row with more than ROW_MAX = 256 positive edges. None exists on today's mainnet data (84 rated agents) or in the demo, so (b) is latent. It becomes attacker-reachable if 02-bis/04-bis start omitting expensive pairs with a declared sPlus (E1/EFF1). (a) A -> X -> Y, then A vouches a new W: mass 0.7037 -> 0.6296, NotBetter until minRefresh (600 blocks by default), while the incumbent overstates t_X 2x (0.2222 vs 0.1111). proveEdge(anchor row, W) on the incumbent (242,610 gas) credits eLow and the update passes at once (test_a_proofUnlocks). In the D-only variant (equal mass 0.5556, D halved), a proof does not help with a large eLowMax (distrustMass is never amended): it waits for the window, as ENCODING §5 states for a lower D.
details_en.evidence: l.578 fast path '(mNew + s.eLowEff >= s.mass && qNew <= qCur && dNew >= s.distrustMass)'; l.579 window '(age > s.minRefresh && qNew <= qCur + s.slackRefresh)'. l.723 q = ceil((sum - ePos - 1)·aD/aN) keeps the declared-omission margin (margins(), l.910) and the truncation margin (l.711-715), both proportional to t_u. Comment l.557-558: 'an honest certificate at its integer fixed point has q = 0 whatever the graph size', false once sPlus is declared. Finder PoCs re-run and passing: FinderA2 test_growthMassDropRefused and test_growthDistrustDropRefused, FinderA6 test_growthWithDeclaredOmissionWaitsMaxAge. Own tests: phase2/v5c_work/c/test/V5cA1c.t.sol (3/3) and V5cA1c2.t.sol (D variant: accepted after the proof only through eLowEff > eLowMax with eLowMax = 1e16; still refused with eLowMax = 1e18). Intent for (a): Verified.t.sol test_openReplacementRule claims growth is 'accepted at once' only when 'the row stays under GRID (no dilution)', and a decrease is 'refused until the incumbent is PROVEN to overstate'. ENCODING §5 says 'the refresh window lets an unproven decrease (revocation) through' and 'a forgiven slash (lower D) waits for the window'. Overbroad doc claims: docs/chantiers/rapports/integration.md:108 'graphe qui grandit : certifié sans attente'; CR-conseil.md:1312. Path to (b) in the solver: ppr.cap_row with sPlus = g.splus (true sum), export.py:201 sets HDR_SPLUS when sPlus != committed S+, watcher.py:12-13, certifier.py replacement_wait.
details_en.fix: (b) Make q comparable across graphs: judge the declared-omission and truncation margins per unit of mass (for example accept if qNew·mCur <= qCur·mNew, or exempt a margin whose omitted share (sPlus - S+)/B+ is unchanged), and correct the l.557 comment. Alternatively, document prove-then-submit and have the certifier prove the new positive edges itself when replacement_wait returns a maxAge wait. (a) Docs only: say that renormalising growth takes the decrease route (a proof, or the window for D).

constats.titre: `dryRun` sans `newNodes` : inutilisable pour un certificat qui ajoute ses nœuds en ligne
constats.resume: `dryRun` vérifie nCert contre le nodeCount courant et n'accepte pas de `newNodes` : il revert `BadNCert` sur le cas standard « petit premier certificat » que `submitCertificate` accepte.
constats.scenario: Set neuf (nodeCount = k) : `dryRun(setId, 4, …)` revert `BadNCert`, la soumission avec 3 nœuds en ligne passe (MESURÉ). Le certificateur du dépôt n'appelle jamais `dryRun` (il estime la transaction complète) : impact limité aux outils tiers.
constats.correctif: Donner un argument `newNodes` à `dryRun` (nCert borné par nodeCount + entrées) ou documenter qu'il faut d'abord ajouter les nœuds.

details_en.summary: dryRun has no newNodes argument and checks nCert against the current nodeCount, so it reverts BadNCert on any certificate whose nodes travel inline in submitCertificate (the certifier's standard small case, e.g. a first certificate); but solver/certifier.py never calls dryRun, so the impact is an unusable helper, not a broken pre-check.
details_en.failure_scenario: Reproduced (ScratchDryRun.test_dryRunCannotCheckAFirstCertificateWithNewNodes): a fresh set has nodeCount = k; dryRun(setId, 4, vec, rows) reverts BadNCert, while submitCertificate(setId, 4, max, newNodes = 3 agents, vec, rows) is accepted and isTrusted(101) is true. certifier.plan puts the new nodes inline when there are <= inline_nodes_max (100) of them (certifier.py:422-440), but run_once pre-checks each transaction with Chain.estimate = `cast estimate --from <submitter>` of the full submitCertificate call with newNodes (certifier.py:241-242, 586-592), which models the append, the shape, the fp bound and the registry re-reads. No caller of dryRun exists in solver/, plugin/, indexer/ or scripts (only ENCODING.md §3 and the ERC draft mention it). Real impact: a third-party certifier cannot use dryRun for such a certificate and must eth_call submitCertificate.
details_en.evidence: AnchoredReputation.sol:591 `function dryRun(bytes32 setId, uint32 nCert, bytes calldata vectors, bytes calldata rows)`; :599 `if (nCert < s.nCert || nCert > s.nodeCount || nCert < k) revert BadNCert();` vs submitCertificate :503 `if (newNodes.length != 0) _appendNodes(s, setId, newNodes);` before the same check at :506. `git grep -n dryRun` -> contracts/src (591), contracts/ENCODING.md:69, docs/erc/anchored-reputation.md:648 only.
details_en.fix: Give dryRun a newNodes argument (bound nCert by nodeCount + number of entries), or document that the nodes must be added first and point certifiers to eth_call submitCertificate.

constats.titre: `dryRun` ne fait que l'arithmétique
constats.resume: `dryRun` exécute seulement `_verifyPass` : il saute la règle de forme (qui ne lit pas le registre) et la borne 2^63 des empreintes, et renvoie donc eUp/eEff/graphRoot pour des certificats que `submitCertificate` refuse.
constats.scenario: Ligne d'ancre portant un wallet, arête vers une ancre, empreinte = 2^63 : `dryRun` répond, la soumission revert (MESURÉ). Aucun outil du dépôt n'appelle `dryRun` (le certificateur estime `submitCertificate` lui-même) : seul un outil tiers qui s'y fie obtient un faux OK.
constats.correctif: Appeler aussi `_verifyRows(..., reads = false)` et contrôler les empreintes < 2^63 dans `dryRun`, ou le documenter comme purement arithmétique.

details_en.summary: dryRun runs only _verifyPass: it skips the shape rule of _verifyRows (registry-free when reads = false) and the ownerFp < 2^63 bound enforced only in _storeVectors, so it returns eUp/eEff/graphRoot for certificates that submitCertificate rejects; no in-repo tool calls dryRun, so this is a tooling-only gap.
details_en.failure_scenario: Reproduced: an anchor row carrying a wallet makes dryRun return eEff 0.444 WAD, then submitCertificate reverts EdgeMismatch(0, 256); an edge to an anchor node passes dryRun, then submit reverts EdgeMismatch(0, 0) (ScratchDryRun); ownerFp = 2^63 passes dryRun, then submit reverts ValueTooLarge (V4Verify.test_K12_dryRunAcceptsOwnerFpTooLarge). The candidate's consequence ('the certifier pays the full gas limit of the failed transaction') does not happen with the shipped certifier: it never calls dryRun and pre-checks every transaction with `cast estimate` of submitCertificate itself, which reverts on these inputs (certifier.py:241-242, 586-592).
