Only a third-party tool that trusts dryRun as a validity check gets a false OK.
details_en.evidence: AnchoredReputation.sol:601 `Pass memory P = _verifyPass(s, nCert, vectors, rows);` and nothing else; the shape lives in _verifyRows (:1127 `if (dk >> 248 != KIND_AGENT) revert EdgeMismatch(ri, e);`, _clientRare :1179), which needs no registry read when reads = false; _verifyPass's tooBig (:718) covers the k t-columns only (:694 cp = vecOff + a*8), and the fp lane bound is the orAll of _storeVectors (:1253-1255, :1296-1298). Doc :588-590 promises 'the per-column upper bounds, eEff and graphRoot a submission would produce'. `git grep dryRun`: only the contract, ENCODING.md §3 and the ERC draft.
details_en.fix: In dryRun also call _verifyRows(s, setId, nCert, vectors, rows, P.W, false) and check the fp lanes < 2^63 (both view and registry-free), or document dryRun as arithmetic-only.

constats.titre: `_verifyOwners` ne vérifie ni les ancres ni les agents sans masse
constats.resume: La boucle commence à i = k et ne contrôle que les agents massifs : l'empreinte d'une ancre n'est jamais exigée nulle et un agent sans masse peut porter n'importe quelle empreinte, contrairement à ENCODING §3.1/§3.4. N'importe qui peut ensuite faire flaguer par `proveTransfer` un agent sans masse qui n'a jamais changé d'owner.
constats.scenario: Un tiers resoumet le même certificat avec des empreintes arbitraires (masse, q, D inchangés : accepté), puis `proveTransfer(102)` réussit et `assess` renvoie TRANSFERRED pour un agent jamais transféré (MESURÉ). L'agent n'est payable dans aucun cas : seul le motif affiché est faux ; l'empreinte arbitraire nourrit aussi la malléabilité de K7.
constats.correctif: Vérifier aussi i < k (empreinte 0) et soit toutes les empreintes d'agents certifiés, soit ignorer les nœuds sans masse dans `proveTransfer` et dans le statut TRANSFERRED.

details_en.summary: _verifyOwners starts at i = k, so the ownerFp lane of anchor nodes is never required to be 0, and it checks agents only when they have mass, so a zero-mass agent may carry any fingerprint; anyone can then make proveTransfer flag a zero-mass agent that never changed owner, and assess/decide/explain report TRANSFERRED.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open Registry-verified set. The honest certificate carries the right fingerprints (export.py:260 writes owner_fp for every agent node, 0 for anchors/addresses). A third party resubmits the same t and rows with anchor lane 0xdead and #102 (zero mass) lane 0x1234: same mass/q/D, so the fast path accepts it and both lanes are stored (test_K11_zeroMassWrongFpThenProveTransfer). assess(102) is OK. Then proveTransfer(setId, 102) succeeds although #102 never moved, and assess(102) returns TRANSFERRED; the plugin says 'Do not pay: the agent changed owner since it was certified' (verdict.ts:68) instead of UNTRUSTED. This lasts until the next certificate, and the certifier does not react to a third-party CertificateSubmitted (it is not in REGISTRY_EVENTS). Control with the correct fp: proveTransfer reverts NothingToProve. The agent has zero mass, so it is never payable either way: only the refusal reason is wrong. Anchor fingerprints are never read (assess and proveTransfer look up agentKey only), so for anchors the only effect is a garbage vectorAt lane and vectorRoot malleability (feeds K7). Neither the indexer nor the watcher looks at ownerFp, so nothing flags it.
details_en.evidence: AnchoredReputation.sol:1187 `for (uint256 i = k; i < n; ++i)` (anchor records 0..k-1 skipped); :1191-1193 non-agent nodes must be 0 (only for i >= k); :1202 `if (mass && fp != uint160(identity.ownerOf(key & ID_MASK)) & LANE_MASK)` (zero-mass agents unchecked); :1735-1737 proveTransfer flags on any mismatch, mass not considered; :1419 F_TRANSFERRED => TRANSFERRED. ENCODING.md §3.1: 'ownerFp_i = uint160(ownerOf(agentId)) & (2^63 − 1) for an agent node; 0 for other nodes ... Registry-verified checks it for every agent of mass > 0'; §3.4 table '0 for other nodes'. Note: for zero-mass agents the code follows §3.4's 'mass > 0' restriction, but §7.3/proveTransfer then trusts an unchecked lane. Scratch: V4Verify.t.sol test_K11_zeroMassWrongFpThenProveTransfer and test_K11_control_correctFp (pass).
details_en.fix: Check i < k too (anchor fp must be 0), and either check ownerFp for every certified agent or make proveTransfer (and the TRANSFERRED status) ignore nodes without mass.

constats.titre: Contrôle de transfert strict conditionné à trust ≠ 0 au lieu de « masse > 0 »
constats.resume: Le `ownerOf` en direct (D35) ne tourne que si la somme pondérée arrondie `x.trust` est non nulle, alors qu'ENCODING §3.1/§6 dit « agent de masse > 0 ».
constats.scenario: k = 2, λ = 0,5/0,5, t = 1 wei : trust = 0 avec une masse > 0 ; après transfert, `assess` renvoie OK au lieu de TRANSFERRED (MESURÉ). L'agent n'est jamais trusted et le payeur répond NO_WALLET : seul le statut est faux.
constats.correctif: Conditionner sur la masse (OU des couloirs t déjà chargés) ou corriger ENCODING §3.1/§6 en « trust > 0 ».

details_en.summary: The strict-mode live ownerOf check runs only when x.trust != 0 (floored lambda-weighted sum), not for every agent of mass > 0 as ENCODING §3.1/§6 say, so a transferred agent whose t is non-zero but floors to trust 0 reports status OK instead of TRANSFERRED.
details_en.failure_scenario: k = 2, lambdas 0.5/0.5, strictTransfer, agent #101 certified with t^(0) = 1 wei (any t <= y is a valid sub-solution), so c_0 = floor(0.5 * 1) = 0 and trust = 0 while mass > 0 (its fp was checked at submission at the Registry-verified level). #101 is transferred: assess(101) returns status OK instead of TRANSFERRED (V4Verify.test_K13_massPositiveTrustZeroTransferredShowsOK); with t^(0) = 2 wei (trust 1) it returns TRANSFERRED (control). The agent is never trusted (trustLow >= theta > 0 needs trust > 0), and TrustGatedPayer._policy (l.454-456) checks the wallet first, which a transfer clears (NO_WALLET). Only when the new owner set a wallet does _ancreReason (l.514-516) give UNTRUSTED instead of ANCRE_STATUS/TRANSFERRED. So only the reported status/reason is wrong.
details_en.evidence: AnchoredReputation.sol:1421 `if (!moved && s.strictTransfer && x.trust != 0) {` (comment: 'only when it can matter (a node without mass is never trusted)'); :1365-1366 trust = sum floor(lambda_a t / WAD); mass at submission = 'any t lane non-zero' (:1195-1201). ENCODING.md §6 'Transfer (D35): strict = live ownerOf for an agent of mass > 0'; §3.1 'In strict mode an agent of mass > 0 with a wrong or zero fingerprint is TRANSFERRED'.
details_en.fix: Gate on mass (OR of the t lanes already loaded in the loop) instead of x.trust, or change §3.1/§6 to say 'trust > 0'.

constats.titre: Message d'erreur du plafond de gas : chiffre v0 (« 12 k arêtes ») environ 20 fois trop haut
constats.resume: Le message cite « an update breaks around 12 k edges at k = 3 », tiré de l'historique v0 de GAS.md sans date ni étiquette ; pour un set Registry-verified le chiffre actuel est d'environ 630 arêtes sous 30 M (CALCULÉ, GAS.md).
constats.scenario: Une mise à jour Registry-verified d'environ 500 arêtes dépasse le plafond et l'opérateur lit que la limite est 20 fois plus loin ; même texte pour un lot `addNodes` trop gros (NODES600).
constats.correctif: Message dépendant du niveau et du type de transaction, avec les chiffres datés actuels, ou pas de chiffre.

details_en.summary: The operator-facing error for a transaction above tx_cap quotes 'GAS.md: an update breaks around 12 k edges at k = 3', an undated, unlabelled CALCULÉ figure from GAS.md's 'Historique R5 (contrat v0, 27/09)' section; for the certifier's default Registry-verified sets the current GAS.md figure is ~630 edges at k = 3 under 30 M (~480 under the 25 M cap), and the same text is printed when an addNodes or reserveCapacity chunk is the transaction over the cap.
details_en.failure_scenario: Default SetConfig (registry_verified=True). A Registry-verified update of ~500 edges at k = 3 estimates ~24 M (45.5 k/edge, GAS.md P1, MESURÉ 28/09) -> limit ~25.8 M > 25 M -> RuntimeError '... (GAS.md: an update breaks around 12 k edges at k = 3; beyond, the verification must be split)': the operator is told the break point is ~20-25x farther than it is. Even for Submitter-attested v1 the slope is ~4.1 k/edge (GAS.md v1 table: 1 382 551 at E = 300 -> 12 578 055 at E = 3 000), i.e. ~5.5 k edges under the cap, not 12 k. The NODES600 case (addNodes chunk over the cap) gets the same irrelevant explanation.
details_en.evidence: certifier.py l.590-591: `raise RuntimeError(f"{tx.fn}: gas limit {lim} > cap {self.cfg.gas.tx_cap} (GAS.md: an update breaks " "around 12 k edges at k = 3; beyond, the verification must be split)")`. GAS.md l.105 '## Historique R5 (contrat v0, 27/09) — conservé pour comparaison', l.126 'La mise à jour, elle, casse vers **12 k arêtes à k = 3**'; current section l.78 '(CALCULÉ, pente mesurée, avis unique) : (30 M − 1,3 M) / 45,5 k ≈ **630 arêtes à k = 3**'. SetConfig l.96 `registry_verified: bool = True`. CLAUDE.md §2: 'ne jamais reprendre un chiffre sans le sourcer et le dater. Marquer explicitement mesuré / auto-déclaré / estimé / non vérifié.'
details_en.fix: Make the message depend on the set level and tx kind, with the current dated GAS.md figures (Registry-verified ~630 edges at k = 3 under 30 M, CALCULÉ 28/09; addNodes ~45.9 k/node, MESURÉ 01/10), or simply print the estimate and point to GAS.md without a number.

constats.titre: `--identity`/`--reputation` jamais comparés aux registres du contrat
constats.resume: Les registres qui déclenchent le recalcul sont des entrées libres : avec les adresses mainnet sur le testnet (le piège documenté dans CLAUDE.md §3), `eth_getLogs` renvoie [] sans erreur et tous les déclencheurs se taisent.
constats.scenario: Seuls le premier tour et le rafraîchissement à environ 22 h subsistent ; rien n'est journalisé (vérifié sur testnet-rpc le 06/10).
constats.correctif: Lire `identity()`/`reputation()` sur le contrat au démarrage (ou refuser un écart).

details_en.summary: The registries whose events trigger recomputation (--identity/--reputation) are free CLI inputs never compared with AnchoredReputation.identity()/reputation() (public immutables), so a wrong pair, e.g. the mainnet vanity addresses on the testnet (the trap CLAUDE.md documents), makes every registry trigger silently dead: only the start round and the maxAge - refreshLead refresh remain.
details_en.failure_scenario: Testnet certifier started with --identity 0x8004A169... --reputation 0x8004BAa1... (mainnet addresses) against a contract built on 0x8004A818.../0x8004B663...: registry_events queries addresses without code, eth_getLogs returns [] with rc 0 (checked 06/10 on testnet-rpc for the last 100 blocks), evs is always empty, nothing is journaled, relevant() never runs. Revocations, wallet changes, transfers, new endorsements and the registry 'Upgraded' event no longer trigger a recertification; the set is recomputed only when age > maxAge - refreshLead (268 000 blocks, ~22.5 h at 0.302 s/block). Requires an operator mistake; no repo script invokes certifier.main with these flags.
details_en.evidence: certifier.py l.653-654: `ap.add_argument("--identity", required=True, help="IdentityRegistry address of the chain")`, `ap.add_argument("--reputation", required=True, ...)`; l.678 `registry_events(chain, a.identity, a.reputation, frm, head)`; no other use or check of a.identity/a.reputation. AnchoredReputation.sol l.214-215: `IIdentityRegistry8004 public immutable identity;` / `IReputationRegistry8004 public immutable reputation;`. CLAUDE.md §3/§7: testnet registries at 0x8004A818…/0x8004B663…, 'les adresses mainnet n'ont pas de code sur le testnet'. Probe: phase2/v7b_work/regaddr_probe.txt.
details_en.fix: Drop the two flags and read identity()/reputation() from the contract at startup (or ap.error when they differ).

constats.titre: Le `Signer` est construit différemment par le certificateur et le watcher
constats.resume: Le certificateur force le mode keystore dès `--send` (même sans `--keystore` ni `--from`), le watcher ne le prend que si `--from` et `--keystore` sont fournis ; aucun drapeau manquant n'est refusé par argparse.
constats.scenario: `certifier.py --send --from X` sans keystore : `TypeError` au premier envoi, à chaque tour ; sans `--from` : `AttributeError` à chaque tour ; le watcher, lui, envoie en `--unlocked` ou se contente de « préparer » ses preuves sans prévenir (reproduit).
constats.correctif: Un `signer_from_args()` commun : `--send` exige `--from`, keystore ssi `--keystore` (alors `--password-env` requis), jamais de rétrogradation silencieuse.

details_en.summary: certifier.main and watcher.main duplicate the same CLI/Signer plumbing (--rpc/--contract/--set-config/--set-id/--data/--from-block/--from/--keystore/--password-env/--send/--interval/--once) but build the Signer with different rules: the certifier forces mode 'keystore' whenever --send (even without --keystore or --from), the watcher picks keystore only if --from and --keystore are both given, else unlocked, else none; missing flags are never rejected by argparse.
details_en.failure_scenario: certifier.py ... --send --from 0xf39f... (no --keystore; the 'unlocked account on a local fork' mode the module docstring item 8 promises): Signer(mode='keystore', keystore=None, password_env=None); each round syncs, recomputes, estimates the first tx, then Chain._run -> Signer.env -> os.environ.get(None) raises TypeError 'str expected, not NoneType' (reproduced), journaled 'error' and retried forever; watcher.py with the same flags sends with --unlocked. certifier.py --send without --from: AttributeError ''NoneType' object has no attribute 'lower'' at check_submitter/estimate every round, whereas watcher.py --send without --from gets signer=None, so watch_once runs with send=False and prove() returns status 'prepared': the operator asked to 'REALLY send proofs' and nothing is sent, silently. Only misconfigured invocations are affected; the full --send --from --keystore --password-env path builds the same Signer in both.
details_en.evidence: certifier.py l.667-668: `signer = Signer(a.sender, "keystore", a.keystore, a.password_env) if a.send else (Signer(a.sender) if a.sender else None)`; watcher.py l.280-281: `signer = C.Signer(a.sender, "keystore", a.keystore, a.password_env) if a.sender and a.keystore else (C.Signer(a.sender) if a.sender else None)`, l.298 `send=a.send and signer is not None`, l.160-161 `if chain.signer is None: return {**res, "status": "prepared", ...}`; certifier.py l.198 `return ["--keystore", self.keystore]`, l.203 `os.environ.get(self.password_env, "")`, l.233 `self.signer.address.lower()`. Offline reproduction with the verbatim expressions: phase2/v7b_work/signer_probe.py.
details_en.fix: One shared signer_from_args(ap, a) used by both mains: --send requires --from (ap.error otherwise), keystore mode iff --keystore (then require --password-env), else unlocked; never silently downgrade --send to 'prepared'.

constats.titre: `replay_identity_events` garde l'owner courant dans pastOwners
constats.resume: La règle « anciens détenteurs hors owner courant » est appliquée par `load_identity` et `from_indexer.identity_file`, pas par `replay_identity_events`.
constats.scenario: Historique A→B→A : pastOwners {7: [A, B]} d'un côté, {7: [B]} de l'autre (reproduit) ; aucun cas dans le snapshot, aucune sortie calculée ne change, mais le test de parité casserait au premier cas réel.
constats.correctif: Faire le `discard` une seule fois dans `Identity.apply_transfer`.

details_en.summary: The rule that past holders exclude the current owner is applied separately by load_identity (graph.py:207) and from_indexer.identity_file (from_indexer.py:155-156), but not by replay_identity_events, even though all three replayers are supposed to share Identity.apply_*. The versioned-snapshot path and the indexer export therefore write a different pastOwners for an agent that came back to an earlier owner. No computed output changes.
details_en.failure_scenario: History mint->A, A->B, B->A for agent 7. replay_identity_events (the snapshot.py path) yields owner A, pastOwners {7: [A, B]}. from_indexer.identity_file on the same OwnerChange rows yields owner A, pastOwners {7: [B]}. Impact today is limited to that reports-only field. The versioned snapshot has 0 such agents (out of 72 with pastOwners). run_mainnet's 'ancien owner' measure (run_mainnet.py:346) iterates g.pairs, where R6 has already removed the current owner's pair, so even an A->B->A agent would not change it. tests/test_indexer_parity.py:41 compares the two past_owners maps and would start failing on the first snapshot that contains such an agent.
details_en.evidence: graph.py:128-131 apply_transfer adds `frm` to past_owners and never discards `to`; replay_identity_events:243-260 has no post-pass. graph.py:206-207 `# past_owners = détenteurs passés, hors owner courant` / `idn.past_owners = {t: {a for a in s if a != owner.get(t)} ...}`; from_indexer.py:155-156 `for a, s in idn.past_owners.items(): s.discard(idn.owner.get(a))`. PoC v7c_work/k24.py: "replay_identity_events: {'7': '0xaa..'} {'7': ['0xaa..', '0xbb..']}" vs "from_indexer.identity_file: {'7': '0xaa..'} {'7': ['0xbb..']}"; 'snapshot agents with current owner in pastOwners: 0'.
details_en.fix: Do the discard once in Identity.apply_transfer (self.past_owners.get(agent_id, set()).discard(to) after adding frm) and drop the two ad-hoc copies in load_identity and identity_file.

constats.titre: `dec_to_wad` dans le contexte Decimal par défaut (28 chiffres)
constats.resume: Une borne de plus de 28 chiffres significatifs une fois mise à l'échelle WAD est arrondie puis passe le contrôle d'intégralité ; le miroir `rules.ts` est exact et lève : les deux divergent sur un tel schéma.
constats.scenario: « 12345678901.000000000000000001 » perd 1 wei, « …0000000000000000001 » (19 décimales) est accepté par Python et refusé par rules.ts (MESURÉ) ; sans effet avec le schéma livré.
constats.correctif: Parser exactement (Fraction ou contexte local avec piège Inexact), règle des 18 décimales comme rules.ts.

details_en.summary: graph.dec_to_wad multiplies in Python's default 28-digit Decimal context, so a tag bound with more than 28 significant digits once scaled to WAD is rounded and then passes the integrality check. A representable bound loses precision, and a non-representable one (19+ decimals) is accepted instead of raising. The TypeScript mirror rules.ts decToWad is exact and throws in that case, so the reference and the indexer disagree on such a schema.
details_en.failure_scenario: Take a schema bound "12345678901.000000000000000001". dec_to_wad returns 12345678901000000000000000000 (1 wei lost), and that rounded value is what make_set_block commits in the setId and what quantize uses, while rules.ts decToWad returns ...0001. The bound "12345678901.0000000000000000001" (19 decimals) is accepted by the solver and rejected by rules.ts ('bound not representable in WAD'). This needs a bound of at least 1e10 written with full 18-decimal precision. The shipped schema_reference.json tops out at '1000000000000' (one significant digit), so it is cosmetic today.
details_en.evidence: graph.py:304-308 `d = Decimal(str(s)) * WAD` / `if d != d.to_integral_value(): raise ...` / `return int(d)` (default context, prec=28). export.py:148 commits `"min": str(schema[t].min_wad)` (the rounded value). rules.ts:24-31 parses with BigInt and `if (frac.length > 18) throw`. PoC v7c_work/dec.py: 'DEC28 12345678901.000000000000000001 -> 12345678901000000000000000000' and '12345678901.0000000000000000001 -> 12345678901000000000000000000', while '0.1234567890123456789 -> raises'. v7c_work/dec28.mts (real rules.ts): '-> 12345678901000000000000000001' and '-> throws bound not representable in WAD'.
details_en.fix: Parse bounds exactly: Fraction(Decimal(s)) * WAD with a denominator == 1 check, or a local decimal context with enough precision and the Inexact trap on; mirror rules.ts' 18-fraction-digit rule.

constats.titre: `synthetic.metrics` : la colonne « lignes pour e ≤ θ » est sous-évaluée
constats.resume: `rows_needed` traite ntrunc comme un nombre de nœuds massifs tronqués alors qu'il indexe un tri où les nœuds sans masse viennent en premier.
constats.scenario: deg = 2 : 1 445 lignes publiées contre 1 656 réellement gardées (−12,7 %, MESURÉ) ; les chiffres deg = 5 de RESULTS.md et du CR sont trop bas d'environ 6 lignes ; la conclusion (la troncature ne gagne presque rien) se renforce.
constats.correctif: `rows_needed = (mx[order[ntrunc:]] > 0).sum()`, puis régénérer out/synthetic.md et les chiffres cités.

details_en.summary: In synthetic.metrics, rows_needed = #massive − min(ntrunc, #massive) treats ntrunc as a count of truncated massive nodes. But ntrunc indexes argsort(mx), where every zero-mass node sorts first. The column 'lignes pour e ≤ θ' of out/synthetic.md is therefore under-reported by the number of zero-mass nodes, and it can drop to 0 when ntrunc ≥ #massive. 'arêtes pour e ≤ θ', computed from order[ntrunc:], is correct.
details_en.failure_scenario: Seed 0, N_H = N_S = 1000, g = 10, α = 1/3 (PoC wA/t4_synthetic_rows.py, re-run). deg=2 has 211 zero-mass nodes and reports 1445 rows, while 1656 nodes are really kept (order[ntrunc:]): −12.7 %. deg=5 reports 1845 vs 1851, deg=10 reports 1707 vs 1709. The deg=5 figures quoted in solver/RESULTS.md ('1 802 à 1 983 sur 1 996') and CR-conseil ('1 973 lignes sur 1 996') are low by about 6 rows. The conclusion drawn from them (truncation barely helps, AM-R4.5) only gets stronger once corrected, so no decision is affected. The published deg=2 rows are wrong by ~12 %.
details_en.evidence: synthetic.py:103-111 `mx = t.max(1)`; `order = np.argsort(mx)`; `ntrunc = int(np.argmin(ok)) if not ok.all() else n`; `rows_needed = int((mx > 0).sum()) - min(ntrunc, int((mx > 0).sum()))`; `kept = order[ntrunc:]`; `edges_needed = int(outdeg[kept].sum())`. Zero-mass nodes add 0 to cum, so they always lie inside order[:ntrunc], and rows_needed = n − ntrunc − #zero instead of n − ntrunc. PoC output: 'deg=2: zero-mass nodes=211, reported rows=1445, rows actually needed=1656, kept nodes (order[ntrunc:])=1656'. out/synthetic.md:13 '| 2 | 10 | 1/4 | ... | 1792 | 1556 | 11388 |'.
details_en.fix: rows_needed = int((mx[order[ntrunc:]] > 0).sum()) (the same kept set as edges_needed), then regenerate out/synthetic.md and the figures quoted in RESULTS.md and CR-conseil.

constats.titre: Watcher : le contrôle « ligne sans source vide » a été supprimé (commit 230be35)
constats.resume: La correction équivalente (écart SHAPE) n'a été ajoutée qu'à `indexer/src/lib/audit.ts` (12a2005) : le watcher saute en silence une ligne d'agent sans source qui porte des arêtes, c'est-à-dire la ligne d'attaque K6/L1.
constats.scenario: Certificat accepté via la désynchronisation K6 avec une ligne sans SRC portant une arête fabriquée : `discrepancies = []` côté watcher, SHAPE côté indexeur ; seule l'alerte est perdue (aucune preuve on-chain possible).
constats.correctif: Rétablir l'écart non prouvable avec alerte au journal ; la vraie correction est K6 (02-bis).

details_en.summary: Commit 230be35 deleted the watcher's check that a source-less agent row is empty (it emitted a SOURCE discrepancy when rows[u] was non-empty), while 12a2005 added the equivalent SHAPE discrepancy only to indexer/src/lib/audit.ts: watcher.audit now skips a source-less agent row that carries edges (`if client is None: continue`) without any discrepancy or journal entry, so the K6/L1 attack row is invisible in the bot's journal.
details_en.failure_scenario: A certificate accepted through the K6 _verifyRows desync (address node 0x02||address(0) with a non-empty row) commits, for agent #5 whose agentWallet is 0, a row without SRC carrying a fabricated +10000 edge to #6. watcher.audit: want = source_of(5) = (None, ''), have = (None, '') -> client None -> continue: discrepancies = [] (scratch phase2/v8_work/srcless.py), while the indexer audit reports SHAPE for the same row. Nothing can prove it on-chain (proveEdge BadProof(7), proveWallet NothingToProve: L1), so the bot's journal was the only place an operator could have seen it; impact limited to the lost alert and conditional on the K6 contract bug (otherwise _clientRare rejects such a row at both levels).
details_en.evidence: watcher.py:100-101 `if client is None: continue  # agent without source: an empty row, nothing else to audit`; git show 230be35 -- solver/watcher.py removes `if rows[u]: out.append(Discrepancy("SOURCE", u, None, "none", int(val), None, None))`; indexer/src/lib/audit.ts:90 SHAPE '// a source-less agent row MUST be empty' (12a2005). Contract: _clientRare (AnchoredReputation.sol:1168) reverts for H_NE != 0 on a source-less agent row, but _verifyRows l.1120 `if (client == address(0)) continue;` does not skip the row's edges (K6).
details_en.fix: Restore the check: when client is None and rows[u] is non-empty, emit a non-provable SHAPE/SOURCE discrepancy (with a journal alert) mirroring audit.ts; the root fix is K6 in the contract (02-bis).

constats.titre: `check.ts` s'arrête sur une page courte au lieu d'une page vide
constats.resume: FORMAT.md §7 impose l'arrêt sur page vide (from_indexer.py le fait) ; sous un plafond de lignes serveur inférieur à 1 000, `check.ts` ne lit que la première page.
constats.scenario: Fausse alerte d'incohérence de l'indexeur (jamais un faux vert) dès qu'un rôle Hasura plafonne les lignes.
constats.correctif: Arrêt sur page vide, une seule règle de pagination pour les deux clients de l'interface.

details_en.summary: check.ts's keyset paginator stops on a SHORT page (`page.length < 1000`), whereas the same GraphQL interface's specified reader stops on an EMPTY page so that a server-side row cap below 1 000 cannot truncate silently; under such a cap check.ts reads only the first page of every entity and reports a false indexer inconsistency.
details_en.failure_scenario: With a Hasura row cap R < 1000 on the queried role (self-hosted config or a stricter Cloud permission), all('Feedback'), all('OwnerChange') and all('WalletChange') return R rows each: getClients/getLastIndex mismatches, 'Σ getLastIndex 9283 != indexed feedbacks R' and the mint-count check fail, exit code 1, while from_indexer.py reads the same endpoint completely. The direction is a false alarm, never a false green; with today's Envio Cloud endpoint the check was green (README.md:38), so the trigger is a configuration change.
details_en.evidence: check.ts:46-58: `limit: 1000` ... `out.push(...page); if (page.length < 1000) return out; last = page[page.length - 1]!.id;`. solver/FORMAT.md §7 (l.146): 'Pagination stops on an empty page (a server-side row cap below 1 000 must not truncate silently).' solver/from_indexer.py:69-86 GraphQLSource.rows: `if not page: return out` (docstring 'Stops on an EMPTY page, not on a short one'). Unchanged at a8eefc5.
details_en.fix: Stop on an empty page in check.ts (one shared paginator rule for both clients of the interface, and say so in SCHEMA.md 'Access').

constats.titre: `check.ts` ne vérifie que ce que l'indexeur a déjà vu
constats.resume: La liste des agents et couples vient des avis indexés : un agent dont tous les avis ont été manqués n'est jamais interrogé, et ni valeur, ni tag1, ni révocation ne sont comparés.
constats.scenario: Une révocation manquée laisse l'arête active dans SetEdge et dans l'export (le certificat est ensuite refusé par la relecture) alors que `pnpm check --full` reste vert ; le tag tronqué de NUL passe aussi.
constats.correctif: Appeler `getClients` pour chaque agent minté et comparer chaque avis indexé (au moins le dernier par triple) à `readFeedback` via Multicall3.

details_en.summary: The live consistency check derives its list of agents and couples from the indexed feedbacks themselves, so an agent whose feedbacks were all missed is never queried and 'Σ getLastIndex == #feedbacks' only holds over indexed couples; it also never reads value, tag1 or revocation status, so a missed FeedbackRevoked or a corrupted tag passes with ok:true.
details_en.failure_scenario: The indexer misses the only NewFeedback(s) of agent N (e.g. a HyperSync/range gap): N is absent from clientsOf, so neither getClients(N) nor getLastIndex(N, c) is called, sumChain and fbs.length both exclude it, and the report is ok:true (a missing client of an agent that keeps at least one indexed feedback IS caught by getClients). A missed FeedbackRevoked leaves revokedAtBlock null: the edge stays active in SetEdge and in the from_indexer export, the certifier commits it and the Registry-verified re-read reverts EdgeMismatch, while `pnpm check --full` (README 'What it proves: live consistency with the registries') stays green; the NUL-stripped tag of candidate NUL also passes.
details_en.evidence: check.ts:86-87 fetches only `agent_id client feedbackIndex blockNumber` of Feedback; :99 `const agents = [...clientsOf.keys()];` (agents with an indexed feedback only); :113-117 getLastIndex only for indexed couples; :121 `sumChain += r.result ?? 0n` over those couples, :128 compared with fbs.length; ABI :29-35 has no readFeedback/isRevoked, so value/valueDecimals/tag1/revocation are never compared. The identity part already enumerates every minted agent (:134-148) and could drive getClients for all of them. README.md:82 presents the script as the live consistency proof.
details_en.fix: Call getClients for every minted agent (from OwnerChange), and compare each indexed feedback (or at least each latest per triple) with readFeedback (value, decimals, tag1, isRevoked) through Multicall3.

constats.titre: `publish.sh` : la garde avant `rsync --delete` accepte un sous-dossier du clone, `.git` compris
constats.resume: La garde se contente d'un `grep` de la sous-chaîne « ygk94/ancre-indexer » dans l'URL d'origine, vrai pour tout dossier à l'intérieur du clone.
constats.scenario: `scripts/publish.sh ~/ancre-indexer/.git` remplace le `.git` du clone par les sources de l'indexeur : historique local et commits non poussés détruits (reproduit sur un clone de test) ; avec `…/src`, une copie imbriquée est poussée sur la branche publique. Erreur d'opérateur requise.
constats.correctif: Exiger que DST soit la racine du work-tree (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) et une URL d'origine exacte.

details_en.summary: The safety check before `rsync -a --delete` only greps the output of `git -C "$DST" remote get-url origin` for the substring 'ygk94/ancre-indexer', which succeeds for any directory inside such a clone, its .git directory included, and for any origin URL merely containing that substring, so a mistyped destination is wiped.
details_en.failure_scenario: `scripts/publish.sh ~/ancre-indexer/.git` passes the guard and rsync --delete replaces the clone's .git with the indexer sources: local history and unpushed commits are destroyed (reproduced on a scratch clone: afterwards `git log` -> 'not a git repository'). `scripts/publish.sh ~/ancre-indexer/src` passes too: the clone's src/ is replaced by a nested copy of the indexer, which is installed, tested, staged by `git add -A` (whole tree from a subdirectory) and pushed to the public main (with --deploy also to `envio`, spending one of the free-plan deployments on a broken layout). Operator error is required.
details_en.evidence: publish.sh:12-13 `git -C "$DST" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null | grep -q "ygk94/ancre-indexer" || { ...exit 1; }` then :14-16 `rsync -a --delete ... "$SRC/" "$DST/"` (the 'P test/vectors/' filter protects DST-relative paths only), :35 `git add -A`, :41-42 pushes. Reproduced in phase2/v9_work/pub (local scratch repo, origin URL set but never contacted, only the guard and the exact rsync line run): 'guard PASSES for .../clone/.git', 'guard PASSES for .../clone/src', 'guard refuses .../clone/nonexistent'; after the rsync, .git contains config.yaml and src, and `git -C clone log` fails. Same result as the finder's phase1/d3/fakeclone.
details_en.fix: Require DST to be the work-tree root (`[ "$(git -C "$DST" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" = "$(cd "$DST" && pwd -P)" ]`) and match the origin URL exactly (e.g. `(^|[:/])ygk94/ancre-indexer(\.git)?$`).

constats.titre: `decodeRows` plus strict que le contrat sur les sources nulles (plantage déjà corrigé)
constats.resume: Une ligne d'ancre avec H_SRC et 20 octets à zéro (acceptée on-chain, K10) fait lever `decodeRows` ; le handler l'attrape désormais (`ancre.ts:131-133`, déjà corrigé pour le plantage) mais classe le certificat UNDECODABLE et ne l'audite pas. À l'inverse, une ligne sans source encodée avec SRC = 0x0 produit une fausse alerte SOURCE dont le remède revert `NothingToProve`.
constats.scenario: Un soumetteur tiers ajoute ces 20 octets à une ligne d'ancre d'un certificat par ailleurs fautif : accepté on-chain, jamais audité par l'indexeur (test sur le code actuel). Le solveur honnête n'émet jamais ce cas.
constats.correctif: Traiter un SRC nul comme « pas de source » dans `decodeRows` (ou signaler SHAPE au lieu de lever).

details_en.summary: decodeRows is still stricter than the contract on zero sources: an anchor row with the SRC bit and 20 zero bytes (accepted on chain, K10) makes it throw, and the new CertificateSubmitted handler now catches that and files the directly-submitted certificate as UNDECODABLE (no crash any more, but no audit); conversely a source-less agent row encoded with SRC = 0x0 (also accepted on chain) is decoded as source '0x0' and reported as a SOURCE discrepancy whose remedy, proveWallet, reverts NothingToProve.
details_en.failure_scenario: Open set, a third-party submitter calls submitCertificate directly with row u=0 (anchor) carrying hdr 0x8000|nE + 20 zero bytes: the contract accepts it (_clientRare only rejects a non-zero wallet on anchor/address rows), decodeRows throws EncodingError 'anchor row with SRC/VIA_OWNER', ancre.ts:131-134 sets status UNDECODABLE, 0 Discrepancy rows, SetHealth UNAUDITED: any dilution or omitted negative elsewhere in that certificate is never reported by the live audit, and the UNDECODABLE label ('not called directly') is false. Second case (scratch test): an honest certificate plus an empty row for agent #2 (no wallet) encoded with SRC = 0x0 is AUDITED with [SOURCE, u=3, client 0x0, proof proveWallet] and the set shows DISCREPANCY, while proveWallet would revert NothingToProve (_sourceHolds returns true for a zero committed source and a zero wallet). The honest solver never emits a zero SRC (export.py:194-207), so only a crafted submission triggers either case.
details_en.evidence: The crash consequence of the original candidate is already fixed: ancre.ts:119-134 wraps decodeRows/auditRows in try and `if (!(e instanceof EncodingError)) throw e; status = "UNDECODABLE";` (l.132-133). Still present: certificate.ts:64 `if (hdr & SRC) { ... src = toHex(b.subarray(o, o + 20)) ... }` (zero bytes give a truthy '0x00..0') and :71 `if (k !== undefined && u < k && (src || viaOwner)) throw new EncodingError(...)`; ancre.ts:120 passes k = set.anchors.length. Contract: AnchoredReputation.sol:1152 fast path only for wallet != 0; :1167-1170 agent row with wallet 0 = source-less; :1179 anchor/address rows only reject wallet != 0. audit.ts:92-95 reports SOURCE when row.src ('0x0') !== client (undefined). proveWallet: AnchoredReputation.sol:1699 + _sourceHolds:1831-1833 -> NothingToProve. Scratch tests on the current handlers (phase2/v9_work/ix/test/v9.test.ts): 'DECODE-anchor UNDECODABLE 0 UNAUDITED 0', 'DECODE-agent AUDITED [["SOURCE",3,"0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000","proveWallet"]] DISCREPANCY'.
details_en.fix: Mirror the contract exactly: treat a zero SRC as 'no source' in decodeRows (or report SHAPE instead of throwing), so the row is audited and a zero source is never reported as SOURCE.

constats.titre: `--max-amount ""` supprime le plafond sans erreur
constats.resume: `inp.maxAmount ? parseUsdc(...) : undefined` (pay.ts:31, inspect.ts:30, override.ts:72) traite une chaîne vide comme « pas de plafond », alors que toute autre valeur invalide lève ANCRE_BAD_AMOUNT. Même motif pour `--amount` dans check.ts:31.
constats.scenario: `--max-amount "$CAP"` avec CAP vide : une offre à 250 USDC est retenue (MESURÉ) ; pour `pay`, `maxPerPayment` borne encore, pour l'override rien d'autre que la lecture humaine.
constats.correctif: Tester `!== undefined` et rejeter la chaîne vide (un helper `optionalUsdc()` commun).

details_en.summary: `inp.maxAmount ? parseUsdc(inp.maxAmount) : undefined` (pay.ts:31, inspect.ts:30, override.ts:72) treats an explicitly empty --max-amount as 'no cap'. oclif and the host's resolveInputs hand '' to the command, while any other malformed amount is rejected with ANCRE_BAD_AMOUNT.
details_en.failure_scenario: An agent runs `mm ancre pay $URL --agent-id 12 --max-amount "$CAP" --confirm` with CAP empty (a templating slip; SKILL.md tells it to pass the approved amount). It could also be `--max-amount=`. Through the real @oclif/core 4.14 parser + schemaToFlags + resolveInputs, inp.maxAmount is "", maxAmount becomes undefined, and selectOffer keeps a 250 USDC offer (v6_work/poc/d3e_maxamt.mjs). With '0.01' the same offer gives ANCRE_NO_OFFER, and 'abc' gives ANCRE_BAD_AMOUNT. The guard against a server raising its price between inspect and pay is gone without any message. For pay, the payer's maxPerPayment still caps the amount (selectOffer, then the contract's OVER_LIMIT). For override (payerCap = false), only the human's own reading of the amount in the terminal and in MetaMask remains. check.ts:31 has the same pattern for --amount ('' -> 0n, so OVER_LIMIT is never tested).
details_en.evidence: pay.ts:31 `maxAmount: inp.maxAmount ? parseUsdc(inp.maxAmount) : undefined`; inspect.ts:30 and override.ts:72 identical; config.ts:43 parseUsdc('') would throw ANCRE_BAD_AMOUNT (regex /^\d+(\.\d{1,6})?$/). PoC output: `["--max-amount",""] inp.maxAmount="" -> maxAmount=undefined -> 250 USDC offer: 250000000`.
details_en.fix: Use `inp.maxAmount !== undefined ? parseUsdc(inp.maxAmount) : undefined`, so that '' is rejected as ANCRE_BAD_AMOUNT, in pay, inspect and override, and the same for check's --amount. Better still, one shared optionalUsdc(inp.x) helper.

constats.titre: `check` : une erreur RPC sur `getAgentWallet` devient WALLET_MISMATCH
constats.resume: `.catch(() => zeroAddress)` transforme une erreur passagère en `decide(agentId, 0x0, …)`, qui répond WALLET_MISMATCH pour un agent dont le wallet est bien posé.
constats.scenario: 429 ou délai dépassé sur `--rpc-url` : le skill annonce « payTo n'est pas le wallet de l'agent » pour une vérification sans offre.
constats.correctif: Remonter ANCRE_RPC_ERROR au lieu d'avaler l'erreur.

details_en.summary: checkFlow swallows every getAgentWallet error into zeroAddress, and the payer then reports WALLET_MISMATCH for a trusted agent instead of an RPC error.
details_en.failure_scenario: `mm ancre check 12` on a trusted agent whose agentWallet is set: the getAgentWallet read fails transiently (429 or timeout on rpc.monad.xyz via --rpc-url). .catch(() => zeroAddress) means decide(12, 0x0, 0) is called; TrustGatedPayer._walletCheck (TrustGatedPayer.sol:505) reads the real non-zero wallet, which is != 0x0, and returns WALLET_MISMATCH. The skill reports 'payTo is not the wallet of the agent the offer claims to be' for a check that has no offer at all. NO_WALLET is only correct when the registry itself returns 0 or reverts.
details_en.evidence: V3 verifier (partial save): CONFIRMED.
details_en.fix: Do not swallow the getAgentWallet error: surface ANCRE_RPC_ERROR, or call decide with the real wallet only when the read succeeded.

constats.titre: `check --naive` : un échec de la partie naïve fait perdre le verdict ANCRE
constats.resume: Les lectures `getClients`/`getSummary` ne sont pas isolées : une erreur RPC fait échouer toute la commande.
constats.scenario: Agent #182 (7 665 clients) : `getSummary` avec environ 245 ko de calldata dépasse une limite du RPC ou de la passerelle mm, la commande échoue et le verdict UNTRUSTED déjà calculé n'est jamais affiché, ce qui casse la scène de démo.
constats.correctif: Entourer la partie naïve d'un try/catch et rendre le verdict avec `naive.error`.

details_en.summary: In checkFlow --naive, any failure of the optional naive reads (getClients/getSummary over every client) throws and discards the ANCRE verdict already computed by decide.
details_en.failure_scenario: `mm ancre check 182 --naive` (the DEMO.md scene): getClients returns 7,665 clients, and getSummary is called with ~245 KB of calldata, reading every feedback. A 429 on the 25-rps RPC, or an eth_call gas or body limit on the mm gateway (ctx.publicClient), makes read() throw ANCRE_RPC_ERROR (flows.ts:74). The whole command fails and the UNTRUSTED verdict from decide (TrustGatedPayer.sol:226, flows.ts:92) is never shown; there is no try/catch around lines 94-109.
details_en.evidence: V3 verifier (partial save): CONFIRMED.
details_en.fix: Wrap the optional naive reads in try/catch and return the ANCRE verdict with naive.error instead of failing the command.

constats.titre: Sorties de `payFlow` non journalisées (GET payé qui échoue, signataire non opérateur, refus du wallet)
constats.resume: Quand le GET payé lève (connexion coupée après l'envoi de la signature, délai, Ctrl-C), `payFlow` rend UNKNOWN avec une autorisation vivante mais n'écrit rien au journal, contrairement à sa branche « 2xx sans PAYMENT-RESPONSE » et à override.ts:146 ; l'arrêt « signataire non opérateur » et un refus du wallet ne sont pas journalisés non plus (D47, commit c28f88d « chaque sortie journalisée »).
constats.scenario: Le serveur reçoit la signature, règle, puis coupe la connexion : journal vide (reproduit sur `dist` par trois agents), l'écran de démo ne montre rien alors que l'USDC a pu partir.
constats.correctif: Journaliser `unknown` dans ce catch et les autres sorties ; mieux, une seule fin de flux `settlePaid()` partagée avec l'override.

details_en.summary: payFlow returns outcome UNKNOWN with a live signed authorisation when the paid GET throws (connection dropped after the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE was sent, timeout, Ctrl-C abort) but writes NO journal entry, unlike its own 2xx-without-PAYMENT-RESPONSE branch (l.256) and override.ts:146; the non-operator-signer stop (l.220) and a wallet refusal/exception in signTypedData are not journaled either, contrary to D47 ('every refusal and payment is journaled') and commit c28f88d ('chaque sortie journalisée').
details_en.failure_scenario: `mm ancre pay <url> --confirm`: the server receives PAYMENT-SIGNATURE, settles, then drops the connection (or SIGINT aborts io.signal): d.fetch rejects, lines 239-240 return {outcome: UNKNOWN, signed: true, liveAuthorization} without d.journal (reproduced by three finders on dist with a throwing fetch stub: journal [] vs ['unknown'] for the 2xx case). `mm ancre journal` and the demo screen never show a payment whose USDC may have left the payer until validBefore, and SKILL.md tells the agent paid:false/signed:true means 'the settlement was refused (the gate working)'.
details_en.evidence: V3 verifier (partial save): CONFIRMED; also reproduced by A4 (a4/poc_pay.mjs) and SIMP (simp/plug/journal_gap.mjs). flows.ts:239-240 catch returns without j(...); flows.ts:256 j('unknown', ...); override.ts:146 j('override_unknown', ...).
details_en.fix: Journal 'unknown' in the paid-GET catch (and journal the non-operator and wallet-refusal exits); better, share one settlePaid() tail between payFlow and override.run.

constats.titre: Note d'override attachée à SETTLEMENT_FAILED alors que l'override refuse ce cas
constats.resume: Quand `explain` dit OK (échec du facilitateur, fenêtre expirée), `payFlow` ajoute quand même la note « seul l'humain peut passer outre », mais `override` répond ANCRE_OVERRIDE_NOT_NEEDED.
constats.scenario: Fenêtre x402 expirée après une MFA lente : l'humain suit la note et tombe sur une impasse.
constats.correctif: N'attacher la note que si le refus vient d'ANCRE.

details_en.summary: The human-override note is attached to SETTLEMENT_FAILED (a failure that explain says is not ANCRE's), but the override command refuses exactly that case.
details_en.failure_scenario: pay: the facilitator or server fails (expired window after a slow MFA approval, or a facilitator outage). explain returns OK, afterFailure gives SETTLEMENT_FAILED with pay:false, and flows.ts:269-270 adds HUMAN_OVERRIDE_NOTE ('Only the human may override this refusal'). The human runs `mm ancre override <url>`; inspectChallenge -> decide says PAY, and override.ts:74 throws ANCRE_OVERRIDE_NOT_NEEDED. The guidance points to a dead end, and the existing test (flows.test.mjs 'explain says OK') never checks that the note is absent.
details_en.evidence: V3 verifier (partial save): CONFIRMED.
details_en.fix: Attach HUMAN_OVERRIDE_NOTE only when the refusal is ANCRE's (explain reason != OK).

constats.titre: `--rpc-url` : la chaîne du RPC n'est jamais comparée à `--chain-id`
constats.resume: `hostDeps` crée un client sans chaîne et n'appelle jamais `eth_chainId` : `check` peut rendre le verdict de l'autre réseau sous le `--chain-id` demandé.
constats.scenario: `ANCRE_RPC_URL` testnet oublié, `mm ancre check 12 --chain-id 143` avec un payeur présent à la même adresse sur les deux réseaux : verdict testnet (PAY dans le PoC) rendu comme verdict mainnet. `inspect` échoue proprement, `payer status` lève ANCRE_WRONG_CHAIN, `pay` ne prend pas `--rpc-url` (MESURÉ).
constats.correctif: Créer le client avec la chaîne de `CHAINS[cfg.chainId]` et vérifier `getChainId()` une fois.

details_en.summary: With --rpc-url / ANCRE_RPC_URL, hostDeps builds `createPublicClient({ transport: http(rpcUrl) })` with no chain and never calls eth_chainId, so `check` (which reads only cfg.payer, never cfg.usdc) returns the verdict of whatever contract sits at the payer address on the RPC's network, under the --chain-id the user asked for.
details_en.failure_scenario: ANCRE_RPC_URL=https://testnet-rpc.monad.xyz left over from a rehearsal, then `mm ancre check 12 --chain-id 143 --payer P`, where P also has code on 10143 (CREATE address: same deployer key, same nonce on both networks): identity(), getAgentWallet and decide are read on the testnet payer and its testnet ANCRE, and the testnet verdict (PAY in the PoC) is returned with no ANCRE_WRONG_CHAIN; the result carries no chainId, so nothing reveals it. Reproduced with the real hostDeps + checkFlow against a fake RPC that says chainId 0x279f (v6_work/poc/k20_chain.mjs): verdict PAY, JSON-RPC methods seen = eth_call only. Scope narrower than stated: inspect fails closed (balanceOf(cfg.usdc) -> ANCRE_RPC_ERROR, because each chain's USDC address has no code on the other one, measured with cast code on 06/10), payer status throws ANCRE_WRONG_CHAIN (flows.ts:310) and pay never takes --rpc-url (pay.ts:28); override is the M4 case.
details_en.evidence: host.ts:14 `const client = rpcUrl ? createPublicClient({ transport: http(rpcUrl) }) : ctx.publicClient(cfg.chainId);` (no chain, no getChainId); flows.ts:89-92 checkFlow reads only cfg.payer/identity; statusFlow alone has the `getAddress(usdc) !== cfg.usdc` -> ANCRE_WRONG_CHAIN guard (flows.ts:310-312). PoC output: `check --chain-id 143 via a 10143 RPC -> PAY ... eth_chainId called: false`; `payer status -> ANCRE_WRONG_CHAIN`; `inspect -> ANCRE_RPC_ERROR balanceOf() failed on 0x7547...`. Low because the command is read-only, the trigger is a user misconfiguration plus a payer address shared by both networks, and pay/the payer contract are unaffected.
details_en.fix: In hostDeps, when rpcUrl is given, create the client with the chain of CHAINS[cfg.chainId] and check `await client.getChainId() === cfg.chainId` once (throw ConfigError ANCRE_WRONG_CHAIN otherwise); optionally reuse statusFlow's payer.usdc() == cfg.usdc check in check/inspect.

constats.titre: Ctrl-C n'arrête pas la page de signature de l'override
constats.resume: `humanSign` ne prend pas d'AbortSignal ; l'hôte transforme Ctrl-C en `io.signal.abort()`, que rien n'écoute.
constats.scenario: La page reste servie et la commande bloque jusqu'à 5 minutes ; si l'onglet est signé entre-temps, le flux reprend après une annulation (MESURÉ).
constats.correctif: Passer `d.signal` à `humanSign`, fermer le serveur et rejeter sur abort.

details_en.summary: humanSign takes no AbortSignal and override.ts does not pass io.signal to it. The host's renderer turns Ctrl-C into io.signal.abort() (it installs a SIGINT listener, so Node does not exit), so a human who cancels the override leaves the one-time signing page serving and the command blocked until the 5-minute timer fires.
details_en.failure_scenario: The human runs `mm ancre override <url>`, confirms, the page URL is printed, then presses Ctrl-C to cancel. The plain renderer's `process.on('SIGINT', l)` only calls t.abort(). Nothing in humanSign listens to it: the server keeps serving / and /template, and the promise settles only at the timeout (human.ts:88-93, 5 min by default). Measured with the built human.js and a host-like SIGINT handler (v6_work/poc/a4g_sigint.mjs): after SIGINT, signal.aborted = true, the page answers HTTP 200, /template still answers 200, and humanSign rejects only at timeoutMs. Repeated Ctrl-C does nothing more, and when the timer fires the host prints nothing because the signal is aborted. If the still-open tab is signed in the meantime, the flow resumes after a cancel. The paid GET then fails at once on the aborted signal (override.ts:144-147), and the result is OVERRIDE_UNKNOWN with 'Your signed authorisation can still be settled', although it was never sent. No funds are at risk.
details_en.evidence: human.ts:11-19 HumanSignRequest has no signal field; human.ts:55-99 no abort listener, only `setTimeout(..., req.timeoutMs ?? 5 * 60_000)`; commands/ancre/override.ts:68 `humanSign: (req) => humanSign({ ...req, onUrl: ... })` (no signal) while override.ts:55 passes `signal: base.signal` only to the fetches; host Command-gQSSC_E9.js plain renderer: `process.on('SIGINT',l)` with `l=()=>{c(),t.abort()}`, and `signal:t.signal` in io.
details_en.fix: Add `signal?: AbortSignal` to HumanSignRequest and pass d.signal from overrideFlow. On abort, clear the timer, close the server and reject with ANCRE_OVERRIDE_NOT_SIGNED 'cancelled'. Also check d.signal.aborted before going on after humanSign returns.

constats.titre: Double clic sur la page d'override : signature refusée avec un faux motif après « Signed »
constats.resume: Chaque GET `/template` réémet une autorisation (nouveau nonce) ; un second clic pendant la première demande fait vérifier la signature n1 contre le modèle n2.
constats.scenario: La page répond « Signed. You can close this tab », puis le terminal refuse avec « The signature does not come from the connected account » (MESURÉ). Rien n'est payé, mais l'humain est trompé et doit recommencer.
constats.correctif: Conserver les modèles émis par nonce et vérifier contre celui signé, ou un seul modèle par chargement ; ne répondre à `/done` qu'après acceptation.

details_en.summary: Each GET /template calls prepare() again, which draws a new nonce and window and overwrites `issued` both in human.ts and in override.ts. If the button is clicked a second time before /done, the human approves the first MetaMask prompt: the page replies 200 'ok' ('Signed. You can close this tab'), and override.ts then checks sig(n1) against the n2 template and refuses with the false message 'The signature does not come from the connected account'.
details_en.failure_scenario: The human clicks 'Connect MetaMask and sign' and does not see the signature popup, which often opens behind the window. They click again. The second handler gets accounts at once (the origin is now connected), fetches /template (nonce n2, override.ts:103-105 keeps n2) and queues a second signature request. The human approves prompt #1 (n1). human.ts:70-79 accepts the POST, answers 'ok' and resolves; override.ts:121-123 rebuilds the typed data with n2, the recovered address differs, and the result is ANCRE_OVERRIDE_BAD_SIGNATURE, journaled override_refused. Prompt #2 then fails 'Failed to fetch' because the server is closed. Re-run of a4/poc_dblclick.mjs on a fresh build: 'two templates, nonces differ: true', 'override error: ANCRE_OVERRIDE_BAD_SIGNATURE', page answered '200 ok'. Nothing is paid (fail-safe), but the human was told 'Signed', the terminal blames the wrong cause, and the human must start over. A true sub-second double click on a first connection is probably absorbed by MetaMask's -32002 'request already pending' on eth_requestAccounts (not tested in a browser). The click while the sign prompt is pending is the realistic trigger.
details_en.evidence: human.ts:66-68 `if (r.method === "GET" && u.pathname === "/template" && !settled) { issued = req.prepare(); ...}` (no once-guard); human.ts:76-79 replies `w.writeHead(200).end("ok")` before the plugin verifies; override.ts:103-106 `prepare = () => { issued = newAuthorization(..., d.random32()); ...}`; override.ts:120-123 verifies against `{ ...issued, from: signer }` and throws 'The signature does not come from the connected account'. HumanSignature.template (the human.ts copy) is never used by override.ts.
details_en.fix: Keep every issued template keyed by nonce and verify the posted signature against the template it signs (the page posts back td.message.nonce), or issue one template per page load. Answer /done only after the plugin has accepted the signature, so the page never says 'Signed' for a refused one.

constats.titre: `-f json` ou un format persistant contournent le refus « --json » de l'override
constats.resume: `MACHINE_OUTPUT` ne reconnaît que `--json`, `--toon`, `--format` ; l'alias `-f` de l'hôte et `mm config set format json` passent.
constats.scenario: `mm ancre override <url> -f json` : l'hôte choisit le rendu sans tête mais `isInteractive` répond vrai (MESURÉ avec les méthodes de `Command` de mm 7.0.0). Défense en profondeur seulement (la signature owner/treasury reste le vrai contrôle).
constats.correctif: Utiliser `io.isInteractive` fourni par l'hôte, en plus du test TTY.

details_en.summary: MACHINE_OUTPUT = /^--(json|toon|format)(=|$)/ misses the host's short alias and its persisted setting: `-f json`, `-f=json`, `-fjson`, `-f toon` and `mm config set format json` all make mm use the headless structured renderer, while isInteractive still returns true, so the override's documented 'refuses ... with --json' defence is bypassed.
details_en.failure_scenario: In a terminal (or a pty), `mm ancre override <url> -f json`. The host's base flag `format` has char 'f' (the ancre:override manifest lists format: char f, options text/json/toon). lastFormatFromArgv/resolveExplicitFormat return 'json', isExplicitHeadless is true, and the host runs the headless renderer (io.isInteractive = false). argv holds '-f' and 'json', the regex matches neither, and isInteractive(true, true, argv) returns true. The override proceeds with JSON output. Measured with the host's own Command.prototype methods, the @oclif/core 4.14 parser and the built interactive.js (v6_work/poc/a4e_format.mjs): for -f json / -f=json / -fjson / -f toon / config format=json the host is headless and the plugin says interactive. Only defence in depth (interactive.ts:2-4 and README say the binding check is the owner/treasury signature), but the README sentence 'refuses to run ... with --json' is false for these spellings, and test/override.test.mjs:182 covers only --json, --toon, --format=json and --format.
details_en.evidence: interactive.ts:6 `const MACHINE_OUTPUT = /^--(json|toon|format)(=|$)/;`; host @metamask/agent-wallet 7.0.0 dist/chunks/Command-gQSSC_E9.js: `baseFlags={format:j.Flags.string({char:'f',...options:[text,json,toon]})...}`, `lastFormatFromArgv` handles `--format`/`-f` X, `--format=`, `-f=`, `resolveConfiguredFormat(){let e=t('format')...}`, `shouldUsePlainRenderer(){return ve()&&!this.isExplicitHeadless()}`; the headless renderer passes `io.isInteractive:!1`, the plain one `isInteractive:!0`. commands/ancre/override.ts:39-40 builds argv from process.argv + ctx.argv only.
details_en.fix: Use the host's own decision: `io.isInteractive`, which is false whenever mm picked the headless renderer, by flag, alias or config, together with the stdin/stdout TTY check. Or at least match -f/-f=/-f<fmt> and the configured format. Add the alias cases to the test.

constats.titre: Override « mal configuré » refusé seulement si owner ET treasury sont des adresses de l'agent
constats.resume: Le README dit « owner OU treasury » ; le code ne refuse que si les deux sont bannis.
constats.scenario: owner = Agent Wallet, treasury = humain : l'override passe normalement ; l'agent, owner, peut même faire `transferOwnership(K)` sans 2FA (transaction vers le payeur autorisé par Guard Mode) puis faire accepter K comme humain (MESURÉ).
constats.correctif: Refuser si owner OU treasury est banni (ou corriger le README), et aligner `statusFlow.isHuman` (K21).

details_en.summary: overrideFlow refuses as misconfigured only when BOTH owner and treasury are banned (humans.length === 0). The README says the override is refused when the owner OR the treasury is an Agent Wallet address. A payer whose owner is the Agent Wallet therefore gets a normal override, with no ANCRE_OVERRIDE_MISCONFIGURED.
details_en.failure_scenario: A payer is set up with owner = the Agent Wallet and treasury = the human (README condition 4 broken: the agent can setPolicy, setOperator, unpause, transferOwnership). `mm ancre override <url>`: banned = {payer, operators, host wallets}, humans = [treasury], and the flow prints 'from YOUR OWN wallet (treasury)' and pays (OVERRIDE_PAID in v6_work/poc/a4f_owner.mjs) instead of surfacing the setup error the README promises. In that setup the agent, as owner, can also call payer.transferOwnership(K), a transaction to the allowlisted payer, so no 2FA. The override then accepts K, a key the agent holds, as 'the human' through the real gateway (same PoC: OVERRIDE_PAID human = K). This is the case the README rule was meant to exclude. payer status does flag owner = Agent Wallet (guarantee check ok:false), and in this setup the agent can already redirect the payer's own funds through setPolicy, so the override adds no new loss of funds.
details_en.evidence: override.ts:83-88 `const humans = [owner, treasury].map(getAddress).filter((a) => !banned.has(a)); if (humans.length === 0) throw new FlowError("ANCRE_OVERRIDE_MISCONFIGURED", "The payer's owner and treasury are the agent's addresses ...")`. README.md:87-88 'if the owner or treasury is itself an Agent Wallet address, the override is refused as misconfigured'. TrustGatedPayer.sol:346 `transferOwnership(address newOwner) external onlyOwner` (the treasury is immutable, TrustGatedPayer.sol:200).
details_en.fix: Throw ANCRE_OVERRIDE_MISCONFIGURED when owner OR treasury is in `banned` (as the README says), or correct the README to the 'both' rule. Either way, align statusFlow.isHuman with the same banned set (K21).

constats.titre: Offres au-dessus de `maxPerPayment` filtrées avant `decide` : OVER_LIMIT inatteignable
constats.resume: `selectOffer` écarte l'offre trop chère et lève ANCRE_NO_OFFER avec un indice trompeur (« exact USDC only »), sans entrée de journal ni note d'override, contrairement au SKILL.md.
constats.scenario: maxPerPayment 0,01 USDC, offre à 0,02 : pas de verdict OVER_LIMIT, pas de journal, alors que l'override est conçu pour ce cas.
constats.correctif: Ne pas filtrer sur `maxPerPayment` dans `selectOffer` : laisser `decide` répondre OVER_LIMIT, journaliser et proposer l'override.

details_en.summary: Offers above the payer's maxPerPayment are filtered before decide, so the OVER_LIMIT verdict documented in SKILL.md is unreachable from inspect/pay; the agent gets ANCRE_NO_OFFER with a misleading hint, no journal entry and no override note.
details_en.failure_scenario: maxPerPayment = 0.01 USDC and the provider asks 0.02. challenge() (flows.ts:136) passes maxPerPayment to selectOffer, which drops the offer and throws ANCRE_NO_OFFER with the hint 'ANCRE pays "exact" USDC on eip155:143 only' (x402.ts:96). decide/OVER_LIMIT (TrustGatedPayer.sol:455, verdict.ts:74) is never reached. payFlow never journals the refusal (contrary to D47 'every refusal is journaled') and shows no humanOverride, although the override is designed for exactly this case (payerCap=false).
details_en.evidence: V3 verifier (partial save): CONFIRMED.
details_en.fix: Do not filter on maxPerPayment in selectOffer: let decide return OVER_LIMIT, journal it and attach the override note.

constats.titre: Preuves : tout échec de lecture du registre vaut « agent brûlé » ou « source changée »
constats.resume: `proveEdge` (l.1652-1654) et `_sourceHolds` (l.1830) traduisent tout échec d'une lecture plafonnée à 120 k (revert quelconque, gas, retour court) en wNew = 0 ou en ligne annulée, alors que la soumission fait les mêmes lectures sans plafond. Un getter d'identité qui réussit mais coûte plus de 120 k après une mise à jour permettrait de « prouver » chaque arête supprimée jusqu'à STALE.
constats.scenario: Hypothétique : proxy UUPS mis à jour par l'EOA unique vers une implémentation plus coûteuse sans changer `getVersion()`. Aujourd'hui les quatre lectures d'une arête coûtent environ 45 k (GAS.md) et la v2.0.0 n'a pas de burn : le déclencheur est absent. La variante par famine de gas (63/64) n'est pas faisable.
constats.correctif: Ne traiter comme « pas d'agent » que le revert ERC721NonexistentToken et revert `RegistryUnreadable` sur tout autre échec, ou appliquer la même politique de gas à la soumission et aux preuves.

details_en.summary: proveEdge (l.1652-1654) and _sourceHolds (l.1830) treat any failure of a 120k-gas-capped identity read (revert of any kind, out of gas, short return) as 'agent does not exist / source changed', while submitCertificate makes the same identity reads as uncapped high-level calls, so an identity getter that succeeds but costs more than 120k gas would let anyone prove every committed edge as dropped and push the set to STALE.
details_en.failure_scenario: Hypothetical: the identity proxy (UUPS, upgradable by one EOA) is upgraded to an implementation whose isAuthorizedOrOwner or getAgentWallet costs > 120k gas for existing agents. If getVersion() changes, checkRegistry sets registryChanged and assess returns REGISTRY_CHANGED before STALE (l.1382 vs l.1386), so widening the old certificate has no visible effect; but after recertification under the new version (submission works, its identity calls are uncapped), every proveEdge on a committed edge gets okA/okW = false, so wNew = 0, and proveWallet voids agent rows, until eLowEff > eLowMax and all agents are STALE. If the getters revert outright, submission reverts too, so the widening is moot. Today the reads cost about 45k for all four registry calls of one edge (GAS.md), v2.0.0 has no public burn, and isAuthorizedOrOwner reverts only for nonexistent ids, so the trigger is not present.
details_en.evidence: l.1652-1654 `if (okA && okW && auth == 0 && address(uint160(wal)) != client) {...}` else wNew stays 0; l.1830 `if (!okW) return v.wallet == address(0);`; l.1586 `staticcall(VIEW_CALL_GAS, ...)` with VIEW_CALL_GAS = 120_000 (l.45); uncapped identity calls in submission at l.1130, 1153, 1169, 1174, 1202. Upstream IdentityRegistryUpgradeable v2.0.0 (scratchpad copy): isAuthorizedOrOwner = ownerOf + _isAuthorized, getAgentWallet never reverts, getVersion pure '2.0.0', no burn. The 63/64 gas-starvation variant is not feasible (the post-call work in proveEdge far exceeds 1/64 of 120k). Not tested; it would be confirmed by a mock identity whose isAuthorizedOrOwner burns > 120k gas: submitCertificate succeeds and proveEdge on a committed edge succeeds with wNew = 0.
details_en.fix: Treat only an ERC721NonexistentToken revert as 'no agent' (keeping proofs against fabricated edges to never-minted ids) and revert RegistryUnreadable on any other failure (out of gas, short return, other revert data), or use the same gas policy for submission reads and proof reads.

constats.titre: Pas d'annulation individuelle d'une autorisation upto (Permit2)
constats.resume: Le type 3 n'annule que les nonces EIP-3009 ; aucune fonction n'appelle `Permit2.invalidateUnorderedNonces` (indexé sur msg.sender, donc seul le payeur pourrait le faire) et `_parse` ne borne pas la deadline : une autorisation upto signée reste réglable tant que l'agent est trusted.
constats.scenario: L'opérateur signe un upto à deadline très lointaine puis veut le retirer : pause, retrait d'opérateur ou baisse du plafond bloquent, mais tout redevient valide dès que le levier est levé (MESURÉ). Déclencheur incertain : le plugin ne paie qu'en exact (fenêtre ≤ 300 s) et seul `scripts/t1.mjs` signe de l'upto.
constats.correctif: Ajouter `invalidatePermit2Nonces(wordPos, mask)` (owner ou opérateur), éventuellement borner la deadline dans `_parse`.

details_en.summary: The payer cannot revoke a single upto (Permit2) authorisation. Kind 3 only cancels EIP-3009 nonces, and no function calls Permit2.invalidateUnorderedNonces, which is keyed on msg.sender so only the payer itself could call it. _parse does not bound the deadline either, so a signed upto stays settleable by its facilitator whenever the agent is trusted before the deadline. The owner only has global, reversible levers.
details_en.failure_scenario: The operator signs AncreUptoPayment(cap 5000, deadline 2^256-1) for a trusted agent, then wants to retract it. Pausing, removing the operator, or lowering maxPerPayment below the cap each blocks it, but isValidSignature returns MAGIC again as soon as that lever is lifted (probe). An exact authorisation, in contrast, is killed for good by a kind-3 cancel. The trigger is uncertain: the shipped plugin pays exact only, with windows of at most 300 s, and only scripts/t1.mjs signs upto (deadline now + TTL). Confirming it needs an upto client that signs deadlines long enough for retraction to matter, or a spec requirement that every authorisation be revocable.
details_en.evidence: TGP:216 `if (p.kind == KIND_CANCEL) return _sigOk(p, blob) ? MAGIC : INVALID;`; kind 3 digest TGP:443 `CancelAuthorization(address(this), nonce)` in the USDC domain only. The payer touches Permit2 only in approvePermit2 (TGP:354-357, usdc.approve) and the nonceBitmap read (TGP:486-488); no invalidateUnorderedNonces call exists; the deadline TGP:416 is unbounded. Probe V2Probe.t.sol::test_k3_uptoAuthorisationRevivesAfterGlobalLevers (PASS): MAGIC -> setPaused(true) INVALID -> setPaused(false) MAGIC; setOperator(op,false) INVALID -> setOperator(op,true) MAGIC; setPolicy(setId,4999) INVALID -> setPolicy(setId,1e6) MAGIC; exact + kind-3 cancel -> 'authorization is used or canceled'. Trigger: plugin/src/lib/x402.ts:81 `if (o.scheme !== "exact")`, :121 MAX_TIMEOUT_S = 300; only plugin/scripts/t1.mjs:125-127 signs upto; the plugin never uses kind 3 either (no 'cancel' in plugin/src). Not documented either way (PAYER.md:46 lists kind 3 as EIP-3009 only).
details_en.fix: Add an invalidatePermit2Nonces(wordPos, mask), callable by the owner or an operator, that calls Permit2.invalidateUnorderedNonces from the payer; like kind 3, it moves no funds. Optionally also cap the upto deadline in _parse.

constats.titre: valueDecimals > 18 : le solveur lève là où le contrat ignore le tag
constats.resume: `value_to_wad` (et `rules.ts` quantize) lève pour valueDecimals > 18, alors que `_normalize` renvoie (false, 0) : un seul avis de ce type, dernier de son triple sur un tag filtré, ferait échouer `build_graph` pour tout le set.
constats.scenario: Inatteignable avec le registre v2.0.0 (`require(valueDecimals <= 18)`), atteignable après une mise à jour du proxy UUPS, scénario que le projet modélise (PLAUSIBLE).
constats.correctif: Faire rendre `None` (rejeté) à quantize comme `_normalize`, et pareil dans rules.ts (chantier 03).

details_en.summary: graph.value_to_wad raises ValueError for valueDecimals > 18, and so does the indexer mirror rules.ts quantize (line 61), whereas the contract's _normalize returns (false, 0): the tag yields nothing and the rest of the graph is untouched, as ENCODING §4 says ('valueDecimals > 18 ⇒ rejected'). One such feedback, when it is the latest non-revoked one of its (client, agent, tag1) on a filtered endorsement tag, therefore aborts build_graph for the whole set. Registry v2.0.0 rejects such feedback at write time, so the bug cannot fire today.
details_en.failure_scenario: Not reachable on ReputationRegistry v2.0.0 (giveFeedback: require(valueDecimals <= 18, "too many decimals")). It becomes reachable if the single-EOA UUPS proxy is upgraded to an implementation without that require, a scenario ANCRE explicitly models (Upgraded is always 'relevant', REGISTRY_CHANGED). Then build_graph raises 'valueDecimals hors [0,18]' in the certifier and the watcher on every round, so there is no recertification and the set goes STALE, while the contract would simply ignore that tag. A superseded or revoked dec>18 feedback is harmless: quantize only sees the latest one per triple.
details_en.evidence: graph.py:324-328 `"""... (dec <= 18 garanti par le registre)"""` / `if not 0 <= decimals <= 18: raise ValueError("valueDecimals hors [0,18]")`, called from quantize:339 and combine_pairs:454/461 with no try. AnchoredReputation.sol:1572-1573 `function _normalize(...) { if (dec > 18) return (false, 0);`, used in the re-read loop :1531 (the tag is marked seen and yields nothing). ENCODING.md:171 '(... valueDecimals > 18 ⇒ rejected)'. rules.ts:61 `if (decimals < 0 || decimals > 18) throw new Error("valueDecimals out of [0,18]")`. from_indexer.py:130 passes valueDecimals through unchecked. Registry source (scratchpad ReputationRegistryUpgradeable.sol:105) `require(valueDecimals <= 18, "too many decimals")`. PoC v7c_work/dec.py: 'DEC18 build_graph raised: ValueError valueDecimals hors [0,18]', while a later index on the same triple gives '2 edges'.
details_en.fix: Make quantize return None (rejected, counted in rejet_hors_bornes) when decimals is outside [0, 18], exactly like _normalize, and apply the same change to rules.ts quantize (chantier 03) so that the two mirrors stay identical.

constats.titre: Signature d'opérateur high-s : le plugin la laisse passer, le payeur la refuse
constats.resume: `_recover` refuse s > n/2 (documenté), mais `normalizeSignature` (plugin/src/lib/payer.ts:102) ne ramène jamais s dans la moitié basse, et le contrôle local du plugin (viem) accepte high-s : un tel paiement est signé, envoyé, puis refusé à /verify avec un motif trompeur.
constats.scenario: Si le signataire du wallet serveur ne normalise pas s, environ un paiement sur deux échoue en BAD_OPERATOR_SIG avec « mauvaise méthode de connexion ? ». Déclencheur inconnu : le keyring BYOK (viem) a produit 0 high-s sur 300 (MESURÉ), le mode serveur requis n'a pas pu être testé.
constats.correctif: Dans `normalizeSignature`, si s > n/2 : s = n − s et inverser v ; ou accepter high-s côté contrat (les nonces du jeton bornent déjà le rejeu).

details_en.summary: _recover rejects high-s operator signatures, as PAYER.md §2 ('low s') documents. But the plugin's normalizeSignature (plugin/src/lib/payer.ts:102) never canonicalises s, and the plugin's local check (viem recoverTypedDataAddress + isOperator, flows.ts:218-219) accepts high-s. A high-s signature from the wallet therefore passes the plugin and is refused at settlement as BAD_OPERATOR_SIG.
details_en.failure_scenario: Suppose the server-wallet signer returns s > n/2. pay signs, recovers the operator locally and sends the blob. USDC's isValidSignature returns 0xffffffff and the facilitator refuses. explain gives BAD_OPERATOR_SIG, and the agent is told 'the signing wallet is not an operator of this payer (wrong mm login method?)', plus a human-override note. The failure is closed (no funds move), and with a non-normalising signer it hits about half of all payments. Whether it triggers is unknown: mm's BYOK keyring (viem) produced 0 high-s signatures in 300, while the server-wallet mode required by README condition 1 signs remotely (Mimir) and the CLI relays that signature unmodified. Confirming it needs a few dozen AncrePayment signatures through mm in server-wallet mode, checking whether any has s > n/2.
details_en.evidence: TGP:530 `if (uint256(s) > HALF_N || (v != 27 && v != 28)) return address(0);` (PAYER.md:37 "ECDSA, 65 bytes, low s, v ∈ {27, 28}"). plugin/src/lib/payer.ts:102-121: the 65-byte branch only maps v 0/1 to 27/28. Node probe scratchpad/phase2/v2_work/k5.mjs (viem 2.57.2, plugin dist): viem privateKeyToAccount.signTypedData gives 0/300 high-s; recoverTypedDataAddress on the high-s twin returns the operator; verifyTypedData on it returns true; normalizeSignature returns it unchanged. Forge V2Probe.t.sol::test_k5_highSValidForEcrecoverRefusedByPayer (PASS): ecrecover(high-s) == operator, isValidSignature INVALID, explain BAD_OPERATOR_SIG; the existing test_highSAndBadVRefused agrees. mm 7.0.0 (plugin/node_modules/@metamask/agent-wallet): BYOK = viem privateKeyToAccount (low-s); server mode = EvmServerAdapter.submitSignTypedData -> submitSignatureRequest(eth_signTypedData_v4), a remote black box. Outcome text: verdict.ts:76; override note: flows.ts:269-270. plugin/README.md Status: pay through the real executor is 'Not yet tried'.
details_en.fix: In normalizeSignature, when s > n/2 set s = n - s and flip v (27 <-> 28). Alternatively accept high-s in _recover: token nonces bound replay and `reported` is keyed by the token hash, so malleability is harmless here.

constats.titre: `nodeIndexPlus1` en mapping : une page MIP-8 froide par nœud
constats.resume: Chaque nouvel agent paie sa propre page (environ 28,5 k gas MESURÉ, environ 60 % du coût d'`addNodes`) ; les agentId sont denses et petits.
constats.scenario: Un tableau à indexation directe (u32 compactés) coûterait 36 à 56 % de moins sur `addNodes` (MESURÉ en micro-benchmark).
constats.correctif: Tableau aligné sur les pages pour les agents, mapping conservé pour les adresses.

details_en.summary: The reverse node index nodeIndexPlus1 is a nested mapping, so every new agent node pays a fresh slot on its own cold MIP-8 page: 28.5k gas measured, about 60 % of addNodes' 45.9k per node. Agent ids in the node table are u32 and dense on mainnet, so a page-aligned direct-indexed array of packed u32 lanes would cost 2.8k (consecutive ids) to 15.6k (one id per slot) per node, and reads would still touch a single cold page.
details_en.failure_scenario: Micro-benchmark of _appendNodes' check-then-write pattern (network = monad, isolated txs, 200 inserts): mapping 28,528 gas per key; 8 x u32 per slot at base + (agentId >> 3): 2,769 per id (consecutive) and 15,552 per id (stride 7). On GAS.md's split first certificate (addNodes 22.96 M for 500 nodes, MESURÉ) that is about 13 M (-56 %) saved per 500 consecutive ids and about 8 M (-36 %) per 500 scattered ids (ESTIMATED with ~12k per id for 1,237 ids spread over 1..10,262). Each addNodes transaction would then hold about 1.5-2.3x more nodes. Reads (_assess AR:1353, proveTransfer AR:1722, _sums AR:1847) still cost one cold page. This is an efficiency gain, not a defect.
details_en.evidence: AR:218 `mapping(bytes32 => mapping(bytes32 => uint256)) public nodeIndexPlus1;`; written per node in _appendNodes AR:476 `if (m[key] != 0) revert NodeExists(key);` + AR:480 `m[key] = ++n;` (plus the contiguous key slot AR:478), agent ids decoded as u32 at AR:467; anchors AR:296. GAS.md:40 'newNodes : ≈ 46 k par nœud en v1, deux slots par nœud, mapping et clé contiguë ; le v0 ... 28,8 k'; GAS.md:55 'addNodes : 22,96 M pour 500 nœuds (≈ 45,9 k par nœud) ... MESURÉ'; GAS.md AM-R5.3 '28,7 k par nouveau nœud (une page de mapping par clé)' (cost acknowledged, no alternative layout evaluated). Re-ran effbench/test/Scan.t.sol::test_reverseIndexLayouts: `mapping 200 keys|5727428|per key=28528`, `packed 200 dense ids|601387|per id=2769`, `packed 200 ids stride 7|3145187|per id=15552`. No off-chain consumer reads the public getter (grep over *.py/*.ts: only AR uses nodeIndexPlus1). Caveat for the fix: cheaper node insertion also makes AM-R5.7 / A1b junk-node padding of permissionless sets cheaper by the same ratio.
details_en.fix: For KIND_AGENT nodes, keep index + 1 in a page-aligned per-set array of packed u32 lanes at keccak('ANCRE.idx.v1', setId) & ~127 + (agentId >> 3) and keep the mapping for anchor and address nodes; add a nodeIndexOf(setId, key) view if a getter is needed; weigh this against AM-R5.7 (junk-node cost).

constats.titre: Dix fonctions Yul jumelles W=2/W=4, dont les copies W=4 ne sont exercées par aucun test
constats.resume: validate/scatterPos1/scatterPosK/scatterNeg/vetoMark existent en deux versions qui ne diffèrent que par les décalages et le pas ; cinq fonctions paramétrées par W, appelées avec un 2 ou un 4 littéral, donnent un bytecode identique.
constats.scenario: Environ 50 lignes dupliquées dans la boucle chaude ; un correctif fait sur une jumelle et mal reporté sur l'autre partirait sans test.
constats.correctif: Fusionner en cinq fonctions paramétrées par W et ajouter un vecteur W = 4 à la suite de tests.

details_en.summary: _rowLoop carries ten twin Yul functions (validate2/4, scatterPos1_2/4, scatterPosK_2/4, scatterNeg2/4, vetoMark2/4) that differ only in the dst/weight shift amounts (240/224 vs 224/208) and the edge stride (8 vs 10); five W-parametrised functions (shD = 256 - 8W, shW = shD - 16, step = W + 6) called with the literal 2 or 4 from the existing switch arms compile to byte-identical bytecode, and the W = 4 copies are executed by no test or vector.
details_en.failure_scenario: About 50 duplicated lines in the verifier's hot loop (merged file: 2,004 vs 2,054 lines). The W = 4 twins only run when a submitter sends rows with W = 4 (export.py picks W = 4 only for n > 0xFFFF, the contract also accepts W = 4 for small n), and no Solidity test or vector ever does: a fix made to the W = 2 twin and not ported by hand, with its different shift constants, to the W = 4 twin ships untested. The merge costs 0 gas (identical bytecode).
details_en.evidence: AR:769-832 (W = 2: `shr(240, wd)` dst, `shr(224, wd)` w, `add(p, 8)`) vs AR:834-896 (W = 4: `shr(224, wd)`, `shr(208, wd)`, `add(p, 10)`), otherwise token-identical; call sites AR:924-926, 949-961, 968-970 already `switch W case 2 {..} default {..}`. Rebuilt myself (forge 1.8.3, solc 0.8.28, via_ir, optimizer 200, repo foundry.toml) the repo file and the finder's merged variant (diff reviewed line by line: only the merge, plus one comment dropped): creation and runtime bytecode without CBOR metadata are byte-identical (runtime 33,409 bytes, sha256 3b6ea59932cd... for both; scratch phase2/v5b_work/{orig,spec}, cmpbc.py). No W = 4 anywhere in the tests: every encoding in contracts/test is CertLib.encodeRows(g, 2) / rowBytes(.., 2) / leaves(g, 2) (Profile, RegistryBench, AnchoredReputation, Gas, Fuzz, Verified, Upgrade, Fork, TrustGatedPayerFork, Base._submit used by Diff.t.sol); the 13 `calldata.rows` blobs of solver/vectors (9) and solver/vectors/violations (4) all start with byte 0x02; no hand-crafted row blob with a 0x04 width byte; export.py:258 `W = 2 if n <= 0xFFFF else 4` and the largest test graph has 10,000 nodes.
details_en.fix: Replace each pair by one Yul function taking W (shD = 256 - 8W, shW = shD - 16, step = W + 6), keep the literal `switch W case 2 / default 4` at the call sites (same bytecode), and add one W = 4 test or vector (also covers K7's W = 4 acceptance).

constats.titre: Littéraux magiques dans le Yul au lieu des constantes
