constats.resume: `header()`, `processRow`, `factors`, `capLane` codent en dur 0x0fff, 256, 0x8000, 0x4000, 0x2000, 10000, 1e18, 0x7fff… alors que H_NE, ROW_MAX, H_SRC, H_SPLUS, H_ALIAS, GRID, WAD, LANE_MASK sont utilisables en Yul.
constats.scenario: Un changement de format fait sur les constantes laisserait `_rowLoop` lire l'ancien format pendant que `_verifyRows`/`_parseRow` lisent le nouveau (classe de défaut de K6).
constats.correctif: Utiliser les constantes dans le Yul (bytecode identique).

details_en.summary: The Yul functions of _rowLoop and _storeVectors hard-code the row-format and arithmetic constants: 0x0fff, 256, 0x8000, 0x4000, 0x2000 in header(), 10000 in processRow (and 10000 / 20000 in validate2/4), 1e18 in factors(), 0x7fffffffffffffff in capLane(). H_NE, ROW_MAX, H_SRC, H_SPLUS, H_ALIAS, GRID, WAD and LANE_MASK can all be used inside these Yul functions, and substituting them gives byte-identical bytecode.
details_en.failure_scenario: The §3.2 row header is decoded three times (K26): the Solidity decoders _verifyRows (AR:1109-1119) and _parseRow (AR:1767-1777) use H_SRC/H_SPLUS/H_ALIAS/H_NE, while the Yul header() uses the bare literals. Change a flag or the H_NE width in the constants (an ENCODING v2) and _verifyRows/_parseRow follow it while _rowLoop keeps the old layout. The compiler raises no error, and the arithmetic pass and the Registry-verified re-read / proofs then parse rows differently (K6 failure class). It is maintenance risk only, with no gas cost either way.
details_en.evidence: AR:982 `let nE := and(hdr, 0x0fff)`, AR:983 `if gt(nE, 256) { failRows(4) }`, AR:986 `and(hdr, 0x8000)`, AR:991 `and(hdr, 0x4000)`, AR:997 `switch and(hdr, 0x2000)`, AR:935-936 `if lt(bP, 10000) { bP := 10000 }`, AR:907 `div(tsum, 1000000000000000000)`, AR:1241 `if gt(x, 0x7fffffffffffffff) { y := 0x7fffffffffffffff } // LANE_MASK`; constants AR:39-61 (`ROW_MAX = 256`, `WAD = 1e18`, `GRID = 10_000`, `LANE_MASK = (1 << 63) - 1`, `H_SRC = 0x8000`, `H_SPLUS = 0x4000`, `H_ALIAS = 0x2000`, `H_NE = 0x0fff`). The same file already uses constants in other assembly blocks (AR:718 LANE_MASK, AR:1255/1275 SENTINEL). The finder's substituted variant (8 literals in factors/processRow/header/capLane replaced by WAD, GRID, H_NE, ROW_MAX, H_SRC, H_SPLUS, H_ALIAS, LANE_MASK; diff reviewed) compiles (so the constants are accepted inside Yul functions), and I rebuilt it myself: creation and runtime bytecode without metadata are byte-identical to the repo file (phase2/v5b_work/{orig,cons}, cmpbc.py). Overlaps K26 (three header decoders); the literal-vs-constant drift is the part added here.
details_en.fix: Use H_NE, ROW_MAX, H_SRC, H_SPLUS, H_ALIAS, GRID, WAD and LANE_MASK inside the Yul functions (for 20000, mul(2, GRID) or a named constant). Better still, merge the three header decoders (K26).

constats.titre: En-tête de ligne décodé trois fois
constats.resume: La disposition §3.2 est décodée par le `header()` Yul de `_rowLoop`, par `_verifyRows` et par `_parseRow`. Les copies ont déjà divergé : K6 est exactement l'oubli de `_verifyRows`.
constats.scenario: Tout changement de format est à faire dans trois décodeurs ; un oubli désaligne la relecture du registre et la règle de forme alors que les feuilles Merkle restent justes.
constats.correctif: Un `_rowHeader(rows, off, W) → (RowView, next)` partagé par `_verifyRows` et `_parseRow` (ou faire enregistrer par `_rowLoop` l'offset des arêtes de chaque ligne).

details_en.summary: The §3.2 row layout (u:W, hdr, [SRC 20], [SPLUS 4], [ALIAS ref W], edges of W+6) is decoded three times: the Yul header() of _rowLoop, _verifyRows (a second pass with its own offset arithmetic) and _parseRow.
details_en.failure_scenario: The copies have already diverged: K6 is exactly _verifyRows's copy forgetting to skip the nE edges of a client-0 row (l.1120). _verifyRows also has none of header()'s structural checks (row order, u < n, end of buffer) and relies on _rowLoop having run first. Any format change has to be made in three decoders; a miss misaligns the registry re-read and the shape check, while the Merkle leaves (from _rowLoop) stay right.
details_en.evidence: AnchoredReputation.sol:975-1021 (header(): u, hdr, nE, SRC, SPLUS, ALIAS ref, edge range), 1104-1125 (_verifyRows re-decodes u, hdr, SRC, SPLUS skip, ALIAS skip, nE, edges), 1763-1785 (_parseRow).
details_en.fix: One Solidity `_rowHeader(rows, off, W) -> (RowView, next)` shared by _verifyRows and _parseRow (or have _rowLoop record each row's edge offset/client info for _verifyRows); the Yul hot path can stay specialised.

constats.titre: Chemin de forme seule : poids et index décodés avant le `continue`
constats.resume: Dans `_verifyRows`, le chemin `reads = false` (tous les certificats Submitter-attested) décode w et feedbackIndex avec des slices vérifiées avant `if (!reads) continue`.
constats.scenario: Environ 820 gas par arête, 18 à 20 % d'une mise à jour attestée (MESURÉ).
constats.correctif: Ne lire que dst sur ce chemin et sauter W+6 octets ; lire w/fIdx avec `_be` sur le chemin Registry-verified.

details_en.summary: In _verifyRows every edge decodes its weight and feedbackIndex with checked calldata slices (rows[off+W:off+W+2], rows[off+W+2:off+W+6]) before `if (!reads) continue`, so on the shape-only path (every Submitter-attested certificate) they are decoded and bounds-checked for nothing. _rowLoop has already proven that every row lies inside `rows`. Skipping them costs a measured 820 gas per edge, 18-20 % of an attested update.
details_en.failure_scenario: Submitter-attested update of an existing certificate (x -> x, network = monad, isolated transactions): E = 300 / n = 100 / k = 3 costs 1,376,573 gas against 1,130,473 with a `!reads` branch that only checks the dst kind and steps W + 6 bytes (-17.9 %). E = 3,000 / n = 1,000 / k = 3 costs 12,525,290 against 10,064,290 (-19.6 %). Both sizes save 820 gas per edge. On Monad the submitter pays the gas limit, and the per-transaction certificate ceiling of the attested level grows by the same fraction. The Registry-verified path pays the same checked-slice overhead, although rows were already bounds-checked (not measured).
details_en.evidence: AR:1121-1128 `for (uint256 e; e < nE; ++e) { uint256 dst = _be(rows, off, W); int256 w = int16(uint16(bytes2(rows[off + W:off + W + 2]))); uint256 fIdx = uint32(bytes4(rows[off + W + 2:off + W + 6])); off += W + 6; uint256 dk = _keyAtBase(kb, dst); if (dk >> 248 != KIND_AGENT) revert EdgeMismatch(ri, e); if (!reads) continue;`: w and fIdx are used only after the continue (AR:1129-1135). Rows are already bounds-checked by _rowLoop before _verifyRows runs (AR:512-513; AR:1030 `if gt(next, end) { failRows(5) }`, AR:1041 `if iszero(eq(off, end)) { failRows(6) }`). Re-ran effbench/test/ShapeLoop.t.sol::test_shapeLoop (effbench AnchoredReputation.sol, Base.t.sol, CertLib.sol and Mocks.sol identical to the repo; the variant AnchoredReputationV.sol only inserts the `if (!reads) { for edges: kind check via _be; off += step } continue;` block; set from Base._policy: registryVerified false, submitters [this]): `current=1376573 variant=1130473 saved/edge=820` and `current=12525290 variant=10064290 saved/edge=820`. Distinct from K26 (row header decoded three times). Note: the extra slice checks are not a guard either. With the K6 desync they can only turn some misparsed rows into reverts, and K6 needs its own fix.
details_en.fix: In _verifyRows, branch on `reads` before decoding the edge. The attested path checks only the dst kind and does `off += W + 6`; the verified path reads w and fIdx with the unchecked _be helper, as _rowLoop already bounds-checked the rows (best done together with the K26 header merge).

constats.titre: R6, R7 et l'empreinte d'owner écrits deux fois, avec des politiques d'échec différentes
constats.resume: Contrôleurs (R6) dans `_verifyRows` et `proveEdge`, résolution de source (R7) dans `_clientOf/_clientRare` et `_sourceHolds`, `& LANE_MASK` en ligne à trois endroits alors que `ownerFingerprint()` existe. La soumission revert sur un échec de lecture, les preuves le traduisent en « brûlé » (K14).
constats.scenario: Un changement D20/D44/D10 appliqué à une seule copie laisserait les preuves facturer des arêtes que la soumission refuse (ou l'inverse).
constats.correctif: Helpers internes `_isController`, `_sourceOf`, `ownerFingerprint()` partout, chacun avec une politique d'échec explicite.

details_en.summary: R6 (controller rejection), R7 (source resolution) and the owner fingerprint are each implemented twice or more: R6 in _verifyRows and proveEdge, R7 in _clientOf/_clientRare and _sourceHolds, and `& LANE_MASK` on ownerOf inline at three sites although ownerFingerprint() exists.
details_en.failure_scenario: The arithmetic is the same today, but the failure semantics already differ: _verifyRows uses high-level calls that revert on a registry failure, while proveEdge and _sourceHolds map a failed read to 'not a controller / burnt / changed' (K14). A future D20/D44/D10 change applied to only one copy would let proofs bill edges that submission refuses (or the reverse). A fingerprint change made in _verifyOwners but not in _assess would make every certified agent TRANSFERRED in strict mode.
details_en.evidence: AnchoredReputation.sol:1130 `identity.isAuthorizedOrOwner(client, j) || identity.getAgentWallet(j) == client` vs 1652-1654 (_staticWord, `okA && okW && auth == 0 && address(uint160(wal)) != client`); _clientOf/_clientRare 1146-1182 vs _sourceHolds 1827-1838; `uint160(identity.ownerOf(key & ID_MASK)) & LANE_MASK` at 1202, `(o & LANE_MASK)` at 1423 and 1736, vs `ownerFingerprint(address)` 2051-2053 (public pure, callable internally). FORMAT.md R6/R7 (l.26-27).
details_en.fix: Shared internal helpers `_isController(client, j) -> (ok, bool)`, `_sourceOf(j, row)` and ownerFingerprint() at every site, each with one explicit failure policy.

constats.titre: `getAgentWallet`/`ownerOf` rappelés sans cache dans `_verifyRows`
constats.resume: Un appel par arête entrante et par ligne, plus `ownerOf` par agent massif, alors que le registre ne peut pas changer dans la transaction.
constats.scenario: Environ 1 k gas par appel redondant, 2 à 4 % du certificat de démo (MESURÉ/CALCULÉ).
constats.correctif: Un tableau mémoire wallet[n] rempli au premier usage.

details_en.summary: Registry-verified _verifyRows calls identity.getAgentWallet(j) once per incoming edge of j (AR:1130) and again for j's own row (_clientOf AR:1153), with no per-node cache. All registry calls are STATICCALLs inside one view pass, so the value cannot change between them. ownerOf is called once per massive agent in _verifyOwners (AR:1202), which is redundant only with the VIA_OWNER row check (AR:1174).
details_en.failure_scenario: Demo act-2 certificate (GAS.md P1: 300 edges, 100 nodes = 97 agents, k = 3, Registry-verified, 14.97 M gas MESURÉ): up to 300 per-edge + 97 per-row getAgentWallet calls for at most 97 distinct agents, so about 300 redundant warm calls. Each costs 1,042 gas on the ERC-1967 proxy mock (measured); the real v2.0.0 getter also hashes the 'agentWallet' metadata key, so 0.3-0.6 M gas, 2-4 % of the certificate (ESTIMATED). A hub agent with 200 incoming committed edges alone wastes about 200k. The verifier works correctly; this is gas only, paid by the submitter (on Monad, at the gas limit).
details_en.evidence: AR:1130 `if (identity.isAuthorizedOrOwner(client, j) || identity.getAgentWallet(j) == client) {` inside the per-edge loop (getAgentWallet evaluated whenever the client is not a controller, i.e. for every honest edge); AR:1153 `if (reads && identity.getAgentWallet(key & ID_MASK) != wallet) revert EdgeMismatch(ri, ROW_MAX);` per agent row; AR:1174 `identity.getAgentWallet(j) != address(0) || identity.ownerOf(j) != wallet` (VIA_OWNER rows); AR:1202 `identity.ownerOf(key & ID_MASK)` per massive agent. IERC8004.sol declares ownerOf/getAgentWallet/isAuthorizedOrOwner `view` (STATICCALL), and _verifyRows is `internal view`. Real getter (scratch IdentityRegistryUpgradeable.sol:126-130): `bytes memory walletData = $._metadata[agentId]["agentWallet"]; return address(bytes20(walletData));`. GAS.md:76 lists 'getAgentWallet(j)' per edge plus 'getAgentWallet(u)' per agent row in the per-edge decomposition (cost acknowledged, not optimised). Re-ran effbench/test/Scan.t.sol::test_warmWalletCall: `warm repeated getAgentWallet via ERC-1967 proxy, per call=1042`.
details_en.fix: Keep a memory cache uint256[n] of wallet | 1 << 160 per node index, filled on first use, shared by the row SRC check (AR:1153/1169/1174) and the per-edge controller check (AR:1130); optionally cache ownerOf for VIA_OWNER rows reused by _verifyOwners.

constats.titre: Adressage des couloirs de vecteurs recopié à 4 endroits
constats.resume: slot = base + (i>>2)·(k+3) + v, décalage (i&3)·64, & LANE_MASK : écrit en ligne dans `_assess`, `proveTransfer`, `_setFlag` et `_widen` en plus de `vectorAt` (externe, donc non réutilisable tel quel).
constats.scenario: Cohérent aujourd'hui ; un changement de disposition (nouveau couloir, pas k+4) demande environ sept modifications, et un oubli dans `_setFlag` écrirait les bits de transfert et de veto dans le couloir d'un autre nœud sans revert.
constats.correctif: Un helper interne `_lane(setId, k, i)` utilisé partout, `vectorAt` compris.

details_en.summary: The vector-lane address (slot = _vecBase(setId) + (i >> 2) * (k + 3) + v, shift (i & 3) * 64, & LANE_MASK) is written out inline in _assess, proveTransfer, _setFlag and _widen, in addition to vectorAt.
details_en.failure_scenario: Consistent today. The layout is also hard-coded in _storeVectors, reserveCapacity and certifier.plan (stride k + 3), so changing it (another lane, a stride of k + 4) means editing about seven places. If one is missed, for example _setFlag, the transfer bit and the V13 veto bit are OR-ed into another node's lane, and nothing reverts.
details_en.evidence: AnchoredReputation.sol:1357-1358 + 1363, 1371-1373 (_assess); 1725-1726 + 1731-1732 (proveTransfer); 1905-1906 (_setFlag); 1928-1929 + 1936 (_widen); 2014-2015 (vectorAt). vectorAt is `external`, so it cannot be reused as is: an internal helper is needed.
details_en.fix: One internal `_lane(setId, k, i) -> (slot0, shift)` (or `_laneSlot(setId, k, i, v)`) used by _assess, proveTransfer, _setFlag, _widen and vectorAt.

constats.titre: `_pairEdge` renvoie un `tag` qu'aucun appelant n'utilise
constats.resume: Le quatrième retour (suivi via minTag/maxTag) est jeté par les deux appelants.
constats.scenario: Variables de pile et gas inutiles dans la boucle D14 de chaque relecture (environ 50 à 190 gas, MESURÉ).
constats.correctif: Renvoyer (ok, w, idx).

details_en.summary: _pairEdge returns a fourth value `tag`, tracked through minTag/maxTag in the scan loop with an extra ts.hash read on each min/max update, and both callers discard it: `(ok, wt, idx,)` in _verifyRows and `(ok, wNew,,)` in proveEdge. Returning (ok, w, idx) does the same job.
details_en.failure_scenario: Dead work in the D14 loop that runs on every Registry-verified edge re-read and every proveEdge. Removing it lowers submitCertificate in Verified.t.sol by 67 gas on average (median -126, max -189) and proveEdge by 47 on average. The unused return also suggests a 'deciding tag' that the contract never reports (graph.py/SetEdge do report one).
details_en.evidence: AR:1506 `returns (bool ok, int256 w, uint256 idx, bytes32 tag)`, AR:1519-1520 `bytes32 minTag; bytes32 maxTag;`, AR:1533-1534 `(minW, minIdx, minTag) = (wt, j, ts.hash)` / `(maxW, maxIdx, maxTag) = (wt, j, ts.hash)`, AR:1542-1543 return them. Only two callers (grep `_pairEdge(`): AR:1133 `(bool ok, int256 wt, uint256 idx,) = _pairEdge(s, client, j);` and AR:1656 `(ok, wNew,,) = _pairEdge(s, client, agentJ);`. Re-ran the Verified.t.sol gas report on the repo copy and on the finder's 3-value variant (diff reviewed: exactly the removal): submitCertificate avg/median/max 266,350/248,015/510,271 -> 266,283/247,889/510,082; proveEdge avg 181,397 -> 181,350. All 129 local tests pass on the variant (Upgrade.t.sol fork setUp fails on every variant: pinned historical block not served by the RPC).
details_en.fix: Drop the `tag` return and minTag/maxTag (or report the deciding tag in EdgeMismatch/EdgeProven if it is wanted).

constats.titre: `proveWallet` appelle `_sums` complet pour n'utiliser que s0/b0
constats.resume: Lecture inutile de `nodeIndexPlus1[agentKey(0)]` (page MIP-8 froide) et boucle d'amendements ignorée ; formules capDim/prepaid dupliquées avec `proveEdge`.
constats.scenario: Environ 5 à 8 k gas par `proveWallet` (MESURÉ) ; un changement d'arrondi fait dans une seule preuve facturerait différemment le même fait.
constats.correctif: Un helper `_committedRow` partagé, `_sums` réduit à la superposition des amendements.

details_en.summary: proveWallet calls the full _sums(s, setId, e, eb, amends, 0) but reads only m.s0 and m.b0, which are computed before the amendment overlay. The nodeIndexPlus1[setId][agentKey(0)] lookup (a cold mapping slot, so a cold MIP-8 page) and the whole amendments loop are wasted. proveEdge and proveWallet also repeat the same plumbing (NoCert, _openRow, alias _openSource, _sums, capDim = ceil(S0/B0), prepaid = (sDecl - S0)/B0).
details_en.failure_scenario: Every proveWallet pays for a lookup of agent #0 and a scan of amendments it ignores. With an s0/b0-only helper the Verified.t.sol gas report gives proveWallet median 99,439 -> 94,551 (-4,888) and max 176,998 -> 168,538 (-8,460), and on Monad the prover pays its gas limit. The capDim/prepaid formulas are written twice (AR:1667/1673 and AR:1704/1707): a rounding change made in one proof and not the other would bill the same row fact differently.
details_en.evidence: AR:1703 `EdgeSums memory m = _sums(s, setId, e, v.isAlias ? src.row : r.row, amends, 0);` then only `m.s0`, `m.b0` are read (AR:1704 capDim, AR:1707 prepaid). _sums AR:1847 `uint256 jp1 = nodeIndexPlus1[setId][agentKey(agentJ)];` (agentJ = 0), AR:1856-1858 set s0/b0 before the AR:1860-1870 amendment loop, whose outputs (sP, sN, wOld, wCommitted) and jp1 proveWallet never reads. Duplicated plumbing: AR:1641/1695, 1643/1696, 1645/1702, 1649/1703, 1667/1704, 1673/1707. The amends are authenticated by st.h (AR:1801), so skipping the overlay changes no outcome. Re-ran forge test --match-path test/Verified.t.sol --gas-report (network = monad) on the repo copy and on the finder's `_committed(s, e, eb)` variant (diff reviewed: only that helper and the call): proveWallet min/avg/median/max 63,853/113,966/99,439/176,998 -> 63,850/109,610/94,551/168,538. All 129 local tests pass on the variant; the only failure is Upgrade.t.sol, which forks mainnet at a pinned block the RPC no longer serves (an environment problem, the same on every variant).

constats.titre: Code mort du solveur (périmètre réduit)
constats.resume: Mort : `ppr.distrust_float`, `ppr.U64_MAX`, `graph.GRID_WAD`, `Q_MAX`, le paramètre `lambdas` de `power_from_zero`, `rejected` dans `watcher.audit`, cinq imports, le drapeau `reject_controllers` (et la garde inatteignable de `row_of`). Pas mort : `ppr.is_trusted` (utilisé par `app/scripts/export_act1.py`) et `keep_detail` (utilisé par `indexer/analytics/survival_scan.py`).
constats.scenario: Environ 25 lignes inutiles dans la référence normative ; supprimer `is_trusted` ou `keep_detail` casserait l'export de l'acte 1 ou l'analyse de survie.
constats.correctif: Supprimer le code mort listé, garder `is_trusted` et `keep_detail`.

details_en.summary: Narrowed: real dead code in the solver (ppr.distrust_float, ppr.U64_MAX, graph.GRID_WAD and Q_MAX never referenced; power_from_zero's `lambdas` parameter unused; watcher.audit's `rejected = g.r6_pairs` never read; unused imports MODES in export.py, node_key in certifier.py, np/ANCHOR/solve_float in run_mainnet.py; build_graph/combine_pairs' reject_controllers is never passed by any caller, so row_of's 'boucle_ignoree' guard is unreachable), BUT two items of the candidate are wrong: ppr.is_trusted is called (app/scripts/export_act1.py computes the act-1 PAY bit with it, explicit theta/m/rho) and keep_detail=False is passed by indexer/analytics/survival_scan.py:191.
details_en.failure_scenario: Cost only: ~25 unreferenced lines, one unused parameter and 5 unused imports in the module that is the normative reference for rules.ts and the contract; the never-used reject_controllers=False switch is the only path on which the row_of self-loop guard can fire (under R6, src(j) is always a controller of j). Following the candidate literally would break code: deleting ppr.is_trusted makes app/scripts/export_act1.py fail with ImportError (the act-1 screen data), and deleting keep_detail makes indexer/analytics/survival_scan.py fail with TypeError.
details_en.evidence: grep over the repo: `distrust_float` (ppr.py:71), `U64_MAX` (ppr.py:31), `GRID_WAD` (graph.py:44), `Q_MAX` (graph.py:45) appear only at their definition; power_from_zero(n, anchors, aN, aD, rows, splus, lambdas, max_iter) never reads lambdas (ppr.py:265-291); watcher.py:74 `rejected = g.r6_pairs` is the only use; export.py:16 imports MODES, certifier.py:38 imports node_key, run_mainnet.py:21-25 imports np, ANCHOR, solve_float, none used afterwards; reject_controllers appears only in graph.py:417/470/493/507. Refuting the rest: app/scripts/export_act1.py:25 `from ppr import ... is_trusted ...` and :56 `if ci is not None and is_trusted(cert, ci, theta=THETA, m=M, rhoN=RHO_N, rhoD=RHO_D)` (journal 07.md:209: 'le bit PAY / REFUSE vient de ppr.is_trusted du solveur'); indexer/analytics/survival_scan.py:191 `graph.build_graph(fbs, ident, schema, filt, anchors=[], keep_detail=False)`. graph.py:536 itself says the guard is 'impossible under R6 ... kept as a guard'.
details_en.fix: Delete distrust_float, U64_MAX, GRID_WAD, Q_MAX, the unused imports, power_from_zero's lambdas, watcher.audit's `rejected`, and the reject_controllers flag (turn the row_of guard into an assert); keep ppr.is_trusted (used by export_act1; optionally read theta/m/rho from a SetConfig.policy()) and keep_detail.

constats.titre: `synthetic.py` réimplémente le solveur PPR flottant
constats.resume: `solve`, la borne de fuite, le leave-one-out et WAD sont recopiés ; le budget somme les poids signés (pas de B⁻ séparé).
constats.scenario: Identique aujourd'hui (écart 1,7e-18) car pas d'arête négative ; une seule arête négative fait diverger les deux (7,8e-6, MESURÉ) : l'étude de α ne porterait plus sur le modèle certifié.
constats.correctif: Importer `ppr.solve_float`, `leak_bound`, `trust_robust` et `graph.WAD`.

details_en.summary: synthetic.py re-implements, instead of importing them, the float PPR solver (solve ≈ ppr.solve_float), the leak bound (line 96-98 ≈ ppr.leak_bound), leave-one-out (line 91-92 ≈ ppr.trust_robust) and WAD (line 29 = graph.WAD). integer_check in the same file already imports graph/ppr, so reuse is possible. Its budget bp = max(1e4, Σ q) sums signed weights and keeps negative entries in C, unlike ppr/graph, which use B⁺ = max(GRID, Σ q⁺) for C and a separate B⁻ for D.
details_en.failure_scenario: The α measurements (D2, out/synthetic.md) come from this private copy. They match the reference only because the synthetic graphs have no negative edge. Measured on make_graph(seed 7, 150/150, deg 5, g 10): max |synthetic.solve − ppr.solve_float| = 1.7e-18, and the leak bounds are equal (0.0087751). After adding one slash edge (q = −10000), the two solvers differ by 7.8e-6. A slash scenario added to synthetic.py, or any change to the D5/D7/D32 conventions in ppr, would leave the α study on a different model from the certified one, and no test would fail.
details_en.evidence: synthetic.py:29 `WAD = 10**18`; :69-82 `def solve(...)`: `bp = np.maximum(10000, np.bincount(src, weights=q, minlength=n))`, `c = q / bp[src]`, power iteration identical to ppr.py:53-68; ppr._arrays:44-48 uses `g.bplus(u)` and `cw = e.q / bp if e.q > 0 else 0.0`. synthetic.py:96-98 bound = ((1−α)/α)·Σ comb[src]·c over edges into S from outside, the same formula as ppr.py:357-368. synthetic.py:91-92 `robust = srt[:, m - 1:].sum(1)` vs ppr.py:378-381 `sum(s[m - 1:])`. synthetic.py:164-165 `from graph import ANCHOR, AGENT, Edge, Graph` / `from ppr import certify, e_eff`. PoC v7c_work/k27.py output quoted above.
details_en.fix: Build a Graph (or pass arrays=(src, dst, cw, dw) with the reference budgets) and call ppr.solve_float / leak_bound / trust_robust and graph.WAD; delete the private copies.

constats.titre: Watcher : chemins Merkle en O(R²)
constats.resume: `audit()` reconstruit tous les niveaux de l'arbre pour chaque ligne (et chaque source d'alias).
constats.scenario: 1 000 lignes : 1,85 s contre 0,003 s ; 2 000 : 7,37 s (MESURÉ) ; environ 30 s à 4 000 lignes (CALCULÉ).
constats.correctif: Calculer `merkle_levels` une fois par audit.

details_en.summary: audit() builds a Merkle path for EVERY row (and a second one for each alias source) through _ref -> export.merkle_proof(leaves, pos), which recomputes merkle_levels(leaves) (all R leaves hashed up to the root) on each call, so auditing a certificate costs O(R^2) keccaks instead of O(R) once plus O(log R) per path, and paths are built even for rows with no discrepancy.
details_en.failure_scenario: Measured with the repo's merkle_proof (re-run of scratchpad/eff_merkle.py): R = 250 -> 0.11 s, 1 000 rows -> 1.85 s vs 0.003 s with the levels computed once, 2 000 rows -> 7.37 s vs 0.006 s; quadratic extrapolation ~30 s at 4 000 rows, i.e. one polling interval spent hashing before any proof is estimated, on every audit.
details_en.evidence: watcher.py:57-58 `_ref` calls merkle_proof(leaves, pos) for each row; l.87-88 call _ref for r and, for aliases, srow; export.py:52-61 merkle_proof loops over `merkle_levels(leaves)[:-1]`, and merkle_levels (l.34-44) rehashes the whole tree; watcher.py is the only caller.
details_en.fix: Compute `levels = merkle_levels(leaves)` once in audit() and slice each path from it (or build paths lazily, only for rows that get a provable discrepancy).

constats.titre: `recomputeEdgesInto` : un `await` séquentiel par arête entrante
constats.resume: Chaque changement de contrôleur d'un agent à N arêtes entrantes coûte environ 3N allers-retours de stockage enchaînés dans la phase de préchargement d'Envio ; les `get` répétés sont servis par le cache d'Envio.
constats.scenario: Sans effet sur les données réelles (2 arêtes entrantes au maximum) ; un contrôleur pourrait répéter `approve()` pour ralentir l'indexeur si N grandit.
constats.correctif: Charger Agent/AnchorSet une fois, calculer les décisions avec `Promise.all`, puis appliquer les écritures et un seul delta de stats.

details_en.summary: recomputeEdgesInto awaits recomputeRefEdge one SetEdge at a time, so every controller change (Transfer, agentWallet MetadataSet, Approval, and each owned agent on ApprovalForAll) of an agent with N incoming reference edges costs about 3N sequential storage round trips in Envio's preload phase instead of about 3; the repeated Agent/AnchorSet gets per edge are real in the code but are served from Envio's in-memory store, so they cost nothing.
details_en.failure_scenario: Agent J with N incoming 'ref' SetEdge rows: one approve(x, J) by its controller runs, per edge in turn, TripleLatest loads for every endorsement tag of the reference filter, then the matching Feedback rows, then Operator(owner-client) (edges.ts:21-25, view.ts:20-23), i.e. ~3N dependent rounds per batch. Real data is harmless (max 2 incoming SetEdge rows per agent in the Monad fixture; the 7 662-feedback farm uses tag 'eve', outside the filter); N only grows if N distinct clients each post a filter-tag feedback on J, after which every controller event of J adds ~3N ms-scale round trips to its batch (indexer lag, not a wrong result).
details_en.evidence: state.ts:94-98: `if ((await getAgent(context, agentId)).refEdgeRows === 0) return; const edges = await context.SetEdge.getWhere({ agent_id: { _eq: agentId } }); for (const e of edges) if (e.set_id === REF_SET) await recomputeRefEdge(context, e.client, agentId, block);` (line 97 now, 95 before the +2 lines of a8eefc5); recomputeRefEdge :68-73 re-gets Agent and AnchorSet('ref') per edge and edgeDecision :21 gets the Agent again. Envio LoadLayer.res:28-29/72-79 and LoadManager.call skip ids already in the in-memory store, and getWhere results are put in the store by id (LoadLayer.res:386-392), so those repeats and SetEdge.get(edgeId) are cache hits; the TripleLatest/Feedback/Operator loads of each edge are not, and the `await` in the loop serialises them. solver/tests/fixtures/indexer/SetEdge.json: 11 rows, at most 2 per agent.
details_en.fix: Load Agent/AnchorSet once, compute the edge decisions with Promise.all over the edges, then apply the SetEdge writes and ONE summed bumpStats delta (a naive Promise.all over recomputeRefEdge would race on ChainStats read-modify-write).

constats.titre: Plugin : classes d'erreur dupliquées, code mort, erreurs brutes qui échappent à `toCommandError`
constats.resume: FlowError, X402Error et ConfigError sont identiques ; `identityAbi` défini deux fois ; `HumanSignature.template` jamais lu ; `CHAINS[*].rpc` jamais lu. Les `Error` brutes de `normalizeSignature`/`encodeExactBlob` sortent sans code ANCRE_* (l'hôte propose alors « Run the command again », contraire à la règle « pas de retry »). Les helpers upto ne sont PAS morts (utilisés par `scripts/t1.mjs`).
constats.scenario: Environ 25 lignes dupliquées ou mortes ; chaque nouvelle classe d'erreur doit être ajoutée à `toCommandError` sous peine de perdre son code.
constats.correctif: Une classe `AncreError` unique et un `toCommandError` qui enveloppe toute autre erreur en ANCRE_INTERNAL ; garder les helpers upto.

details_en.summary: Plugin duplication and dead code, mostly as stated. FlowError, X402Error and ConfigError are three identical (code, message, hint) classes that toCommandError has to enumerate. identityAbi is defined twice. HumanSignature.template is filled but never read. CHAINS[*].rpc is never read. Plain Errors thrown on the payFlow path reach the host as code UNKNOWN with the hint 'Run the command again'. One part is wrong: the upto helpers are not dead, because scripts/t1.mjs uses them.
details_en.failure_scenario: Cost: about 25 duplicated or dead lines, not ~60. Each new error class must also be added to host.ts:75, or it escapes without its ANCRE_* code. That already happens to normalizeSignature (payer.ts:107/120, called at flows.ts:215) and encodeExactBlob (payer.ts:130). If the executor returns a signature that is neither 65 nor 64 bytes (a wrapped smart-account or ERC-6492 signature), the plain Error leaves toCommandError unchanged. The host (fatalError chunk `y`) maps it to code UNKNOWN with the hint 'Run the command again...', which goes against SKILL.md's no-retry rule. It is harmless here, since no authorisation has been sent yet. The ancreUptoTypedData / encodeUptoBlob / UptoAuthorization helpers (payer.ts:134-173) are imported by scripts/t1.mjs:20 and used at :127 for test T1's upto path, so they must stay.
details_en.evidence: flows.ts:43-47, x402.ts:27-31, config.ts:13-17 have identical bodies `constructor(readonly code: string, message: string, readonly hint: string) { super(message); }`; host.ts:75 `if (e instanceof FlowError || e instanceof X402Error || e instanceof ConfigError) ...; throw e;`; identityAbi at flows.ts:49-51 and x402-guard.ts:28-30 (same getAgentWallet entry); human.ts:22/79 set `template`, while override.ts reads only sig.address/sig.signature (override.ts:118-141) and keeps its own `issued`; CHAINS is read only at config.ts:26/37, which reads c.network and c.usdc and never c.rpc; grep of src/scripts/test: upto helpers used by scripts/t1.mjs:20,127 and test/lib.test.mjs:142-143.
details_en.fix: One AncreError(code, message, hint) class (the three as aliases), with toCommandError testing it once and wrapping any other Error as ANCRE_INTERNAL. Also share identityAbi, drop HumanSignature.template and CHAINS.rpc, and keep the upto helpers (used by T1).

constats.titre: owner ou treasury peuvent aussi être opérateurs
constats.resume: ÉCARTÉ : la séparation des rôles est la condition 4 de la garantie (README), vérifiée par `mm ancre payer status` ; seule la répétition T1 (testnet, oracle simulé) fusionne les rôles.
constats.scenario: Avec des rôles séparés, l'opérateur ne peut ni `sweep`, ni `setPolicy`, ni `setOperator` (MESURÉ).
constats.correctif: Défense en profondeur optionnelle : refuser owner/treasury = opérateur dans le constructeur et `setOperator`.

details_en.summary: The constructor and setOperator (l.314) let the owner or the treasury also be an operator; that operator key can then sweep or reconfigure everything. But separating the roles is condition 4 of the guarantee in the README, `mm ancre payer status` checks it, and the only deployment that merges the roles is the testnet-only T1 facilitator test, which runs against a mock oracle.
details_en.failure_scenario: No wrong output under the documented conditions. With treasury = operator, one sweep(usdc, balance) by the operator key moves the whole balance to that key (re-probed). README condition 4 excludes that configuration and payer status flags it. With separated roles, the operator cannot call sweep, setPolicy, setOperator or transferOwnership (probe).
details_en.evidence: Mechanism true: TGP:187 only checks for zero addresses; setOperator TGP:314-332 does not compare with owner/treasury; TGP:361 `if (msg.sender != owner && msg.sender != treasury) revert NotOwner();`. Probes: Probe.t.sol::test_probe_operatorAsTreasurySweepsAll and V2Probe.t.sol::test_k2_operatorAloneCannotSweepWhenSeparated (both PASS). Listed as a condition: plugin/README.md:62 "The payer's operator is the Agent Wallet, and its owner and treasury are the human (a different wallet)"; checked by plugin/src/lib/flows.ts:324 `{ check: "owner and treasury are the human (neither the payer, an operator nor the Agent Wallet)", ok: isHuman(owner) && isHuman(treasury) }`; override refuses it (override.ts:86 ANCRE_OVERRIDE_MISCONFIGURED); the demo setup separates the roles (setup-fork.mjs:7-8, 103 "operator = Agent Wallet, owner = treasury = human"). T1.s.sol:9-10 "D is the deployer, owner, treasury and operator of the payer (testnet only)", l.25 `require(block.chainid == 10143)`, l.35-37 a T1Oracle mock in place of ANCRE, 0.1 test USDC: it tests the facilitator (PAYER.md §6), not the guarantee. Documentation gap: PAYER.md:168 "A stolen operator key can pay trusted agents only" does not restate the condition (TGP:359 assumes it: "treasury (the human)").

constats.titre: `reportRefusal` : le premier appelant choisit le bloc tracé
constats.resume: ÉCARTÉ : comportement documenté (une trace par autorisation) ; la raison tracée est vraie à son bloc et infalsifiable, et `explain` reconstruit tout refus ultérieur.
constats.scenario: Trace moins informative possible (STALE transitoire au lieu du veto), jamais fausse (MESURÉ).
constats.correctif: Optionnel : indexer `reported` par (hash, raison, statut).

details_en.summary: reportRefusal is permissionless and runs once per authorisation hash, so the first caller chooses the block whose reason gets traced. This is the documented 'once per authorisation' design. The traced reason is true at its block and cannot be forged, and for policy reasons (PAUSED, OVER_LIMIT, wallet) the event still carries ANCRE's status and triggerTag.
details_en.failure_scenario: The trace can be less informative, but it is never wrong. A third party that reports during a transient ANCRE STALE gets status STALE with triggerTag 0; after recertification, the VETOED refusal of the same live authorisation reverts AlreadyReported (probe). A report made while PAUSED still records status VETOED and triggerTag keccak256('slash') (probe). explain() at any block rebuilds the later refusal, the veto itself is an on-chain ERC-8004 feedback, and no shipped code calls reportRefusal.
details_en.evidence: TGP:259-260 `if (reported[hash]) revert AlreadyReported(); reported[hash] = true;`. Documented: PAYER.md:66-68 "traced on-chain with reportRefusal(hash, blob): once per authorisation, only for a genuine operator-signed authorisation that is still settleable"; TGP:250 "Permissionless on-chain trace of a refusal, once per authorisation"; TGP:136. Cannot be forged: it needs a genuine operator signature, r != OK at that block, and a settleable authorisation (TGP:256-258); the earlier gas sweep (test_probe_gasSweepNoFalseRefusal) gave 0 false reports. The Assessment is computed before the policy (TGP:469-470), so PAUSED keeps the veto: V2Probe.t.sol::test_k4_pausedReportStillCarriesVeto (PASS, caller = arbitrary address). Only ANCRE's own early exits (AR:1383 REGISTRY_CHANGED, AR:1387 STALE, NO_CERT), none of which the payee controls, drop the triggerTag: V2Probe.t.sol::test_k4_staleReportHidesVetoThenAlreadyReported (PASS). Rebuild path: PAYER.md:66, 169 explain(). Consumers: grep finds reportRefusal/RefusalReported only in tests.
details_en.fix: Optional: if the trace must capture the most informative refusal, key `reported` by (hash, reason, status), or allow a new report when the reason or status differs.

constats.titre: `_setPolicy` accepte un set en mode rapide (strictTransfer = false)
constats.resume: ÉCARTÉ : c'est le compromis D25/D35 documenté (mode rapide), appliqué fidèlement par le payeur via `isTrusted` ; seul le commentaire l.495-497 exagère. Durcissement optionnel : refuser `strictTransfer = false` dans `_setPolicy`.
constats.scenario: Avec un set non strict choisi par l'owner, l'acheteur d'un agent vendu est payé jusqu'au `proveTransfer` (MESURÉ) ; avec tout set strict (tous ceux du projet), refus immédiat TRANSFERRED.
constats.correctif: Optionnel : refuser les sets non stricts ou documenter la fenêtre dans PAYER.md §7 et l'afficher dans `payer status`.

details_en.summary: _setPolicy accepts a fast-mode set (strictTransfer = false). In such a set a sold agent stays payable to its buyer until someone posts proveTransfer. That is ANCRE's documented D25/D35 fast-mode trade-off, which the payer applies faithfully through isTrusted; it is not a payer defect. Only the comment at l.495-497 overstates.
details_en.failure_scenario: No wrong output beyond the documented trade-off. With a fast-mode setId chosen by the owner, after the transfer and the buyer's setAgentWallet, isValidSignature returns MAGIC to the buyer until proveTransfer (re-probed). With any strict set, which covers every set the project builds, the same scenario returns ANCRE_STATUS/TRANSFERRED immediately.
details_en.evidence: Mechanism true: TGP:370 `if (ancre.policyOf(setId_).theta == 0) revert UnknownSet();` (no strictTransfer check); AR:1419-1421 `bool moved = flags & F_TRANSFERRED != 0; if (!moved && s.strictTransfer && x.trust != 0) {...ownerOf...}`. Probe scratchpad/pc/test/V2Probe.t.sol::test_k1_fastModeWindowEndsAtProof_strictRefuses (PASS): fast-set payer pays the buyer's wallet; strict-set payer refuses (TRANSFERRED); once any address calls proveTransfer, the fast payer refuses. Documented as intended: CR-conseil.md:999 (D25) "Ce qu'on perd. En mode rapide, la fenêtre de transfert dure le temps que le surveillant prouve le transfert."; CR-conseil.md:47 D35 "ownerOf en direct par défaut (strict) ... mode rapide optionnel"; ENCODING.md:48 "strictTransfer D35: live ownerOf in assess (true recommended)"; docs/erc/anchored-reputation.md:902 "fast mode: the agent is TRANSFERRED only after proveTransfer" and :995; AR:1327 isTrusted "Applies the policy committed in the setId (... transfer mode)"; D39: the owner picks the setId. Every set the project builds is strict: solver/certifier.py:95, solver/export.py:172, plugin/scripts/setup-fork.mjs:91, contracts/test/Base.t.sol:78, all solver/vectors. Documentation gaps only: TGP:495-497 "a transferred agent is not payable anyway (TRANSFERRED)" holds only for strict sets or after a proof; statusFlow's policy (flows.ts:291, 341-349) does not show strictTransfer; README conditions do not mention it; no shipped code calls proveTransfer (grep), so in practice the fast window has no end.
details_en.fix: Optional hardening: make _setPolicy revert when !policyOf(setId_).strictTransfer. Otherwise document the fast-mode window in PAYER.md §7, show strictTransfer in `payer status`, and correct the l.495-497 comment.
